"36089523",
      "32666496"

     "pref": "Every presumed adenoma. EASL advises reassessment with contrast-enhanced MRI after 6 months for all presumed adenomas, and in women a period of 6 months observation after lifestyle change (evidence level II-3, grade of recommendation 2). ACG 2024 uses a looser 6- to 12-month interval and does not tie it to a size trigger (conditional recommendation, low quality of evidence). The Italian multisociety guideline specifies MRI at 6 months after contraceptive discontinuation, repeat at 1 year if unchanged or reduced below 5 cm, and annual ultrasound after the first 18 months — and grades every one of those steps very low quality (D), conditional.",
     "avoid": "Do not treat a lesion still over 5 cm at 6 months as a failed trial. In 194 patients with adenomas larger than 5 cm followed with serial imaging, regression to 5 cm or less had occurred in only 8.5-15.3% at 26 weeks — the exact point at which EASL and ACG advise resection — rising to 23.7-27.1% at 52 weeks, with 69 of 118 (58.5%) regressing below 5 cm eventually at a median of 104 weeks (95% CI 80-128). Time to regression was strongly size-dependent: a median of 63 weeks for lesions under 7 cm, 109 weeks for 7-10 cm and 208 weeks for those over 10 cm (P<0.001). No complication occurred anywhere in that follow-up. A decision point at six months therefore identifies roughly one in six to one in ten of the lesions that will eventually fall below the line, which means the timing of the rule — not only the value of the threshold — drives resections that a longer wait would have avoided.",
     "note": "Read against that, the counter-evidence is thin. The single-institution surgical series that reports no significant regression at six months does not define significant regression and did not look beyond six months, in a literature whose median time to regression is about two years — so the observation arm was never given a fair test before the surgical policy was validated against it. The Dutch cohort has its own problems: 47 of 241 patients were excluded for under six months of follow-up, which removes precisely the patients in whom the guideline rule was applied, and regression is defined as crossing the 5 cm line, so a lesion falling from 12 cm to 6 cm counts as a non-responder. EASL's growth trigger is a diameter increase of 20% or more, taken from RECIST 1.1, which was built for response assessment in solid malignancy and has never been validated in a benign liver lesion; on a 5 cm lesion it is 1 cm, small enough that the measurement convention in the radiology report decides whether the trigger fires."
    }

     "pref": "The 8 mm or 15 mm nodule found on a surveillance or incidental study in a cirrhotic liver. Under CT/MRI LI-RADS v2018 the no-arterial-hyperenhancement observations fall into LR-2 or LR-3 depending on size and feature count, and the management LI-RADS specifies is repeat or alternative diagnostic imaging in 3 to 6 months for LR-3, not discharge and not biopsy.",
     "avoid": "Do not describe either category as benign to the patient, and do not treat the numbers as precise. In the pooled systematic review, 13% (95% CI 8-22) of LR-2 and 38% (31-45) of LR-3 observations were confirmed HCC, and 14% (9-21) and 40% (31-50) respectively were confirmed malignant — a 3-to-6-month interval on a 38% probability is a watch, not reassurance. The authors explicitly label the LR-2 estimate provisional and at high risk of bias, and it rests on 223 observations for HCC and 162 for malignancy.",
     "note": "Two cautions on how the category is reached. The feature that most often lifts a nodule out of LR-2 or LR-3 on a follow-up study is threshold growth, and the 2022 individual-patient-data meta-analysis found no association between threshold growth and HCC (OR 1.6, 95% CI 0.8-3.4) — assessable in only 452 of 4,434 observations, and reported a second time in the same paper as 1.6 (0.7-3.6). Enhancing capsule is weak too, OR 2.4 (1.7-3.5), and reached significance in only one of the three analysis cohorts. Downgraded from B to C: every figure here comes from retrospective cohorts with structural verification bias. A cirrhotic liver with a nodule is, by definition, a liver that needs surveillance anyway; the surveillance programme and the nodule's follow-up interval should be one plan with one owner, not two."
    }

"20829538",
      "9885589"

     "pref": "This is the ACR algorithm's most consequential single rule and it follows the risk fork at clinical decision 0, not the lesion. In a low-risk patient, lesions 1 cm or smaller require no workup at all. In a high-risk patient, MRI is advised in 3 to 6 months to characterise the lesion and assess growth, and for a sub-centimetre lesion found on ultrasound in a patient with a known extrahepatic malignancy the ACR Appropriateness Criteria make MRI without and with contrast the only option they rate usually appropriate.",
     "avoid": "Four honest qualifications, and the first is the most important. Every number in this rule is a convention. The small-lesion stratum was 0.5 cm in the 2010 white paper and 1 cm in 2017; the interval was 6 months and became 3 to 6 months; the three risk tiers became two; the focal-nodular-hyperplasia-versus-adenoma threshold moved from 4 cm to 3 cm. Four thresholds changed in seven years with no new evidence cited and the same subcommittee chair on both occasions, and the committee states that its consensus process meets no specific formal national standard and that its content should not be considered standard of care. Second, the test being ordered is not reliable at that size: per-lesion sensitivity for colorectal metastases below 10 mm was 60.2% for MRI and 47.3% for CT. Third, in the 2,978-patient cancer cohort, 8.2% of small lesions were followed for under 6 months, remained stable and were still classed indeterminate — so a 3-month repeat often resolves nothing. Fourth, the white paper permits the radiologist to deviate from the under-1-cm rule even in low-risk patients when a lesion has suspicious features, in which case MRI is suggested.",
     "note": "Growth over a year is concerning; growth over a shorter timeframe is more urgent. That is the white paper's wording and it is a judgement, not a threshold — and growth was deliberately left out of the algorithm altogether because thresholds vary by risk category, then reinserted as narrative advice. Downgraded from C to D: an underived consensus threshold is grade D however firmly it is stated."
    },

     "opts": [

       "name": "Daraxonrasib for eligible metastatic PDAC; the US indication is not restricted to a RAS mutation",
       "g": "A",
       "when": "RASolute 302 (phase 3, n=500 randomised, 248 daraxonrasib and 252 investigator's-choice chemotherapy, more than 90% with RAS G12 mutations) had dual primary endpoints in the RAS G12 population and met both: median overall survival 13.2 versus 6.6 months, hazard ratio 0.40, P<0.001, and median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review 7.3 versus 3.5 months, hazard ratio 0.45.",
       "pref": "The FDA approval of 26 August 2026 covers adults with metastatic PDAC after at least one systemic therapy, or those not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy. The randomized trial studied patients progressing after one prior line; it does not directly establish the same benefit in untreated patients unfit for combinations.",
       "avoid": "Benefit was shown in the RAS G12 and overall randomized populations. In the small non-G12 subgroup (n=41), PFS HR was 1.38 (95% CI 0.60–3.17) while OS HR was 0.37 (0.15–0.93); these exploratory, imprecise estimates do not establish lack of benefit. Interpretation also requires the open-label design, short follow-up and differential treatment non-initiation (38/252 chemotherapy versus 7/248 daraxonrasib). "Triage — a coordinator and a clinical reviewer check completeness, imaging quality and protocol, duplicate cases, urgent referrals, and whether the question is actually a decision question. A non-pancreas-protocol CT is returned for re-imaging rather than discussed, and the degrees of arterial and venous contact are checked against the images by a named reader before the case is listed — in SWOG S1505, 29% of patients called resectable by their own centres did not meet the criteria on central review. Owners: coordinator and chair.",
   "Imaging currency — the staging scan's date is read out with the case. High-quality CT older than 4 weeks is re-acquired before an operative decision is taken, and a case that waits two board cycles is re-imaged. This is the one operating rule specific to this disease. Owner: coordinator.",
   "Agenda — stable at least 24 hours ahead, approximately 10–12 decision cases per session, each carrying one focused question. Owner: coordinator.",
   "Urgent referral route — a same-week slot with chair approval, used routinely here: cholangitis, a rising bilirubin and gastric outlet obstruction are time-critical, and so is a borderline resectable patient whose scan is about to expire. Owner: chair.",
   "Attendance — surgical oncology or hepatopancreatobiliary surgery, medical oncology, radiation oncology, diagnostic radiology, advanced endoscopy, pathology, genetics or a genetic counsellor, nutrition, palliative care and coordination are all required. Owners: specialty leads.",
   "Resectability call — the category is assigned in the meeting, by consensus, and recorded with the degrees of contact, the date and the names of those who agreed it. A single-reader determination is not accepted as the category, and the category is recorded as what it is: a consensus threshold nobody derived, applied to a measurement with no published inter-reader reproducibility. Owner: chair.",
   "Pathology — pre-alerted for every resection specimen, with the agreed inking and slicing protocol and millimetre reporting of every margin within 1.0 cm of tumour; peritoneal washing results are reported to the board, not only to the chart. Owner: pathology.",

files.old: {"19723142": {"kind": "retrospective cohort", "limitations": ["The authors state the overall survival pattern raises the possibility that a LARGER study would show equivocal R1 to be an intermediate prognostic group, and that larger studies are needed to settle this definitively", "They argue sub-categorisation of R1 could be supported only if a clear distinction between the two R1 groups were evident, which these data do not show", "Involvement of the anterior pancreatic surface, excluded from the R1 definition here, could potentially affect survival", "Histological data were incomplete for a small number of cases, so the multivariable model included 155 of 163 patients", "Meaningful comparison of R1 rates between centres is complicated by the lack of standardised margin terminology and of any internationally recognised pathology protocol"], "critique": ["THE CONCLUSION IS DRAWN FROM A NON-SIGNIFICANT TEST, WHICH IS AN ARGUMENT FROM ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE. 'No significant difference' between 57 and 71 patients (P=0.102) in a cohort with 13.9-month median survival cannot establish equivalence; the medians differ by 2.8 months and the point estimates sit between the R0 and unequivocal-R1 groups exactly as an intermediate category would. The authors concede this in the discussion but the abstract concludes the two should be 'considered synonymous'", "THE COMPARISON THE RULE ACTUALLY NEEDS IS EQUIVOCAL R1 VERSUS R0, AND THAT WAS ALSO NON-SIGNIFICANT (P=0.114). The study therefore cannot distinguish equivocal R1 from either neighbour, which is a statement about power, not biology, in a cohort of only 35 R0 patients", "SINGLE CENTRE, SINGLE PATHOLOGIST, RETROSPECTIVE. One consultant pathologist re-reviewed only the R0 cases, so the reclassification effort was applied asymmetrically - cases already called R1 were not re-examined for over-calling, which is the direction of error that would inflate the 79% figure", "ONLY 35 R0 PATIENTS DEFINE THE REFERENCE GROUP, and their median survival of 25.4 months has a 95% CI of 10.5-40.8 months - a four-fold range. Every comparison in the paper is anchored to this unstable estimate", "THE 1997-2007 ERA MEANS ONLY 27% RECEIVED ADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY, at a time when ESPAC-1 and CONKO-001 were establishing it. Margin status interacts with adjuvant therapy, and a cohort in which three quarters got no chemotherapy cannot speak to the prognostic weight of R1 in a modern pathway", "MARGIN STATUS DID NOT SURVIVE MULTIVARIABLE ADJUSTMENT, which undercuts the premise that getting the R1 definition right matters prognostically. The paper treats this as a technical problem (collinearity with tumour size) rather than as evidence that margin status may be a marker of tumour burden rather than an independent determinant of outcome", "THE DECISION TO EXCLUDE THE ANTERIOR SURFACE, PanIN-3, PERINEURAL AND NODAL INVOLVEMENT FROM THE R1 DEFINITION IS A SERIES OF CONVENTIONS, NOT FINDINGS. Different centres make different choices, and the paper's own argument - that the 79% rate reflects pathology protocol rather than surgical quality - applies equally to its own conventions", "THE MOST IMPORTANT IMPLICATION FOR A PATHWAY IS NOT THE ONE THE PAPER EMPHASISES. If the <1 mm rule moves the R1 rate from 44% to 79% at one centre, then R0 and R1 rates reported in every neoadjuvant and adjuvant trial are a function of local pathology practice. PREOPANC (R0 71% of resected under RCPath <1 mm), ESPAC-5 (R0 14-23%), NORPACT-1 (R0 56% vs 39%) and APACT (no central pathology review, R0 76%) are not comparable to each other, and no trial in this depot reports a pathology quality-assurance measure comparable to the one described here except ESPAC5 and CONKO-007", "The argument that R1 is under-reported because 60-80% of resected patients recur locally is an indirect inference: local recurrence can arise from biologically aggressive residual disease beyond any resectable margin, not only from microscopic margin positivity", "Funded by Cancer Research UK with no declared conflicts, and the senior authors are the ESPAC trialists who went on to apply this definition in ESPAC-4 and ESPAC-5 - a coherent programme, but the definition and the trials that use it come from the same group"], "n": "163 pancreatoduodenectomy specimens; 128 R1 (79%), of which 57 (45% of R1) equivocal and 71 unequivocal; 35 R0", "bottom_line": "This single-centre study of 163 pancreatoduodenectomies supplied the only clinical evidence for the <1 mm R1 rule by showing that 'equivocal' R1 survival (15.4 months) resembles unequivocal R1 (12.6 months) more than R0 (25.4 months), and that the rule raises the R1 rate from 44% to 79% - but the key comparison was non-significant in a small cohort, margin status did not survive multivariable adjustment, and the real lesson is that R0 rates reported across pancreatic trials are largely a function of pathology protocol.", "funding": "Supported by Cancer Research UK. No conflicts of interest are declared."}, "20071702": {"kind": "RCT", "limitations": ["The authors note the optimal duration of biliary drainage before surgery has not been established, with experimental and clinical data suggesting at least 4-6 weeks is needed", "Earlier randomised studies used percutaneous rather than endoscopic drainage, which the authors invoke to explain why their hospital stay result differs from previous trials", "Older trials mixed proximal and distal bile-duct obstruction, now regarded as different diseases needing different treatment", "The authors explicitly flag that with the advent of neoadjuvant chemotherapy the question becomes clinically relevant again, and that given their poor results with PLASTIC stents, drainage during neoadjuvant treatment might be better achieved with METAL stents, which have higher patency and do not affect surgical outcome"], "critique": ["COMPARATOR: surgery within one week of diagnosis, which required dedicated operating-room capacity guaranteed by all 13 hospitals specifically for the trial. This is the key external-validity problem: the control strategy is only available where a jaundiced patient can be operated on within seven days. A pathway that cannot deliver that has not got the comparator the trial tested, and delay without drainage is not what was studied", "PLASTIC STENTS ONLY - AND THE AUTHORS SAY THIS IS THE PROBLEM. The 26% cholangitis and 30% stent-exchange rates are largely properties of plastic endoprostheses over 4-6 weeks. Self-expanding metal stents, which every neoadjuvant protocol in this depot (PREOPANC, PREOPANC-2, NORPACT-1, ESPAC5) specifies or prefers, were not tested. Citing this trial against biliary drainage before neoadjuvant chemotherapy is citing it outside its evidence", "NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY WAS AN EXCLUSION CRITERION, so the trial has nothing to say about the situation in which drainage is now most often needed - bridging a jaundiced patient through months of chemotherapy. NORPACT-1 stented 57% of its neoadjuvant arm and had 2 patients derailed by persistent jaundice; PREOPANC had 10 patients whose treatment was delayed by it. files.new: {"19723142":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["The authors state the overall survival pattern raises the possibility that a LARGER study would show equivocal R1 to be an intermediate prognostic group, and that larger studies are needed to settle this definitively","They argue sub-categorisation of R1 could be supported only if a clear distinction between the two R1 groups were evident, which these data do not show","Involvement of the anterior pancreatic surface, excluded from the R1 definition here, could potentially affect survival","Histological data were incomplete for a small number of cases, so the multivariable model included 155 of 163 patients","Meaningful comparison of R1 rates between centres is complicated by the lack of standardised margin terminology and of any internationally recognised pathology protocol"],"critique":["THE CONCLUSION IS DRAWN FROM A NON-SIGNIFICANT TEST, WHICH IS AN ARGUMENT FROM ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE. 'No significant difference' between 57 and 71 patients (P=0.102) in a cohort with 13.9-month median survival cannot establish equivalence; the medians differ by 2.8 months and the point estimates sit between the R0 and unequivocal-R1 groups exactly as an intermediate category would. The authors concede this in the discussion but the abstract concludes the two should be 'considered synonymous'","THE COMPARISON THE RULE ACTUALLY NEEDS IS EQUIVOCAL R1 VERSUS R0, AND THAT WAS ALSO NON-SIGNIFICANT (P=0.114). One consultant pathologist re-reviewed only the R0 cases, so the reclassification effort was applied asymmetrically - cases already called R1 were not re-examined for over-calling, which is the direction of error that would inflate the 79% figure","ONLY 35 R0 PATIENTS DEFINE THE REFERENCE GROUP, and their median survival of 25.4 months has a 95% CI of 10.5-40.8 months - a four-fold range. Every comparison in the paper is anchored to this unstable estimate","THE 1997-2007 ERA MEANS ONLY 27% RECEIVED ADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY, at a time when ESPAC-1 and CONKO-001 were establishing it. The paper treats this as a technical problem (collinearity with tumour size) rather than as evidence that margin status may be a marker of tumour burden rather than an independent determinant of outcome","THE DECISION TO EXCLUDE THE ANTERIOR SURFACE, PanIN-3, PERINEURAL AND NODAL INVOLVEMENT FROM THE R1 DEFINITION IS A SERIES OF CONVENTIONS, NOT FINDINGS. PREOPANC (R0 71% of resected under RCPath <1 mm), ESPAC-5 (R0 14-23%), NORPACT-1 (R0 56% vs 39%) and APACT (no central pathology review, R0 76%) are not comparable to each other, and no trial in this depot reports a pathology quality-assurance measure comparable to the one described here except ESPAC5 and CONKO-007","The argument that R1 is under-reported because 60-80% of resected patients recur locally is an indirect inference: local recurrence can arise from biologically aggressive residual disease beyond any resectable margin, not only from microscopic margin positivity","Funded by Cancer Research UK with no declared conflicts, and the senior authors are the ESPAC trialists who went on to apply this definition in ESPAC-4 and ESPAC-5 - a coherent programme, but the definition and the trials that use it come from the same group"],"n":"163 pancreatoduodenectomy specimens; 128 R1 (79%), of which 57 (45% of R1) equivocal and 71 unequivocal; 35 R0","bottom_line":"This single-centre study of 163 pancreatoduodenectomies supplied the only clinical evidence for the <1 mm R1 rule by showing that 'equivocal' R1 survival (15.4 months) resembles unequivocal R1 (12.6 months) more than R0 (25.4 months), and that the rule raises the R1 rate from 44% to 79% - but the key comparison was non-significant in a small cohort, margin status did not survive multivariable adjustment, and the real lesson is that R0 rates reported across pancreatic trials are largely a function of pathology protocol.","funding":"Supported by Cancer Research UK. No conflicts of interest are declared."},"20071702":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The authors note the optimal duration of biliary drainage before surgery has not been established, with experimental and clinical data suggesting at least 4-6 weeks is needed","Earlier randomised studies used percutaneous rather than endoscopic drainage, which the authors invoke to explain why their hospital stay result differs from previous trials","Older trials mixed proximal and distal bile-duct obstruction, now regarded as different diseases needing different treatment","The authors explicitly flag that with the advent of neoadjuvant chemotherapy the question becomes clinically relevant again, and that given their poor results with PLASTIC stents, drainage during neoadjuvant treatment might be better achieved with METAL stents, which have higher patency and do not affect surgical outcome"],"critique":["COMPARATOR: surgery within one week of diagnosis, which required dedicated operating-room capacity guaranteed by all 13 hospitals specifically for the trial. Self-expanding metal stents, which every neoadjuvant protocol in this depot (PREOPANC, PREOPANC-2, NORPACT-1, ESPAC5) specifies or prefers, were not tested. "note": "Biochemical cure for apparently sporadic gastrinoma is 60% immediately after resection and 30-40% at 5 years, with 15-year disease-free survival of 15%, so \"cured\" means something different in each syndrome and should be said in those terms. For gastrinoma the strongest datum for operating is not randomised: on prospective NIH, UCSF and Stanford protocols, 160 patients who had a standardised exploration were compared with 35 who met the same criteria but did not have surgery. A gastrinoma was found and removed in 150 of 160 (94%), 51% were disease-free immediately and 41% at last follow-up. Liver metastases developed in 8 of 160 (5%) against 10 of 35 (29%), p=0.0002; death from any cause in 34 of 160 (21%) against 19 of 35 (54%), p=0.0002; disease-related death in 2 of 160 (1%) against 8 of 35 (23%), p=0.00001; and 15-year disease-related survival from first admission was 98% against 74%. Those 35 controls were not randomly formed - 19 refused after consulting their own physician, 10 had MEN1 with no lesion above 2.5 cm and 5 had comorbidity - non-disease mortality was numerically higher in them (31% against 20%, p=0.18), the surgical arm's disease-related figure rests on 2 deaths, cause of death was adjudicated unblinded by the operating investigators, and the controls were imaged every 6 to 12 months against yearly evaluation in the operated patients. "pref": "Two thresholds are in circulation and the board should pick one and write it down. PANDORA used growth of more than 0.5 cm per year as its protocol trigger, and 8 of 76 patients (11%) met it at a median of 17 months. The 2025 MEN1 recommendations use growth of under 1 mm per year as the point at which the imaging interval may be lengthened to every 1 to 2 years, at 92% panel agreement, with intervals individualised to the observed growth rate and the absolute size. In ASPEN, increasing size was the stated indication for surgery in only 4 of the 406 surveillance patients, against patient preference in 42 of 94 operated patients and centre preference in 37.",
     "avoid": "Do not present either number as biological - neither has any cited derivation. One millimetre a year lies below the measurement reproducibility of serial cross-sectional imaging of a small pancreatic lesion across different scanners and readers, and will generate both false stability and false progression. Half a centimetre a year is no better founded: in PANDORA the 8 patients who met it had a mean size at last follow-up of still only 1.2 cm (SD 0.7), and only 2 of them ever crossed 2.0 cm, so the threshold was detecting measurement variation as much as growth. What makes either threshold usable at all is the same modality, the same contrast agent and the same measurement convention every time, which is the one part of this that is entirely within the programme's control.",
     "note": "Record the measurement in the body of the note, in millimetres, naming the phase and sequence it was made on. A growth rate that cannot be recomputed from the chart is not a growth rate. See approval 12."

       "when": "Not required by any of the four guidelines, but the best-evidenced addition since Fukuoka 2017.        "pref": "Where the cyst type is genuinely unresolved, or where a result indicating advanced neoplasia would move a borderline patient to theatre. In a prospective study of specimens from 31 institutions, 1,887 of 1,933 (98%) were adequate: MAPK-pathway or GNAS mutations gave 90% sensitivity and 100% specificity for a mucinous cyst (PPV 100%, NPV 77%), against 77% and 92% for increased fluid viscosity and 73% and 94% for CEA above 192 ng/mL. Adding TP53, SMAD4 or mTOR-pathway alterations at allele frequencies equal to the driver gave 87% sensitivity and 99% specificity for advanced neoplasia (PPV 98%, NPV 92%), rising to 89% and 98% with CTNNB1 (PPV 97%, NPV 93%) and to 93% sensitivity at 95% specificity with cytology added. VHL alterations identified serous cystadenomas (71% sensitivity, 100% specificity) and MEN1 with loss of heterozygosity of TP53, SMAD4, PTEN or RNF43 identified cystic neuroendocrine tumours (68%, 98%; MEN1 alone, 27% and 100%).",
       "avoid": "Read the limits honestly, and do not apply the headline figure to the cyst in front of you without checking which lesion it came from. KRAS, BRAF or GNAS alterations were found in 159 of 167 IPMNs (95%) but KRAS in only 9 of 19 mucinous cystic neoplasms (47%), so for a non-communicating body or tail cyst in a middle-aged woman the sensitivity is 47%, not 90%. Surgical pathology existed for only 251 of 1,832 tested patients (14%), or 251 of the 1,216 with follow-up (21%), so the performance figures rest on the operated minority, and the decision to operate was itself informed by the molecular result — which depresses the measured sensitivity of the comparator criteria and inflates that of the panel. The allele-frequency rules that lift specificity to 98 to 100% were derived in the same group's earlier single-centre cohorts and the confirmation cohort came from the same molecular archive, and every specimen was processed in the one lead laboratory, so 'multi-institutional' describes where the fluid came from and not where it was analysed. The panel is that laboratory's assay rather than a class of test, charged at $750 per specimen in the 2018 series, so another laboratory's panel does not inherit these numbers. Kyoto 2024's own pooled figures for the grade markers are much weaker — TP53, SMAD4, CDKN2A and PIK3CA alterations at 9 to 39% sensitivity and 92 to 98% specificity — so a negative molecular result is not a reason to stand down. Nine resected IPMNs were driver-negative preoperatively and positive on the specimen, which makes the 90% sensitivity partly a property of the aspiration rather than of the sequencing. files.old: {"15131794":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["The analysed patients were a subset who underwent resection for symptoms, concern about malignancy or lack of a definitive diagnosis, so their characteristics may differ from an unselected population and the results may not apply to all patients with a pancreatic cyst","The CEA results, and particularly the cutoff values, may not be applicable if CEA assays with different characteristics are used"],"critique":["The 192 ng/mL threshold was selected to maximise correct classification in the same 112 patients in which it was then tested, with no split-sample, cross-validation or external cohort, so 79% accuracy is an optimistic in-sample estimate and the figure that entered every subsequent guideline was never validated here","Only 112 of 341 enrolled patients (33%) had histological verification, and verification depended on the very findings under test - a worrying EUS appearance or suspicious cytology made resection more likely - which is partial verification bias and distorts the apparent performance of all three tests in directions that cannot be signed from the data given","Mucinous lesions were 60% of the verified cohort and 59% of those were malignant or borderline, far above community prevalence, so the predictive values implied by these sensitivities and specificities do not transport to an incidental cyst clinic","Cytology was read by local cytologists at each of 13 institutions with no central review, while CEA was assayed centrally and blindly; the comparison therefore pits a standardised test against an unstandardised one, which penalises cytology by design","Cyst fluid was explicitly not analysed for amylase, mucin concentration or viscosity, so the comparison omits the cheapest and most widely used discriminators, including the one test that reliably excludes a pseudocyst","Only 7 serous cystadenomas were verified, so the low-CEA half of the claim rests on single digits, and the inflammatory group (n=27) carries a mean CEA of 36.8 ng/mL, which means the test's specificity for mucinous disease is being established largely against pseudocysts rather than against serous lesions","The study's conclusion - that endoscopists should send aspirated fluid for CEA - rests on a marker the data show cannot distinguish benign from malignant mucinous disease, since CEA ranges overlapped widely within the malignant group; the clinical decision that matters is left unaddressed","Histological interpretation was done locally and only reviewed from reports by one study pathologist, not from slides, so the reference standard itself was not uniformly applied"],"n":"341 consecutive patients enrolled and underwent EUS-FNA; 112 with histological confirmation analysed (68 mucinous, 7 serous, 27 inflammatory, 5 endocrine, 5 other)","bottom_line":"The study that established cyst fluid CEA at 192 ng/mL as the most accurate single test for separating mucinous from non-mucinous pancreatic cysts, at about 80% accuracy and better than EUS morphology or cytology either alone or combined; it does not establish that CEA identifies which mucinous cysts harbour high-grade dysplasia or cancer, and its threshold was derived and tested in the same 112-patient surgical subset."},"16111956":{"kind":"systematic review","limitations":["Wide variation in cytology sensitivity between studies, probably reflecting differences in cytopathologist experience, so sensitivity and specificity may be lower in non-specialised centres where aspirates are rarely seen","Rare cystic neoplasms including IPMT, pseudopapillary and solid tumours, cystic islet-cell tumours, lymphangioma, sarcoma and benign cysts - together 10-25% of all pancreatic cystic tumours - were excluded, so the data cannot be applied to them","Too few studies existed to pool other markers or viscosity, and there may be no added benefit from them over amylase, CEA and cytology","No multiple-regression analysis was performed to validate the suggestion that CEA, amylase, cytology and CA19-9 each have independent value in different subsets"],"critique":["The cutoffs were chosen to maximise correct classification within the same pooled dataset in which they are then reported, and the CEA >800 ng/mL threshold is described as 'arbitrarily set'; there is no validation sample, so all the operating characteristics are in-sample","The 450-patient figure is not a cohort: each marker has a different and much smaller denominator (amylase 155, CA19-9 136), the contributing studies did not all measure all markers, and so the apparent mutual consistency of the markers is partly determined by which studies happened to report which assay","The reference standard is not uniform or symmetric: nearly all MCA and MCAC were confirmed histologically or cytologically, whereas in two studies pseudocysts were diagnosed from a pancreatitis history plus follow-up and many SCAs were unverified - differential verification of the malignant arm inflates specificity for mucinous disease","The Frossard data were excluded post hoc because SCA CEA values were discordantly high, with no pre-specified rule and no explanation found; the authors report both versions, which is honest, but the headline numbers are the ones that survive the exclusion","Individual values were read off published scatter grams rather than obtained from authors, so extraction error is unquantified and unquantifiable","The analysis predates and explicitly excludes IPMN, which is now the commonest neoplastic pancreatic cyst; the management table the paper proposes - resect on CEA >800 or malignant cytology, do not resect on CEA <5 or CA19-9 <37 - therefore cannot be applied to the modal patient in current practice, and the omission is noted only as a caveat about rare tumours","Every cutoff has a sensitivity at or below 50%, so all four tests are rule-in only; the paper nonetheless advises 'no resection needed' on the strength of CEA <5 ng/mL and CA19-9 <37 U/mL, whose negative predictive values are 55% and 38% in its own tables","CA19-9 is recommended as an adjunct for indeterminate CEA on the basis of 136 patients and an accuracy of 46%, which is barely better than chance in a cohort with roughly even group sizes"],"n":"12 studies, 450 patients; amylase available in 155 (60 pseudocyst, 32 SCA, 32 MCA, 31 MCAC), CEA in 332 (125/79/64/64), CA19-9 in 136 (66/24/24/22), cytology for malignancy in 111","bottom_line":"Pooled individual-patient data fix the specificity of amylase <250 U/L, CEA <5 ng/mL, CEA >800 ng/mL and CA19-9 <37 U/mL at 95-98% with sensitivities of 19-50%, making each a rule-in rather than a screening test, and put cytology's sensitivity for malignancy at 48%; it establishes nothing about IPMN, which was excluded, and all its cutoffs were fitted to the data that report them."},"16327281":{"kind":"consensus","limitations":["The guidelines are explicitly provisional - the authors state they represent the working group's consensus 'at this moment' and that as understanding grows they will need revision","Considerable gaps are acknowledged in knowledge of the natural history of these neoplasms, with 'practically no information' on the natural history of branch-duct IPMN","Data on the prevalence of invasive carcinoma in MCN are hard to interpret because few studies used ovarian-type stroma as a necessary criterion","More data from pathological studies of branch-duct IPMN over 30 mm without main duct dilation or mural nodules are needed to determine whether all such lesions should be resected immediately","The interval between follow-up examinations 'remains to be determined', and there is no evidence in the literature to define the frequency or type of surveillance required after resection","Frozen-section grading of IPMN is subjective and frozen tissue artefacts compound the difficulty; denuded epithelium frequently makes margin assessment impossible","It is impossible to diagnose minimally invasive carcinoma derived from IPMN or MCN preoperatively","The relative risk and biologic significance of the various grades and subsets of IPMN have not been fully established"],"critique":["There is no cohort - n is null - and every malignancy rate quoted, from 70% for main-duct IPMN to 25% for branch-duct and 6-36% for MCN, is the prevalence of malignancy in resected specimens, that is in cysts selected for operation; the document applies these figures to management decisions about unresected lesions without any correction for that selection, and the arithmetic of what fraction of all such cysts they represent is never attempted","The series behind the tables are small and heterogeneous (12-140 patients, with 8 of 9 main-duct series under 50), and the 'mean of all series' is an unweighted average across studies with different definitions of malignancy, different eras and different inclusion of asymptomatic patients; the authors themselves observe that the two branch-duct series with 30-31% invasive cancer contained no asymptomatic patients, which explains the entire spread and undercuts pooling a mean at all","No evidence grading, no systematic search and no account of how consensus was reached or whether it was unanimous; the thresholds that became the Sendai criteria - 30 mm, mural nodules, main duct >6 mm, symptoms - derive from univariate and multivariate analyses in two Japanese series of 15-32 patients","The recommendation to resect all main-duct and mixed IPMN was made with no data at all on what happens to unresected main-duct IPMN, and is justified in part by inference - that 'clonal progression' and the age difference between benign and malignant cases indicate most benign main-duct lesions will progress - rather than by observation","The recommendation to resect all MCNs rests on malignancy rates from series that largely did not require ovarian stroma, which the text concedes inflates them, and on the assertion that left pancreatectomy carries 'low morbidity and practically no mortality' with no pooled estimate; the risk side of every resection recommendation in the document is unquantified","The 30 mm and 6 mm thresholds that trigger resection on follow-up are the same numbers used to define a low-risk lesion at baseline, with no evidence that a lesion crossing them during observation carries the same risk as one presenting with them","No end point to surveillance is offered, no cost consideration enters, and no competing-risk framing is applied despite an explicitly elderly branch-duct population in the sixth and seventh decades","The working group that wrote the criteria largely comprises the authors of the series on which the criteria are based, and the document records no external review or validation plan"],"bottom_line":"The first international consensus on IPMN and MCN, which fixed the vocabulary - main-duct versus branch-duct, ovarian-type stroma as a requirement for MCN - and introduced the resection thresholds later known as the Sendai criteria; it establishes none of them empirically, since the guideline has no cohort, all its malignancy rates are prevalences in small resected series, and no data on the natural history of unresected lesions existed when it was written."},"22687371":{"kind":"consensus","limitations":["The levels of evidence for all items addressed are low, being 4 or 5, so the authors designate these 'consensus' rather than 'evidence-based' guidelines; grades of recommendation are so low that grade C has been omitted from almost all items as repetitive","The vast majority of the data are retrospective and uncontrolled with limited long-term follow-up, so knowledge of the natural history is still incomplete","Differences in the proportions of each IPMN type and in malignancy risk are partly caused by variation in type definitions, since the correlation between histologic and radiologic criteria is only around 70%","Whether the surveillance interval can be lengthened after 2 years of no change is controversial, with some authors advocating continued 6-monthly surveillance because of the relatively high incidence of PDAC in branch-duct IPMN","Cyst fluid analysis is still investigational, and interpreting biochemical markers is a complex exercise in pattern recognition that should be reserved for patients in whom the information will affect surgical decision-making","It is unclear whether a microscopically positive margin for moderately dysplastic IPMN increases recurrence, and there is little evidence to guide the frequency or type of postoperative surveillance","Recurrence rates after resection are difficult to determine because main duct dilation in the remnant may be secondary to anastomotic stenosis, and better postoperative imaging may reveal previously undetected IPMN","The relationship between a rapid growth rate and malignancy risk remains unclear"],"critique":["n is null - the guideline has no cohort - and the pooled malignancy figures that justify the new risk framework come from 3568 resected IPMNs, so they describe the yield of past operating decisions rather than the risk faced by a surveilled patient; the table itself carries '>' signs because some contributing series reported only invasive cases, meaning numerators and denominators are not consistently defined across the pool","The central change, lowering the main-duct threshold from 10 mm to more than 5 mm, cites references for improved sensitivity but no study comparing outcomes above and below the new line; the same document then classifies 5-9 mm as a worrisome feature not warranting resection, so a duct can define main-duct disease and simultaneously be observed, and the resulting expansion of the 'mixed type' category is noted as a classification problem but its consequences for management are not addressed","The 2-3% annual malignancy rate in observed branch-duct IPMN and the 25.5% resected malignancy rate are placed on facing pages without reconciling that they are incompatible estimates of the same underlying quantity","High-risk stigmata and worrisome features were assembled from univariate associations in surgical series; no multivariable model, no validation cohort and no operating characteristics - sensitivity, specificity, predictive values - are reported for either tier, so a clinician cannot know what a 'worrisome feature' actually predicts","The recommendation to resect every MCN in a fit patient appears two sentences after the statement that ovarian-stroma-defined MCN has under 15% invasive carcinoma and no malignancy below 4 cm without mural nodules; the guidance is more aggressive than the evidence it cites, and the justification shifts to the cost of years of high-resolution imaging rather than to risk","Surgical mortality and morbidity are nowhere quantified in the document, so every resection recommendation is presented one-sidedly, with the risk of the alternative stated numerically and the risk of the intervention not stated at all","The Japanese objection to EUS-FNA of any cyst with worrisome features is recorded as a regional belief supported by two case-level citations, which leaves the single most informative preoperative test governed by geography rather than data and makes the cytology-based criteria unobtainable in much of the world","No stopping rule is offered, no cost analysis is attempted and no competing-risk framing is applied to a disease of the sixth and seventh decades, even though the document's own argument for observing branch-duct IPMN rests on patients being elderly","Fourteen authors, most of whom authored the series pooled in the evidence table, and no declaration of how disagreements were resolved, whether consensus was unanimous, or what conflicts of interest existed"],"bottom_line":"The Fukuoka revision that created the high-risk-stigmata and worrisome-features framework still in use, lowered the main-duct threshold to more than 5 mm, replaced carcinoma in situ with high-grade dysplasia, substaged T1, and moved branch-duct IPMN over 3 cm from resection to observation; by the authors' own account every recommendation rests on level 4-5 evidence, the two risk tiers have no reported operating characteristics, and the malignancy rates behind them are prevalences in resected specimens."},"25793719":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["The study explicitly does not reach the level of evidence needed to make recommendations on the type and timing of follow-up","Features of recurrent IPMN in terms of invasion were defined through radiology and cytology for patients who were not reoperated","12 of 412 resections could not be pathologically reclassified and 8 patients were lost to follow-up","The authors cannot rule out that the small branch-duct lesions left in the remnant harboured high-grade dysplasia"],"critique":["'Recurrence' is defined as the radiologic appearance of a new IPMN, with growth of knowingly retained
