estimates","Specificity for advanced neoplasia is computed against all other resected cysts, a group enriched for low-grade IPMN and non-neoplastic lesions by the same referral and resection pathway; the quantity a clinician needs - the proportion of molecularly positive cysts under surveillance that will progress - is not estimated anywhere","The senior authors hold a financial interest in the field being validated (an honorarium from Foundation Medicine, and a royalty interest in the GNAS invention through Thrive Earlier Detection), and the paper is in substance a validation of an assay run by the authors' own laboratory and named by them","Nine resected IPMNs were MAPK/GNAS-negative preoperatively and positive on the specimen, which is a false-negative rate the paper attributes to sampling rather than to the test; if sampling is the limiting factor, the 90% sensitivity is a property of the EUS-FNA as much as of the panel, and that cannot be improved by sequencing"],"n":"1933 cyst fluid specimens prospectively tested from 1889 patients at 31 institutions, of which 1887 (98%) from 1832 patients were satisfactory; clinicopathologic follow-up in 1216 patients (66%, 2-35 months, median 21-23); surgical pathology in 251 (21%), of which 246 were pancreatic cysts; plus a retrospective confirmation cohort of 97 (63 mucinous, 34 non-mucinous, 22 with advanced neoplasia) and 87 PanNETs (34 cystic, 53 solid biopsies)","bottom_line":"The largest prospective, real-time, multi-institutional test of cyst fluid NGS, establishing 90% sensitivity and 100% specificity for mucinous cysts, 89%/98% for advanced neoplasia, 93%/95% when combined with cytology, and showing both the AGA and IAP/Fukuoka criteria to be substantially less accurate; it does not establish that acting on the results changes outcomes, and the allele-frequency thresholds were tuned in the same group's earlier cohorts and processed by the same laboratory.","funding":"Supported in part by the National Cancer Institute (1R37CA263622 and 3U01CA200466), the Department of Defense (W81XWH-20-PCARP-TRPA), the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network, the National Pancreas Foundation Western PA Chapter, the Sky Foundation and the Pittsburgh Liver Research Center; AD Singhi has received an honorarium from Foundation Medicine, and RH Hruban has the potential to receive royalty payments from Thrive Earlier Detection for the GNAS invention"},"37406887":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Inevitable biases associated with the observational and retrospective nature of the study","Despite the prospective nature of the institutional databases, retrospective assessment of data collected over 30 years carries variability in feature definitions and in patient management, only partly offset by large numbers and long follow-up","The relatively limited follow-up of surveilled patients","The study was limited to high-volume centres and the extent to which the data are generalisable cannot be determined; there is logic in referring patients followed at low-volume centres to centres of expertise before suggesting discontinuation","Mural nodule size was not available, forcing use of the 2012 rather than 2017 IAP definitions","Patients' data were extracted from each centre's institutional database and in most cases had already been included in prior publications","Accurate diagnosis is particularly difficult in small cysts, so the utmost caution must be exercised before stopping follow-up in the <=15 mm group"],"critique":["The reassuring standardised incidence ratios rest on almost no events: 2 cancers in the Trivial <=15 mm group and 3 in the >=75-year group, giving intervals of 0.10-3.36 and 0.23-3.39 that remain compatible with a threefold excess risk; 'comparable to the general population' is a failure to exclude harm, not a demonstration of safety, and the paper's recommendations are phrased as though it were the latter","The SIR falls with age not because older patients are safer but because the population comparator's pancreatic cancer incidence rises steeply with age - a mechanism the paper states explicitly and then uses to justify stopping surveillance in exactly the group whose absolute risk is highest","The question is what happens after 5 years, but the cohort's median surveillance is 53 months and even the Trivial subgroup's median is 85 months - roughly 2.5 years of observation past the 5-year mark, against the 10-15-year horizons over which Pergolini and Oyama located their events; the paper's own limitation about 'relatively limited follow-up' is doing more work than its placement suggests","164 patients were resected and 843 developed WF or HRS and thereby left the low-risk state, so the denominator for 'no excess risk' is continuously purged of progressors while the person-time they contributed before progressing stays in; this is the same structural issue as in the papers the study argues against, applied in the opposite direction","Malignancy ascertainment was not systematic: 14 of 40 cancers were diagnosed radiologically or by FNA rather than pathologically, and patients lost to follow-up across 12 centres in 8 countries are nowhere accounted for; unascertained cancers bias the SIR numerator downward, which is the direction that favours the conclusion","The authors contrast their result with Oyama's SIR of 6.7 in cysts under 15 mm and attribute the difference to their added 5-year stability criterion, but the two cohorts differ in country, baseline worrisome-feature status, pathology practice, EUS-FNA use and ascertainment method, so the comparison does not isolate stability as the explanation","Of the patients in this 'low-risk' cohort who were eventually resected, 31.8% overall and 38.1% of those resected after 5 years had high-grade dysplasia or invasive cancer; that is the yield of the resections the surveillance programme triggered, and it indicates that when these cysts do declare themselves they are frequently already advanced - a finding that sits uneasily beside the recommendation to stop looking","Three of the senior authors are among the authors of the Kyoto guidelines that adopted the stopping option this paper supports, and the lead centre's prior publications supplied much of the cohort, so the evidence and the guideline it informs are not independent"],"n":"3844 patients with presumed BD-IPMN included from 4356 screened (median age 66, IQR 15; 60.2% female; median initial diameter 12 mm, IQR 9; median surveillance 53 months, IQR 53); 1617 (42%) developed no WF or HRS in the first 5 years ('Trivial BD-IPMN'), of whom 762 (47.1%) had a cyst <=15 mm at 5 years; 164 (4.3%) resected","bottom_line":"In the largest multicentre surveillance cohort of presumed branch-duct IPMN without worrisome features, cysts stable for 5 years carried a pancreatic cancer incidence no higher than the age-matched population in patients over 75 with cysts under 30 mm, or over 65 with cysts <=15 mm, supporting selective discontinuation; with only 2-3 cancers in those subgroups, incomplete ascertainment and a median of roughly 2.5 years of observation past the 5-year mark, it cannot exclude a clinically meaningful late risk.","funding":"The Department of General and Pancreatic Surgery at the University of Verona received funding from the Italian Ministry of Health (Grant FIMP-CUP J38D19000690001)"},"37473969":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["The method provides no training in the technical aspects of performing a high-quality EUS-nCLE examination","The teaching module and targeted feedback came from a single nCLE expert, which may limit reproducibility, although prerecorded feedback has been shown non-inferior to real-time feedback","Training and competency assessment used edited high-yield videos acquired by experts, removing technique variability, which may have produced higher accuracy than would be expected in clinical practice; results may not generalise to real-time procedures by novice operators","Observer selection bias from including only US early-career endosonographers recruited by email and social media","Patient selection bias is inherent in using videos of common cysts with validated nCLE patterns and confirmed histopathology","Unmeasured confounders such as prior exposure to or knowledge of nCLE and variable motivation to learn may partly explain the inefficacy of the refresher intervention","Learning curves were not formally assessed for each cyst subtype","Training in differentiating the degree of dysplasia within IPMNs was not evaluated","Interruptions and lack of nCLE exposure longer than 8 weeks might cause decrements in competency, which was not tested"],"critique":["The refresher arm performed worse than self-learning on accuracy, specificity, confidence and every interobserver agreement statistic; extra expert teaching making readers reliably worse is not a plausible effect, so this is better read as a randomisation failure in 21 people (11 vs 10) than as evidence that refreshers are ineffective - the paper reports it as the latter","Phase 2 uses the same 80 videos, with the same correct answers, that were taught with case-by-case expert feedback in phase 1; reshuffling the order does not remove recognition of individual clips, so the demonstrated 'durability' is confounded with memory of the test set, and the improvement from 85% to 89% is as consistent with learning the answers as with learning the patterns","The senior author designed the teaching module, chose and edited the high-yield clips, delivered all the feedback, co-selected the participants and is a speaker for the device manufacturer; there is no independent reference reader or blinded adjudication anywhere in the design","Prevalence in the video set is engineered at 66% mucinous, so the reported accuracy figures are not transportable to a clinic where most cysts are benign, and no PPV or NPV is given at any realistic prevalence","The per-subtype sensitivities that matter clinically are 57% for MCN and 65% for SCA, meaning a trained reader misses nearly half of MCNs and a third of serous cystadenomas; since the economic case for nCLE is avoiding resection of benign cysts, a 65% sensitivity for SCA undercuts the rationale, and the paper presents the high specificities instead","'Competency' is defined against an arbitrary 10% acceptable and 30% unacceptable error band chosen from meta-analytic accuracies rather than from any outcome, and 5 of 21 readers never reached it yet remain in the pooled phase 2 accuracy of 89%","Several subtype estimates rest on single digits - 3 pseudocysts and 11 SCAs across the whole library - and pseudocyst sensitivity could not even be computed in two of four video blocks for want of true positives","Interobserver agreement for MCN was fair at best (kappa 0.32) and for SCA and NET/SPN only 0.44, which means that the subtype diagnoses the technique is promoted for are not reproducible between trained readers; the conclusion emphasises accuracy and not reproducibility"],"n":"21 early-career nCLE-naive endosonographers (10 advanced endoscopy fellows, 11 practising advanced endoscopists; 86% academic), each assessing 80 nCLE videos twice; videos from 80 patients with confirmed histopathology - 53 mucinous (37 IPMN, 16 MCN) and 27 non-mucinous (11 SCA, 3 pseudocyst, 13 cystic NET/SPN)","bottom_line":"Shows that a remote teaching module plus 80 feedback-supported video readings brings nCLE-naive early-career endosonographers to roughly expert accuracy (89%) for mucinous versus non-mucinous cysts at a median of 38 cases, durable at 8 weeks; it does not establish competence at performing EUS-nCLE, nor performance on unfamiliar cases, and subtype sensitivities of 57-73% with kappa as low as 0.32 undercut the technique's main clinical rationale.","funding":"No funding statement; disclosures: JD Machicado is a speaker for Mauna Kea Technologies, SG Krishna is a speaker for and receives research support from Mauna Kea Technologies, and B Napoleon is a speaker for Mauna Kea Technologies; all other authors disclosed no financial relationships"},"38182527":{"kind":"guideline","limitations":["Although labelled evidence-based, the authors note that most studies on IPMN do not provide high-level evidence","EUS is not recommended in every case because results depend strongly on operator expertise and on resources for adequate cytological and molecular analysis, and its diagnostic ability is highly operator-dependent; MRI cannot be frequently performed in some regions because of cost","The cut-off value of mural nodule size for diagnosing HGD/IC remains controversial, and the presence of a mural nodule alone does not always have high impact on prediction","Thickened or enhancing cyst wall is an ambiguous factor whose measurement methods and predictive cut-off have not been established","Definitions of 'new onset' and 'acute exacerbation' of diabetes have not yet been determined","'Increase in size of MPD' is expected to predict aggressive behaviour but evidence on this dynamic issue is lacking, so it was not included as a worrisome feature","Nomogram limitations include lack of distinction between branch-duct and main-duct IPMN in some models, small numbers of resected IPMNs in some countries or regions, and lack of external validation","Accuracy of diagnosis of pancreatic cystic lesions is only 47-78% and of HGD/IC prediction 73-97%","The necessity of long-term surveillance remains unclear and will be determined by regional health economics, the risk of concomitant PDAC and patient age, condition, life expectancy and preference","T1 substaging per the Verona consensus has been followed by few reports to date and its clinical meaning, especially for the T1 subgroups, must be validated in future; a unique T stage for IPMN with invasive carcinoma remains a challenge","There have been many studies of the impact of low-grade dysplasia at the margin on recurrence but the results are very mixed, with insufficient data to recommend resecting additional tissue"],"critique":["n is null, and the resected-series rates of 31% and 62% high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma remain the quantitative backbone of the risk framework; although this version states plainly that the true rate across all branch-duct IPMNs is much lower, it does not supply that denominator, so the criteria are still calibrated on operated specimens","The two-option recommendation on stopping surveillance after 5 years is a recorded disagreement rather than a finding: the text says most Japanese physicians accept the low progression risk but remain concerned about concomitant PDAC, and the guideline resolves this by permitting either course at SIGN grade C. A pathway built on this cannot claim evidential support for whichever option it adopts","The geographic dependence of the concomitant PDAC rate is stated explicitly - most such studies come from Japan, where the whole gland is sectioned at 5 mm and clinicians are primed to look for it, while elsewhere the risk resembles the general population's - yet the 0.4-1.0% yearly figure and the 3- to 5-fold relative risk are then applied globally without adjustment for where a reader practises","The thresholds that changed did so on weak grounds: 2.5 mm per year replaces 5 mm per 2 years because 2.5 was 'reported most frequently' among values spanning 0.96-3.5 mm per year, and new-onset diabetes enters as a worrisome feature on risk ratios of 1.27 and 1.61 with no agreed definition of 'new onset' - the guideline says so and adopts it anyway","The thresholds that did not change were retained after the same text reports that a mural nodule of 5 mm or more carries an odds ratio of only 1.19-3.16 and MPD of 10 mm or more 1.06-1.76 in the newest multivariable models, and that a 10 mm nodule discriminates far better (odds ratio 7.90 versus 2.93); keeping the 5 mm and 10 mm lines 'because of lack of evidence strongly supporting these revisions' preserves criteria that the cited evidence undercuts, and places the burden of proof on change rather than on the status quo","Bringing EUS and EUS-FNA cytology inside the high-risk-stigmata assessment makes the risk classification depend on an operator-dependent test the same document says cannot be performed at the same level everywhere, and on a cytology with 28.7% overall sensitivity - so a negative result carries almost no weight while a positive one becomes an absolute surgical indication, an asymmetry never stated","No sensitivity, specificity or predictive values are reported for the revised high-risk-stigmata and worrisome-feature lists as a whole, three guideline generations after the framework was introduced; the surveillance protocol is stratified at 20 and 30 mm, and Hamada's subsequent validation in a 3336-patient cohort found risk well separated at 20 mm but not at 30 mm, so one of the two thresholds in the new protocol does not stratify","Surgical mortality and morbidity are again absent from the entire document, as is any cost-effectiveness estimate, even though health economics is invoked as a reason to consider stopping surveillance and as the framing for the whole discontinuation question","Zelga's additive worrisome-feature figures (22%, 34%, 59% and 100%) are quoted as a single study without sample sizes or confidence intervals, and a 100% rate with 4 or more features is the kind of small-cell result that does not survive replication; it is nonetheless the basis for recommending nomogram-assisted surgical decisions","Eleven authors, several of whom also authored the five commissioned systematic reviews and the validation cohorts cited, and the Kyoto working group overlaps substantially with the 2012 and 2017 Fukuoka groups whose criteria are being revised; no conflict-of-interest statement appears in this text extraction"],"bottom_line":"The current international guideline, which brought EUS and EUS-FNA cytology inside the risk classification, simplified surveillance into three size strata, adopted a 2.5 mm/year growth rate and new-onset diabetes as worrisome features, separated intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasm from IPMN, and for the first time offered the option of stopping surveillance for a stable cyst under 20 mm at 5 years; that stopping option is presented as one of two permissible courses at SIGN grade C, no operating characteristics are given for the risk tiers, and the malignancy rates behind the whole framework remain resected-series prevalences.","funding":"Supported by Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKEN) 22K19567 and 23H02984; the acknowledgements thank Prof. Masao Tanaka, Prof. Yoshifumi Takeyama and Prof. Kyoichi Takaori and name the contributors to the five systematic reviews; no conflict-of-interest statement appears in this extraction"},"38442782":{"kind":"review","limitations":["The malignancy risk of the most common cystic lesions - IPMN and MCN - remains poorly understood because of a paucity of natural history data and the difficulty of estimating the true population prevalence","Much of the current literature is limited by selection bias, and long-term prospective comparative effectiveness trials evaluating observation versus resection are lacking","Published studies are limited by incongruous use of definitions: 'malignant' may mean only invasive adenocarcinoma, or high-grade dysplasia, or both, and the criteria for a 'positive' cytology vary, with some studies using cytology only and others the presence of mucin or CEA above 192 ng/mL","The increasing incidence of cysts does not represent an increase in prevalence but detection bias from increased imaging use; although resources spent on diagnosis, surveillance and treatment have increased over two decades, the number of patients diagnosed with and surviving pancreatic adenocarcinoma has not changed","Available studies lack patient-centred factors such as underlying genetic risk, behaviours and comorbidity, and most patients with pancreatic cysts die of another cause","Cyst histologic subtype is often not considered or available when predicting malignant transformation and likely plays a role in prognosis","There is a paucity of data on the ability of cross-sectional imaging to diagnose small (<10 mm) cysts independently of further evaluation, and even EUS-FNA occasionally fails to give a definitive diagnosis in diminutive cysts because of the limited analyses possible on small fluid samples; most cysts are small when discovered, so both patient and provider are left with diagnostic ambiguity","Guidelines that refrain from time-based surveillance recommendations acknowledge insufficient knowledge of the natural history of the cyst and of the patient"],"critique":["n is null and this is a narrative review by three authors with no systematic search, no inclusion criteria and no quality appraisal; its Table 1 assigns malignant potential to each cyst type - 'very minimal', 'minimal', 'moderate' - explicitly 'based on author consensus', which is expert opinion presented in the typographic form of data and is likely to be cited as such","The five long-term branch-duct IPMN series in Table 2 are placed in a single column of 'rate of transformation' at 3.5-5.5% despite having structurally incompatible denominators: Pergolini's 20 of 363 is restricted to patients already observed beyond 5 years, Oyama's 30 of 804 is a competing-risk figure in a five-year survivor subset, and Crippa's 5 of 144 is a non-operative cohort selected for having worrisome features. The apparent agreement across countries and designs is an artefact of tabulating quantities that do not measure the same thing","The statement that branch-duct IPMN without worrisome features carries a risk 'similar to the general population' is taken from Marchegiani 2023, where that conclusion rests on 2 to 3 cancers in the relevant subgroups with confidence intervals reaching above 3; the review repeats the point estimate without the interval, and never sets it against Oyama's 6.7-fold standardised incidence ratio in cysts under 15 mm, which appears in its own Table 2","The cost arguments are presented without reconciliation: $3.6 million per cancer detected and $171,143 per QALY are used to frame surveillance as poor value, while a $20,096 per QALY figure for the same disease sits two paragraphs later, and the review does not explain that the two models differ in cyst size, guideline, era and assumptions","The claim that specificity above 67% for high-grade dysplasia or cancer would make surveillance cost-effective, and 'may be achieved' with NGS, adopts a threshold from a single Markov model and a test whose own validation studies tuned their allele-frequency rules in-sample and were conducted by a single laboratory","The population-versus-individual framing is offered as the crux of the controversy but no quantities are attached to either side - no estimate of how many cancers a stopping rule would miss, nor of how many operations and MRIs indefinite surveillance would add - so the central argument of the review is conducted without numbers","The review opens by observing that spending on cyst surveillance has risen steeply without changing pancreatic adenocarcinoma mortality, which is the strongest available argument that current surveillance does not work; it then describes surveillance strategies at length without returning to that observation, and the figure it uses to illustrate the opposite case is a single patient who progressed after choosing surveillance over completion pancreatectomy","The guideline comparison table reproduces several criteria inaccurately - for example listing the ACR high-risk stigma as 'MPD <10 mm' and a worrisome feature as 'MPD >7 cm' - so a reader using the table rather than the source documents may be misled about what each guideline requires"],"bottom_line":"A current narrative review that lays out cyst types, the diagnostic armamentarium and a side-by-side comparison of the five major guidelines, and frames surveillance cessation as a population-versus-individual trade-off; it establishes no new evidence, its malignancy estimates by cyst type are explicitly the authors' consensus, and its tabulated branch-duct transformation rates pool incompatible denominators into an apparent agreement.","funding":"None; the authors disclose no conflicts"},"38880125":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["The centre's surveillance protocol was not necessarily based on the revised Kyoto guidelines; surveillance was more intense for low-risk IPMNs, with imaging continued at 6- to 12-month intervals, so prospective data are needed on the risk-benefit balance of guideline-compliant surveillance","The cohort was established at a single tertiary care centre and a selection bias should be considered","There might be unaccounted confounding factors, although the findings were not materially altered by adjusting for major patient characteristics","A majority of participants were Japanese and the proportion of concomitant PDAC identified during long-term surveillance was relatively high, which may understate the predictive ability of the Kyoto criteria for carcinoma incidence","Rare parameters such as a caliber change of the MPD and IPMN wall thickening were too infrequent for robust statistical assessment","Further research is needed on the optimal cut-off values of predictive factors - CA19-9 for incidence, and IPMN size for both prevalence and incidence - and the null findings for high CA19-9 and size >=30 mm may be due to unvalidated cut-offs; risk was clearly stratified at 20 mm but not at 30 mm"],"critique":["An odds ratio of 2269 with a confidence interval from 310 to 16,600 is a separation artefact: the no-risk-factor stratum contained a single event among 2189 patients, so the model is fitting a near-empty cell, and reporting the figure as an effect size in the abstract misleads about what was measured","The short-term analysis is a prevalence study in which the exposures - a mural nodule, a dilated duct, positive cytology, jaundice - are themselves the triggers for the work-up that finds the carcinoma; the odds ratios therefore quantify how well the criteria select patients for investigation rather than how well they predict disease, and nothing in the design separates the two","The long-term analysis excludes anyone diagnosed with carcinoma or resected within 6 months, which strips prevalent cancers from the numerator while retaining their risk factors in the denominator, and the worrisome-feature analyses additionally exclude all HRS-positive patients, so the 0/1/2/3-4 feature gradient is measured in a cohort already purged of its highest-risk members","Half the events (68 of 138) were concomitant PDACs, and the worrisome-feature gradient holds only for IPMN-derived carcinoma (P for heterogeneity .002); the criteria therefore validate prediction of the lesion they describe and not of the cancer that accounts for half the carcinoma diagnoses and presents at a metastatic stage three times as often","Derived versus concomitant adjudication in this report rests on imaging continuity and histological transition without molecular confirmation, unlike the same group's 2020 analysis, so the split that carries the main biological conclusion is the least verifiable quantity in the paper","The cohort is the same University of Tokyo prospective database, over overlapping years, as Oyama 2020, with shared authors and an overlapping patient set; this is a re-analysis of a known cohort rather than external validation of the Kyoto criteria, and four members of the Kyoto working group are at this institution","The 2.7% and 6.1% post-five-year incidences bear directly on the guideline's stop-or-continue option, but they come from a centre that surveilled more intensively than the guideline advises - the authors say so - so they are an upper bound on what can be detected, not an estimate of what a guideline-compliant programme would find","Risk was not stratified at the 30 mm threshold that the Kyoto guidelines use to set the shortest surveillance interval, with the >=30 mm hazard ratio (1.75, 1.00-3.08) lower than that for 20-29 mm (2.07); the paper attributes this to an unvalidated cut-off rather than treating it as a failure of the criterion it set out to validate","No sensitivity, specificity or predictive values for the revised HRS/WF classification as a whole appear in the main text - they are relegated to supplementary tables - so a clinician cannot read off what the criteria rule in or out, only relative hazards"],"n":"3336 patients in the whole cohort for short-term analyses (3041 branch-duct, 271 mixed-type, 24 main-duct; baseline risk level none 2189, worrisome features 997, high-risk stigmata 150) and 3179 in the long-term cohort (none 2185, WF 960, HRS 34), with 22,339 person-years and a median follow-up of 6.2 years (range 0.5-23.6)","bottom_line":"The first large validation of the revised Kyoto criteria, establishing that they stratify both carcinoma prevalence (49% with high-risk stigmata vs 1.3% with worrisome features vs 0.05% with neither) and long-term incidence, with risk rising stepwise to a tenfold hazard at 3-4 worrisome features; it does not validate the guideline's surveillance protocol or its 30 mm threshold, the gradient holds only for IPMN-derived and not concomitant carcinoma, and the cohort overlaps the same centre's earlier series rather than providing external validation.","funding":"Supported by KAKENHI grants from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JP22H02841 to T Hamada and JP21K15368 to T Suzuki), the Practical Research for Innovative Cancer Control Program from AMED (JP21ck0106557 to Y Nakai), and grants from the Takeda Science Foundation and the Okinaka Memorial Institute for Medical Research; the funders had no role in the study. T Hamada has received research funding from the Daiichi Sankyo TaNeDS Funding Program; the remaining authors disclose no conflicts"}}
files.new: {"15131794":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["The analysed patients were a subset who underwent resection for symptoms, concern about malignancy or lack of a definitive diagnosis, so their characteristics may differ from an unselected population and the results may not apply to all patients with a pancreatic cyst","The CEA results, and particularly the cutoff values, may not be applicable if CEA assays with different characteristics are used"],"critique":["The 192 ng/mL threshold was selected to maximise correct classification in the same 112 patients in which it was then tested, with no split-sample, cross-validation or external cohort, so 79% accuracy is an optimistic in-sample estimate and the figure that entered every subsequent guideline was never validated here","Only 112 of 341 enrolled patients (33%) had histological verification, and verification depended on the very findings under test - a worrying EUS appearance or suspicious cytology made resection more likely - which is partial verification bias and distorts the apparent performance of all three tests in directions that cannot be signed from the data given","Mucinous lesions were 60% of the verified cohort and 59% of those were malignant or borderline, far above community prevalence, so the predictive values implied by these sensitivities and specificities do not transport to an incidental cyst clinic","Cytology was read by local cytologists at each of 13 institutions with no central review, while CEA was assayed centrally and blindly; the comparison therefore pits a standardised test against an unstandardised one, which penalises cytology by design","Cyst fluid was explicitly not analysed for amylase, mucin concentration or viscosity, so the comparison omits the cheapest and most widely used discriminators, including the one test that reliably excludes a pseudocyst","Only 7 serous cystadenomas were verified, so the low-CEA half of the claim rests on single digits, and the inflammatory group (n=27) carries a mean CEA of 36.8 ng/mL, which means the test's specificity for mucinous disease is being established largely against pseudocysts rather than against serous lesions","The study's conclusion - that endoscopists should send aspirated fluid for CEA - rests on a marker the data show cannot distinguish benign from malignant mucinous disease, since CEA ranges overlapped widely within the malignant group; the clinical decision that matters is left unaddressed","Histological interpretation was done locally and only reviewed from reports by one study pathologist, not from slides, so the reference standard itself was not uniformly applied"],"n":"341 consecutive patients enrolled and underwent EUS-FNA; 112 with histological confirmation analysed (68 mucinous, 7 serous, 27 inflammatory, 5 endocrine, 5 other)","bottom_line":"The study that established cyst fluid CEA at 192 ng/mL as the most accurate single test for separating mucinous from non-mucinous pancreatic cysts, at about 80% accuracy and better than EUS morphology or cytology either alone or combined; it does not establish that CEA identifies which mucinous cysts harbour high-grade dysplasia or cancer, and its threshold was derived and tested in the same 112-patient surgical subset."},"16111956":{"kind":"systematic review","limitations":["Wide variation in cytology sensitivity between studies, probably reflecting differences in cytopathologist experience, so sensitivity and specificity may be lower in non-specialised centres where aspirates are rarely seen","Rare cystic neoplasms including IPMT, pseudopapillary and solid tumours, cystic islet-cell tumours, lymphangioma, sarcoma and benign cysts - together 10-25% of all pancreatic cystic tumours - were excluded, so the data cannot be applied to them","Too few studies existed to pool other markers or viscosity, and there may be no added benefit from them over amylase, CEA and cytology","No multiple-regression analysis was performed to validate the suggestion that CEA, amylase, cytology and CA19-9 each have independent value in different subsets"],"critique":["The cutoffs were chosen to maximise correct classification within the same pooled dataset in which they are then reported, and the CEA >800 ng/mL threshold is described as 'arbitrarily set'; there is no validation sample, so all the operating characteristics are in-sample","The 450-patient figure is not a cohort: each marker has a different and much smaller denominator (amylase 155, CA19-9 136), the contributing studies did not all measure all markers, and so the apparent mutual consistency of the markers is partly determined by which studies happened to report which assay","The reference standard is not uniform or symmetric: nearly all MCA and MCAC were confirmed histologically or cytologically, whereas in two studies pseudocysts were diagnosed from a pancreatitis history plus follow-up and many SCAs were unverified - differential verification of the malignant arm inflates specificity for mucinous disease","The Frossard data were excluded post hoc because SCA CEA values were discordantly high, with no pre-specified rule and no explanation found; the authors report both versions, which is honest, but the headline numbers are the ones that survive the exclusion","Individual values were read off published scatter grams rather than obtained from authors, so extraction error is unquantified and unquantifiable","The analysis predates and explicitly excludes IPMN, which is now the commonest neoplastic pancreatic cyst; the management table the paper proposes - resect on CEA >800 or malignant cytology, do not resect on CEA <5 or CA19-9 <37 - therefore cannot be applied to the modal patient in current practice, and the omission is noted only as a caveat about rare tumours","Every cutoff has a sensitivity at or below 50%, so all four tests are rule-in only; the paper nonetheless advises 'no resection needed' on the strength of CEA <5 ng/mL and CA19-9 <37 U/mL, whose negative predictive values are 55% and 38% in its own tables","CA19-9 is recommended as an adjunct for indeterminate CEA on the basis of 136 patients and an accuracy of 46%, which is barely better than chance in a cohort with roughly even group sizes"],"n":"12 studies, 450 patients; amylase available in 155 (60 pseudocyst, 32 SCA, 32 MCA, 31 MCAC), CEA in 332 (125/79/64/64), CA19-9 in 136 (66/24/24/22), cytology for malignancy in 111","bottom_line":"Pooled individual-patient data fix the specificity of amylase <250 U/L, CEA <5 ng/mL, CEA >800 ng/mL and CA19-9 <37 U/mL at 95-98% with sensitivities of 19-50%, making each a rule-in rather than a screening test, and put cytology's sensitivity for malignancy at 48%; it establishes nothing about IPMN, which was excluded, and all its cutoffs were fitted to the data that report them."},"16327281":{"kind":"consensus","limitations":["The guidelines the criteria therefore validate prediction of the lesion they describe and not of the cancer that accounts for half the carcinoma diagnoses and presents at a metastatic stage three times as often","Derived versus concomitant adjudication in this report rests on imaging continuity and histological transition without molecular confirmation, unlike the same group's 2020 analysis, so the split that carries the main biological conclusion is the least verifiable quantity in the paper","The cohort is the same University of Tokyo prospective database, over overlapping years, as Oyama 2020, with shared authors and an overlapping patient set; this is a re-analysis of a known cohort rather than external validation of the Kyoto criteria, and four members of the Kyoto working group are at this institution","The 2.7% and 6.1% post-five-year incidences bear directly on the guideline's stop-or-continue option, but they come from a centre that surveilled more intensively than the guideline advises - the authors say so - so they are an upper bound on what can be detected, not an estimate of what a guideline-compliant programme would find","Risk was not stratified at the 30 mm threshold that the Kyoto guidelines use to set the shortest surveillance interval, with the >=30 mm hazard ratio (1.75, 1.00-3.08) lower than that for 20-29 mm (2.07); the paper attributes this to an unvalidated cut-off rather than treating it as a failure of the criterion it set out to validate","No sensitivity, specificity or predictive values for the revised HRS/WF classification as a whole appear in the main text - they are relegated to supplementary tables - so a clinician cannot read off what the criteria rule in or out, only relative hazards"],"n":"3336 patients in the whole cohort for short-term analyses (3041 branch-duct, 271 mixed-type, 24 main-duct; baseline risk level none 2189, worrisome features 997, high-risk stigmata 150) and 3179 in the long-term cohort (none 2185, WF 960, HRS 34), with 22,339 person-years and a median follow-up of 6.2 years (range 0.5-23.6)","bottom_line":"The first large validation of the revised Kyoto criteria, establishing that they stratify both carcinoma prevalence (49% with high-risk stigmata vs 1.3% with worrisome features vs 0.05% with neither) and long-term incidence, with risk rising stepwise to a tenfold hazard at 3-4 worrisome features; it does not validate the guideline's surveillance protocol or its 30 mm threshold, the gradient holds only for IPMN-derived and not concomitant carcinoma, and the cohort overlaps the same centre's earlier series rather than providing external validation.","funding":"Supported by KAKENHI grants from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JP22H02841 to T Hamada and JP21K15368 to T Suzuki), the Practical Research for Innovative Cancer Control Program from AMED (JP21ck0106557 to Y Nakai), and grants from the Takeda Science Foundation and the Okinaka Memorial Institute for Medical Research; the funders had no role in the study. T Hamada has received research funding from the Daiichi Sankyo TaNeDS Funding Program; the remaining authors disclose no conflicts"}}

files.old: {"16111953":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The authors state only that the findings 'suggest' a protective effect and that future large-scale studies are required to confirm the benefit","They note there are no data on how long the duct should be stented"],"critique":["Nineteen patients and three events cannot establish an effect. The nominally significant p = 0.02 comes from a 3-versus-0 comparison, and the intention-to-treat analysis the authors themselves perform is frankly negative (p = 0.3) - a result that should have been the headline rather than a mid-paper aside","Stopping early at an interim look triggered by a high event rate in the control arm is the classic route to an overestimated treatment effect; no alpha adjustment is applied, and the trial has roughly a fifth of its planned sample","The three analyses presented (per protocol excluding the failed placement, as-treated, intention-to-treat) give p = 0.05, 0.02 and 0.3 from 19 patients; reporting the most favourable as the result is selective","Single endoscopist, single centre, single operator technique - specifically en bloc snare without a submucosal cushion so as to include the sphincteric musculature - which the authors argue reduces later cannulation-related pancreatitis. The result therefore cannot be separated from one operator's method, and no learning-curve or centre-effect data exist","Patients were blinded but outcome ascertainment depended on patients reporting pain and then having enzymes checked; the endoscopist was necessarily unblinded, and whether the 24-hour telephone assessor's blinding was maintained for the stented patients who returned for fluoroscopy and stent removal is doubtful","Allocation by card from a sealed envelope without blocking or stratification produced unequal arms (11 vs 8) and a 9-year age difference between groups in a 19-patient trial; concealment by opaque envelope is weaker than central randomisation","The outcome window was only 24 hours, so delayed pancreatitis, bleeding, perforation, papillary stenosis and recurrence - the complications that matter over the longer term - were not captured at all","Electrosurgical generator changed during the study (Meditron to ERBE) and all three pancreatitis cases occurred with the ERBE device; generator is therefore confounded with time and potentially with allocation, and is not adjusted for","Pancreatitis was defined as threefold enzyme elevation with pain but enzymes were measured only in symptomatic patients, so asymptomatic hyperamylasaemia and milder events were differentially unascertained","The companion randomised trial in this depot (Lee 2016) found 18% versus 13% pancreatitis with wire-guided versus conventional papillectomy despite 100% stent success in the wire-guided arm, and the later ESGE guideline rates prophylactic stenting as moderate-quality evidence drawing on larger series - so this trial's 0% stented pancreatitis rate is almost certainly an artefact of its size"],"n":"19 patients enrolled and randomised (11 assigned to stent, 8 to no stent); final stent placement achieved in 10, so analysis compared 10 stented with 9 unstented patients","bottom_line":"The first and still most-cited randomised trial of prophylactic pancreatic stenting after snare ampullectomy, reporting 33% versus 0% pancreatitis, but it enrolled only 19 patients, was stopped early at an interim look, and lost statistical significance on its own intention-to-treat analysis - it is a signal consistent with a protective effect rather than proof of one.","funding":"Not stated"},"20071702":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The paper carries no limitations section; the authors note instead that the optimal duration of biliary drainage has never been established and that a shorter period may not allow recovery of metabolic abnormalities while a longer one risks stent occlusion and bile-duct inflammation","They point out that four of five earlier randomised trials used percutaneous rather than endoscopic drainage and included both proximal and distal obstruction, entities now considered different diseases needing different treatment","They concede that, given the poor results with plastic stents, drainage during neoadjuvant treatment might be better achieved with metal stents"],"critique":["The composite primary outcome counts drainage complications and surgical complications in the same tally, so a trial of whether drainage makes surgery safer is decided mainly by whether drainage itself causes harm. On the question clinicians actually ask - does jaundice at operation increase surgical risk? - the trial is null (47% vs 37%, RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.57-1.11), and that is the result buried in the secondary analysis","Plastic stents only. A 26% cholangitis rate and 30% stent-exchange rate are features of 10 Fr plastic endoprostheses left for 4-6 weeks; the trial cannot be read as evidence against short-course drainage or against self-expanding metal stents, which the authors themselves recommend for the neoadjuvant setting","Early surgery required guaranteed theatre capacity within a week at 13 hospitals; 3 patients crossed over to drainage because surgery could not be arranged in time. Outside a trial that logistic constraint is the usual reason drainage happens, so the comparison tests an idealised pathway","Noninferiority was the prespecified frame with a 10 percentage-point margin and one-sided alpha 0.05, yet the trial is universally cited as showing drainage causes harm. Converting a noninferiority design into a superiority claim post hoc, even with a nominal superiority test appended, inflates confidence in the direction of effect","The trial is a pancreatic-head trial: 92% had adenocarcinoma and site was recorded only as 'pancreatic versus periampullary' as a covariate, with no subgroup result for ampullary tumours. Ampullary cancers are typically diagnosed at lower bilirubin, are more often endoscopically accessible and are far more often resectable, so the applicability of these complication rates to ampullary disease is assumed rather than shown","Only 61% of patients ultimately had a resection and 31% had palliative bypass; the palliative subgroup showed the largest difference (55% vs 18%, p = 0.003), so the headline result is partly driven by patients who were never going to benefit from resection and in whom stenting would now be definitive therapy rather than preoperative preparation","No blinding was possible for patients or surgeons, and the primary outcome - a complication 'that prompted an additional intervention resulting in extension of stay, readmission or death' - is partly a healthcare-utilisation endpoint sensitive to unblinded clinician behaviour, even though an adjudication committee classified events blind","Baseline imbalance in sex (70% vs 52% male, p = 0.01) and BMI (24.0 vs 25.2, p = 0.03) occurred despite randomisation and is handled only by covariate adjustment","Mortality was 7% overall and did not differ between arms, but the trial had no power for this: the relative risk for death from a protocol complication was 0.48 with an interval from 0.15 to 1.51","Events were counted to 120 days after randomisation, which in the drainage arm includes a 4-6 week pre-surgical window with no equivalent exposure period in the early surgery arm - so the drainage group was observed at risk for longer before the operation, which mechanically favours early surgery on a time-unadjusted count","A 2003-2008 trial predates routine metal stenting, modern ERCP prophylaxis including rectal NSAIDs and current neoadjuvant pathways; the authors' own recommendation at the end of the paper effectively concedes that the intervention tested is no longer the intervention used"],"n":"202 randomised, 196 analysed (94 early surgery, 102 preoperative biliary drainage) after 6 exclusions (2 withdrew consent, 4 ineligible bilirubin); resection performed in 63 (67%) versus 57 (56%), p = 0.11","bottom_line":"Routine 4-6 week preoperative plastic-stent biliary drainage before resection for pancreatic head cancer roughly doubles overall serious complications (74% vs 39%) because of stent-related cholangitis and occlusion, without reducing surgery-related complications or mortality - so early surgery is preferred when it can be arranged; the trial says nothing specific about ampullary tumours, used only plastic stents, and its null secondary result on surgical complications is the finding most often overlooked.","funding":"Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development, which had no access to outcome data during the trial and no role in analysis or manuscript preparation; no endoscopic equipment or stents were donated by manufacturers. Two authors disclosed lecture or consulting fees (Boston Scientific; GI Dynamics, Covidien, Johnson & Johnson)."},"22782416":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The unadjusted primary analysis did not show a significant benefit for adjuvant chemotherapy, and the authors state explicitly that the positive multivariable result and the gemcitabine-specific result should be considered hypothesis generating","A separate survival analysis for each tumour type could not be built into the trial design because the low incidence of each would have required an unattainably large sample and timeline; the different types were combined pragmatically because presentation and surgery are the same","Intrapancreatic bile duct cancer may need to be treated as a completely separate entity, and grouping should perhaps be avoided not only for ampullary but also for more proximal bile duct cancers","There was no single central review of histological sections - only central review of pathology reports by several experienced pathologists, which the authors argue makes systematic error unlikely","The dichotomised intestinal/pancreatobiliary classification was not widely applied when the trial started","Postoperative CA19-9 had too many missing values to be retained in the final models","The survival effect of chemotherapy was modest, indicating a need for further improvement and for testing combination chemotherapy"],"critique":["The adjustment that converts the result from negative to positive was for age, bile duct histology, poor differentiation and node positivity - and the observation arm was prognostically the worst on two of those at baseline (poorly differentiated 33% vs 22% and 19%; node positive 62% vs 60% and 54%), so the shift from HR 0.86 to 0.75 is partly correcting a randomisation imbalance. That cuts both ways, but it means the 0.75 is not an independent confirmation of the primary analysis; it is the same data with the imbalance removed, and its CI (0.57-0.98) only just excludes 1","The trial was powered on 243 deaths and 430 patients to detect a 12% absolute 5-year gain (HR 0.68) across the pooled periampullary population. It was never powered for the ampullary subgroup, and it is the ampullary subgroup that pathway documents cite. With 297 ampullary patients, 151 deaths and three arms, no hypothesis test for ampullary-only survival is reported at all - the ampullary medians of 40.6/57.8/70.8 months appear without a p value","Pooling created a group in which chemotherapy appeared harmful: in the 96 bile duct patients both regimens had numerically shorter median survival than observation. Any pooled 'benefit' is therefore driven entirely by the ampullary and other patients, and the trial's own discussion concedes bile duct cancer may be a separate entity - which is an argument that the pooled primary analysis answered the wrong question","The subtype analysis that the field quotes as evidence that subtype does not predict chemotherapy response is grossly underpowered: 162 of 297 ampullary tumours (55%) were indeterminate, leaving 80 intestinal and 46 pancreatobiliary split across three treatment arms - roughly 15-27 patients per subtype-by-arm cell. No interaction test, no numbers per cell and no power calculation are given, and 'tests of heterogeneity within pathological subgroups did not reveal any significant findings' is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence","Subtype was assigned from central review of pathology reports, not of slides; the same institutional tradition that produced these categories has since shown that slide-based subtyping has only fair reproducibility and that 40% of ampullary carcinomas are mixed, so 55% indeterminate is unsurprising and the 135 classified cases are a non-random, more clear-cut subset","Overall survival and disease-free survival point in opposite directions by subtype (pancreatobiliary numerically longer OS but significantly shorter DFS), which is biologically incoherent and suggests differential post-recurrence treatment or informative censoring rather than a true subtype effect in either direction","Disease-free survival is positive for both regimens on adjusted Cox analysis (HR 0.69 and 0.68, both p = 0.02) while unadjusted DFS is flatly negative (p = 0.48), the same adjusted/unadjusted divergence as the primary endpoint - consistent with the adjustment carrying the result throughout","Delivery was poor: a fifth of the fluorouracil arm never received a dose, half of each chemotherapy arm did not complete six cycles, and median dose intensity was 78% and 88% of protocol. An intention-to-treat null result under that much non-receipt is uninformative about efficacy, and the authors do not report a per-protocol or dose-intensity sensitivity analysis","Screening data on how many patients were excluded and why were not collected routinely, so the degree of selection into the trial is unknown","Median survival of 35 months in the untreated observation arm is far better than the ampullary literature of the era, implying a fit, early-stage, highly selected population; the absolute benefit of adjuvant therapy in a frailer, node-positive clinic population cannot be read off this trial","Five patients randomised to gemcitabine were excluded post-randomisation as ineligible (3 metastatic, 2 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) along with 1 in observation, a small departure from strict intention-to-treat that moves in the direction of the treatment arms"],"n":"434 randomised, 428 in the primary analysis (144 observation, 143 fluorouracil plus folinic acid, 141 gemcitabine); 297 ampullary, 96 intrapancreatic bile duct, 35 other (10 duodenal, 25 nondescript); 244 deaths (57%) at analysis","bottom_line":"The only randomised trial of adjuvant chemotherapy in resected periampullary cancer was negative on its primary endpoint (HR 0.86, p = 0.25) and became positive only in a prespecified multivariable analysis adjusting for age, bile duct histology, grade and nodal status (HR 0.75, p = 0.03) that the authors themselves call hypothesis generating; it establishes neither a benefit specific to ampullary cancer - the ampullary subgroup was never powered or formally tested - nor that intestinal and pancreatobiliary subtypes respond differently, since only 135 of 297 ampullary tumours could be subtyped at all.","funding":"Cancer Research United Kingdom; National Cancer Institute of Canada and Canadian Cancer Society; Fonds de Recherche de la Societe Nationale Francaise de Gastroenterologie; Fondazione Italiana Malattie del Pancreas; Health and Medical Research Council of Australia and state Cancer Councils; Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group. JPN part funded by the Liverpool NIHR Pancreas Biomedical Research Unit; MM part funded by the Oxford NIHR Biomedical Research Centre. Sponsors stated to have had no role in design, conduct, analysis or manuscript. No author conflicts of interest reported."},"23026934":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["No limitations section; the authors concede only that the ampullary-NOS category doubles as a waste-basket for cases that cannot be confidently assigned, and that whether the intra-ampullary group's survival advantage reflects small invasion size or a genuinely different biology is unknown","They acknowledge the periampullary-duodenal versus duodenal carcinoma survival comparison failed to reach significance because of small numbers"],"critique":["The four categories were assigned retrospectively from archived gross descriptions and slides by the same authors who devised the scheme - no blinded or independent reassignment, and no interobserver agreement statistic, so the reproducibility of the gross algorithm that the whole classification rests on is untested here","The periampullary-duodenal group that anchors the favourable-prognosis claim has only 12 patients, 6 of them node positive; the survival estimates carry no confidence intervals anywhere in the paper and no multivariable model adjusting for T stage, node status or invasion size is reported despite a Cox model being described in the methods","Invasion size - the variable that drives the survival ordering - was in part estimated by applying an invasive/non-invasive ratio read off slides to the gross size, i.e. derived rather than measured, which biases exactly the comparison between the preinvasive-rich (intra-ampullary) and preinvasive-poor (ampullary-ductal) groups","Comparators are convenience cohorts from the same archives (113 PDAC, 55 duodenal) with no matching for stage, size, node status or treatment, and adjuvant therapy is not recorded at all, so the headline 'ampullary carcinoma is distinct from PDAC' survival gap conflates stage migration and resectability with biology","Follow-up was partly obtained from SEER and by telephoning treating physicians, with cases carrying missing values excluded variable by variable, so denominators shift between tables without being stated","Reclassifying 21% of cases out of the ampullary category inevitably removes the worst-prognosis tumours (mostly pancreatic) from the ampullary group, which mechanically improves ampullary survival relative to the historical literature - a definitional effect the paper presents as a biological finding"],"n":"249 strictly defined ampullary carcinomas culled from 1469 malignant pancreatoduodenectomy specimens, compared with 113 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas and 55 non-ampullary duodenal carcinomas","bottom_line":"Establishes a reproducible-in-principle anatomic definition of ampullary carcinoma and shows that four gross/microscopic site-specific subsets differ markedly in stage and outcome, but the prognostic separation rests on small, unadjusted, single-reader subgroups and does not establish the classification's reproducibility or independence from stage.","funding":"Supported in part by the Georgia Cancer Coalition Distinguished Cancer Clinicians and Scientists Program; authors declare no financial interest in any commercial company pertaining to the article"},"25293823":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design with no predefined criteria for proceeding from EUS to endoscopic or surgical resection, which may have produced inconsistent surgical referral and influenced endoscopic outcomes","The exact length of intraductal extension was not documented (only that it ranged from subcentimetre to about 1 cm)","The data represent only the subset of ampullary tumours at the institution that had EUS, since some patients went directly to ERCP"],"critique":["The reference standard is circular for the lesions that matter most: for endoscopically resected adenomas, absence of intraductal extension was assumed whenever resection was complete with a negative margin and cholangiography showed no ductal extension - so EUS is being validated partly against a composite that already includes EUS-era endoscopic judgement, which inflates specificity and accuracy","The two comparisons use different denominators (90, 102 and 81 patients) drawn from the same cohort by availability of ERCP or of a resection specimen, so the claim that EUS and ERCP 'perform similarly' compares non-overlapping subsets rather than paired readings in the same patients","Sensitivity rests on very few events: 9-12 patients with intraductal extension in each analysis, which is why the AUROC confidence intervals are wide and why the EUS-versus-ERCP difference cannot be resolved","The 90% T-staging accuracy is carried almost entirely by correctly calling 65 of 66 lesions confined to the ampulla; for the invasive categories that would actually change management, accuracy was 78-80% and EUS systematically understaged","Six endosonographers and six ERCP endoscopists over 15 years, with no blinding, no central re-reading and no interobserver data; the authors concede EUS is operator dependent and that their results may reflect high-volume performance, which limits transfer to community practice","The 91% complete-resection rate is presented as evidence that EUS triaged patients well, but it is a before-after comparison with the same group's earlier 73% series and could equally reflect cohort selection, era effects or stricter criteria; patients deemed unresectable at EUS were excluded from that earlier study, making the two rates non-comparable","A 1998-2012 accrual spans radial and linear instruments and major changes in echoendoscope technology (GF-UM20 through GF-UC140P), and the radial/linear comparison is reported on 75 versus 21 patients without a formal test","The 17% non-adenomatous rate on papillectomy is a striking finding about referral biopsy reliability, but it also means the cohort's composition - and therefore every accuracy estimate - depends on outside histology that the centre did not verify"],"n":"119 patients undergoing EUS for an ampullary lesion (99 with adenoma or adenocarcinoma); ERCP in 90; surgical pathology available for 102 (EUS comparison) and 81 (ERCP comparison); 58 underwent endoscopic papillectomy","bottom_line":"In expert hands and with no biliary stent in place, EUS stages ampullary lesions about as well as ERCP against surgical pathology and is excellent at confirming T1 disease, but it misses roughly a fifth of intraductal extensions and a fifth of deeper invasion, and this retrospective design with a partly circular reference standard cannot show that adding EUS improves resection outcomes.","funding":"None stated; all authors disclosed no relevant financial relationships"},"2571019":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["No limitations section. The authors note that the retrospective series yielded fewer polyps with fewer biopsies and attribute between-centre variation in reported prevalence (28% to 100%) to the same technical differences","They state that upper gastrointestinal cancer develops slowly in FAP, with a median interval of 22 years after colectomy in a cited series of 37 patients, so natural history was not observed in this study","They acknowledge that the natural history of these polyps is largely unknown, which is why the mortality of prophylactic pancreatoduodenectomy must be weighed against it, and that endoscopic removal is often impractical while photodynamic therapy and vitamin C chemoprevention are unproven"],"critique":["THE STAGING SYSTEM THAT THIS LITERATURE STILL USES WAS NEVER VALIDATED HERE. It was devised from a single cross-sectional screening round, with the four components and their cut-points assigned by the authors on the basis of 'known adenoma/cancer risk factors' rather than derived from or tested against any cancer outcome. No patient in this paper developed duodenal cancer during the study, so the association between stage IV and malignancy is asserted, not measured - and the four subsequent decades have never produced a formal validation, as the Mavani paper in this depot notes","The score has no weighting rationale: polyp number, size, histology and dysplasia each contribute 1-3 points as though equally important, and the stage boundaries (0, 1-4, 5-6, 7-8, 9-12) are arbitrary breaks in a 4-12 point range. Later work in this depot shows large polyp size rather than polyp number carries the cancer risk, and that the score omits the papilla entirely despite this very paper showing that is where the disease concentrates","The paper's own strongest finding - that the papilla is twice as likely to be adenomatous as the surrounding duodenum and that periampullary biopsy found adenoma in 11 patients with an otherwise normal duodenum - is not incorporated into the score that the paper proposes, an internal inconsistency that took until the 2019 ESGE guideline to correct","Because the score requires histology for two of its four components, it mandates biopsy of duodenal polyps and the papilla; ampullary biopsy is now known to cause pancreatitis and to produce fibrosis that compromises later endoscopic resection, so the system creates a harm that current guidelines explicitly try to avoid","47 of the 102 prospective patients also contribute to the retrospective series, so the prospective-versus-retrospective yield comparison is a within-patient comparison of two eras presented alongside a between-series comparison, and the 190-540% increases conflate better instruments, a single experienced endoscopist, and more biopsies without separating them","Everything is cross-sectional: 'stage IV occurred more often in the elderly' is a prevalence observation across ages, not progression, and cannot distinguish disease progression from cohort effects or ascertainment","No interobserver or intraobserver reproducibility data for polyp counting, size estimation or dysplasia grading, the four inputs to the score. Two of the ongoing studies the Soons review lists, three decades later, are still trying to establish exactly this","The mortality comparison used to motivate the programme (9 upper GI versus 4 rectal cancer deaths) comes from a separate 1948-1987 cohort of 197 patients with no denominators by follow-up time and no competing-risk accounting, in an era when colectomy practice and rectal surveillance differed entirely from the screened population","The bile-exposure hypothesis for the distal duodenal and periampullary distribution is offered with experimental and epidemiological citations but no measurement in these patients, and the search for a bile tumour promoter it launched has not succeeded","The surveillance intervals recommended (3 years for mild/moderate, at least yearly for stage IV) are stated without any analysis of interval cancers, cost or patient burden, and remain substantially the intervals in use today","The text extraction for this paper is incomplete and damaged: the 'Severity of duodenal polyposis' table - which carried the number of patients per stage and the mean polyp measurements - renders as an empty stub, and the file continues into an unrelated Lancet article on cell-surface peptidases, so the per-stage distribution beyond the 11 stage IV patients cannot be verified from this source"],"n":"102 patients screened prospectively (69 families, 59 men, 43 women, mean age 41 years, range 14-66);
