but the recurrence-free survival difference favoured surgery at p = 0.052 in only 55 matched patients, T stage is never reported, and allocation was driven by the same variables used for matching.","funding":"A grant from the Korean Society of Gastrointestinal Cancer Research (2021); authors declare no conflict of interest or financial ties"},"37595391":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective single-institution design may introduce selection bias despite the 10-year window at a tertiary academic centre","Many cases lack follow-up biopsy or resection pathology, so the concordance and discordance rates reflect only the cases that had follow-up"],"critique":["The denominator problem the authors mention is fatal to the headline numbers: concordance is computed on 90 of 252 patients (36%), and the patients who went on to resection are precisely those whose biopsy or clinical picture raised concern, so the 8.9% major discrepancy rate is a lower bound on the false-negative rate that could be far higher in the unresected 64%","Sensitivity of 60% for biopsy and 89% for combined biopsy plus cytology is calculated on 20 and 9 cases respectively; no confidence intervals are given, and with 9 cases the combined estimate could as easily be 50% as 99%","The 'combined biopsy and cytology improves sensitivity' recommendation is confounded by indication: cytology was ordered in 88% of periampullary but 17% of ampullary tumours, i.e. precisely for deep-seated lesions where biopsy was expected to fail, so the incremental yield of cytology is not estimable from these data","Three of five pathologists knew the malignant cytology result before signing out the biopsy, so the biopsy diagnoses are not independent of the comparator used to judge them","Assigning 7 of 8 false negatives to 'sampling limitation' rather than interpretive error is a retrospective judgement by the same authors who signed out some of the cases, with no blinded re-review or second-reader adjudication; the one error they did identify was found only because DOG-1 was run retrospectively, which suggests the method would not detect interpretive misses in glandular lesions","The resected series collapses true ampullary (12), distal bile duct (6), pancreatic (1) and GIST (1) tumours into one narrative, so stage and nodal statements mix entities the companion literature insists must be kept apart","No interobserver reproducibility data for the dysplasia grading that generates 27 of the 35 discordances, although the paper cites published intraobserver and interobserver variability in exactly this setting","The p53 immunostain recommended as a practical aid is described from local practice with no accuracy data from this cohort"],"n":"318 ampullary biopsy specimens from 252 patients, with 169 follow-up biopsy/resection specimens available for 90 patients; 21 resected cases analysed clinicopathologically","bottom_line":"Confirms with institutional data that a benign ampullary biopsy does not exclude malignancy - almost 9% of biopsies with follow-up were benign where the resection showed cancer, nearly all from sampling limitation - and suggests combining biopsy with cytology, but the estimates come from the third of patients who had follow-up pathology and the cytology comparison is confounded by indication.","funding":"Not applicable (no funding)"},"38015261":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective single-centre tertiary care experience, limiting generalisability","Identifying recurrence remains technically challenging even with narrow band imaging and high-definition white light, particularly intraductal recurrence","Follow-up was not uniform and the mean duration was only 2.8 years; because an uptick in recurrence may occur after 4 years and not all patients were followed that long, the results may underestimate the true recurrence rate","Given the low number of recurrences, identification of risk factors was underpowered","All procedures were performed by endoscopists with substantial ERCP experience, and papillectomy carries an ASGE level 4 complexity rating, further limiting generalisability"],"critique":["The internal arithmetic does not add up: the abstract reports 20 recurrences, but the en bloc versus piecemeal breakdown gives 13 plus 4 (17), and the complete versus residual breakdown gives 15 plus 2 (17). Three recurrences are unaccounted for in both stratifications, so the denominators behind the comparisons cannot be verified","The paper's central claim about timing is stated two different ways: the abstract says 9 of 20 recurrences (45%) occurred after the first 2 years of surveillance, while the discussion says 'nearly half the recurrences occurred after 3 years of surveillance' and that the probability of recurrence 'experienced a leap 4 years after papillectomy'. The Kaplan-Meier table shows no events in year 4 at all, so the narrative does not match the data","Recurrence counts by resection type run counter to every other series and to the paper's own framing: 19.4% after en bloc versus 7.0% after piecemeal resection, and 16.5% after initially complete versus 6.1% after residual-tissue resection. These are reported without comment, but they are the signature of detection bias - patients with piecemeal or residual disease were scoped more intensively early, had their lesions re-treated, and so were classified as residual rather than recurrent","That classification is the deeper problem: by requiring one negative surveillance endoscopy before an event counts as recurrence, and by allowing multiple treatment sessions within 'complete eradication', the study converts early incomplete resection into non-events and shifts the apparent recurrence curve rightwards - which is precisely the direction needed to argue for longer surveillance","With 20 events and 13 candidate variables, the Cox model is severely overfitted; every adjusted hazard ratio is below 1.4 with intervals spanning 0.1 to 7.7, so the finding that 'no variables predicted recurrence' is uninformative rather than reassuring, as the authors concede","Mean follow-up of 2.8 years against a mean time to recurrence of 3.2 years means more than half the person-time needed to observe the events being described was never accumulated; the 5-year cumulative estimate of 14.5% rests on a thin tail, and the recommendation to extend surveillance to 10 years is driven by a single outlier recurrence at 9.75 years","The 18-year accrual window spans the introduction of high-definition endoscopy, narrow band imaging, radiofrequency ablation and routine rectal NSAIDs (given to only 26.5% of this cohort), so technique, detection sensitivity and complication risk all changed within the cohort, and no era analysis is presented","21 patients with adenocarcinoma are pooled into an adenoma recurrence series; only 12 of them entered the recurrence analysis, and 2 recurred with adenocarcinoma - events with entirely different clinical meaning from an adenoma recurrence, counted in the same rate","The FAP comparison that contradicts the much-cited 58% recurrence figure from Ma et al. is based on 35 FAP patients with a shorter follow-up than that study, and the authors acknowledge this, yet the abstract-level message ('recurrence rate did not differ by baseline pathology') invites readers to drop FAP-specific surveillance","Adverse events of 27.2% including 4.8% perforation and 2.2% severe pancreatitis are higher than in most comparator series in this depot, but are reported without any analysis of predictors or era, and are not weighed against the recurrence findings in the conclusion","Follow-up data were supplemented by telephone calls to patients, an ascertainment method that cannot confirm histological recurrence and introduces differential completeness between patients still attending the centre and those lost to it","Several authors declare consultancies with endoscope and device manufacturers (Boston Scientific, Olympus, Cook, Medtronic) in a paper whose conclusion is to extend endoscopic surveillance to 10 years"],"n":"165 papillectomies screened, 136 patients with adenomatous pathology analysed (mean age 61.9, SD 15; 70 women, 51.5%; mean lesion size 21.2 mm, SD 12); 124 (91.2%) achieved complete eradication and entered the recurrence analysis with 345.8 person-years of follow-up (mean 2.8 years per patient, SD 3.3)","bottom_line":"Reports a 16.1% recurrence rate (5.8 per 100 person-years) after endoscopic papillectomy with recurrences occurring as late as 9.75 years and roughly half after the recommended 2-year surveillance window, which supports longer follow-up; but the event counts are internally inconsistent, the mean follow-up (2.8 years) is shorter than the mean time to recurrence (3.2 years), and the counter-intuitive finding of more recurrence after en bloc and after initially complete resection points to detection bias in how residual disease was classified.","funding":"NIH T32DK007038 (SH). Multiple author disclosures: advisory board membership and consultancies with Boston Scientific, Olympus, Cook Medical, Medtronic, Cernostics, Exact Sciences and Interpace, and research funding from Lucid, Ambu and CDx."},"39642968":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design in which selection bias and missing data cannot be definitively excluded, mitigated by requiring consecutive inclusion and by the matched analysis","No formal study monitoring was possible because of limited resources, and monitoring of cases not included during the study period was not possible","Both low- and high-volume centres were included and centre volume was not analysed, which the authors defend as better reflecting daily practice","Excluding patients with missing data could itself introduce selection bias, although an exclusion analysis showed those patients were comparable on age, sex, comorbidities and lesion size","Recurrence can only be reliably excluded by careful endoscopy with routine biopsy even when macroscopy is normal, and such detailed data are not available in a large retrospective database, so later recurrences cannot be excluded","The reported 16% recurrence after histologic R0 means complete resection should be interpreted with caution","Submucosal injection, used in 24.2% of matched papillectomy patients, is no longer recommended by ESGE but was permitted by the original database criteria and could have influenced the endoscopic results","The study was not designed to analyse survival","Lesions beyond 30 mm could not be evaluated because too few were available in the matched cohorts","A randomised trial would give the highest level of evidence but is judged unrealistic: a two-armed trial would need 190 randomised patients (95 per group, alpha 0.05, power 0.95, effect size 0.5) and with an estimated 30% dropout a screening population of 315 patients with ampullary lesions, and surgical ampullectomy is not broadly available"],"critique":["The matched comparison is almost entirely one-sided in construction: the 62 matched pairs represent 98.4% of the eligible surgical patients but only 10.9% of the eligible papillectomy patients, so the surgical arm is its whole population while the endoscopic arm is a 1-in-9 selection chosen to resemble it. Any residual difference in the matched analysis reflects which papillectomy patients could be matched, not a balanced contrast","Matching omitted the variables that most obviously drove the choice of procedure and the chance of R0: intraductal extension, bile and pancreatic duct dilation, and the use of concomitant ablation (patients ablated at the index papillectomy were deliberately excluded from matching). Table 4 shows intrabiliary extension on imaging and duct dilation still differed significantly after matching (21% vs 8.1%, p = 0.01; 45.2% vs 30.6%, p = 0.001), so confounding by indication survives the propensity model","Follow-up was more than twice as long in the surgical arm in both cohorts (37.5 vs 15.5 months after matching), which biases the recurrence comparison - the paper's clearest finding - against the endoscopic arm's apparent advantage and in favour of the surgical arm's 3.2%; a recurrence rate cannot be compared between arms observed for different durations without a time-to-event analysis, and none is presented for recurrence","Conversely, surveillance intensity was asymmetric in the other direction: endoscopic patients were routinely scoped with biopsies of the scar while surgical patients were not systematically re-scoped, so the fivefold recurrence difference conflates true residual disease with differential ascertainment. The authors acknowledge recurrence 'much depends on the scrutiny of follow-up' but still attribute the difference to the deeper resection plane of ampullectomy","The surgical arm has 63 patients and 6 cancers. Every surgical subgroup statement - 66.6% R0 in cancer (4 of 6), 92.9% R0 in adenoma (53 of 57), 3.2% recurrence (2 of 63) - rests on single-digit numerators, and the only procedure-related death also sits in that arm, so the safety comparison (1.9% vs 3.2%, p = 0.38) has no power at all to detect the morbidity difference that drives the clinical choice","23.2% of the 1673 eligible datasets were excluded for missing or inconclusive data and a further 652 for clinical reasons, leaving 40% of papillectomies and 25% of ampullectomies. The exclusion analysis compares only age, sex, comorbidities and lesion size - not stage, margin or outcome - so it cannot rule out that outcome-related data were differentially missing","The R0 definition is applied to specimens handled by local pathologists at 58 centres over 14 years with no central review, no interobserver assessment and no standard protocol; given that the adjacent literature shows 26% of en bloc papillectomy specimens cannot even be margin-assessed, R0 is being compared between a fragmented endoscopic specimen and an intact surgical one, which structurally favours surgery independent of oncological completeness","Attributing additional ablation at the index procedure to presumed visible residual tissue and therefore reclassifying it as R2 is a reasonable assumption, but it is an assumption made retrospectively by the authors; the 65.9% figure that results is then used as the real papillectomy success rate, and both 80.2% and 65.9% appear in the paper without a single preferred estimate","T1a and T1b cancers are pooled in most analyses despite the authors noting these carry significantly different nodal metastasis risk, and the 13 T1b patients treated endoscopically are precisely the group in whom local resection is most questionable","The matched-cohort severe complication counts are 1 versus 2 events, yet the paper concludes 'both procedures were safe'; with these numbers a two- or threefold difference in serious morbidity would be undetectable","Overall survival is reported as comparable in a study the authors concede was not designed to analyse survival, with median follow-up 21 months in a disease whose resected median survival exceeds 4 years - the survival curves carry essentially no information and should not be used to support equivalence","Procedures spanning 2007-2020 include the pre-ESGE-guideline era, submucosal injection in a quarter of matched endoscopic cases, and the introduction of endobiliary radiofrequency ablation; no era stratification is performed despite technique having changed materially"],"n":"From 2862 patients in the ESAP database (1189 pancreatoduodenectomies excluded first), 1673 remained (1422 papillectomy, 251 surgical ampullectomy); after exclusions 569 papillectomy (40.0% of database papillectomies) and 63 surgical ampullectomy (25.1%) were analysed, with 62 matched pairs; median follow-up 21 months (IQR 10-47)","bottom_line":"The largest comparison of endoscopic papillectomy with transduodenal surgical ampullectomy shows that a third of procedures in both arms were done for the wrong indication (non-neoplastic histology or advanced cancer), that surgery achieves higher initial R0 (90% vs 73%) with far lower recurrence after R0 (3.2% vs 16%) but at 7 times the procedure time and 11 extra hospital days, and that papillectomy fails in two-thirds of T1 cancers; but the matched analysis pairs the entire surgical population with a 1-in-9 selection of endoscopic patients, follow-up was twice as long in the surgical arm, and surveillance intensity differed, so the recurrence gap is inflated by design.","funding":"The authors have not declared a specific grant for this research from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors. Multiple author disclosures including honoraria from FUJIFILM and Falk Foundation and institutional consultancies with Boston Scientific, Cook Medical and Pentax Medical. Ethics approval from the University of Leipzig (455/18-ek)."},"39831703":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective multi-institutional data with the usual biases; overall statistical power remained low because of disease rarity despite multiple centres","The small sample prevented splitting into derivation and validation cohorts, so the proposed score has not undergone formal validation","Ampullary lesions were not separated from duodenal lesions involving the periampullary region, although no outcome difference was found between them","Not every patient was tested genetically for FAP, MUTYH-associated polyposis or other mutations, though all underwent colonoscopy and family history assessment","Sampling bias is acknowledged because the cohort consists only of non-FAP periampullary adenomas that went on to pancreatoduodenectomy; the high malignancy rate reflects selection of high-risk cases by tumour size and location, and the true denominator - including patients managed by endoscopic mucosal resection or transduodenal resection - is unclear","A prospective study to identify the true denominator may not be feasible given the low incidence"],"critique":["The three risk strata are reported with mutually inconsistent numbers: the abstract gives low risk n = 26, intermediate n = 59, high n = 26 with rates 10.3%, 44.1% and 88.2%; the results text gives 11.5%, 41.7% and 84.6%; Table 4 gives 3/29, 26/59 and 30/34. Three different sets of denominators for the paper's central output means the score's calibration cannot be verified from the published data","The score was derived and evaluated in the same 127 patients with no split-sample, bootstrap or cross-validation, no c-statistic, no calibration plot and no sensitivity or specificity at any threshold. An OR of 77.5 for the high-risk group (CI 15.9-375.9) is the signature of an in-sample fit, and the paper's own concession that validation was impossible should preclude clinical use","The denominator problem the authors acknowledge is fatal to the score's intended purpose: everyone in the cohort had a Whipple, so the score is calibrated on the subset already judged to need resection. A patient weighing resection against endoscopic surveillance is by definition outside this population, and applying a 46% baseline malignancy rate to them would badly overestimate risk - exactly the misuse the shared-decision framing invites","Two of the four score components are proxies for obstruction, not for neoplastic progression: 'any preoperative symptom' (worth 2 points) is a list including fatigue, nausea and dark urine, and common bile duct dilation of 9 mm or more. Jaundice and biliary stenting were dropped from the model as redundant with symptoms, which concedes the point - the score largely measures whether the lesion is obstructing, and the discussant at the meeting objected that a jaundiced patient with no other factor scores only 1-2","The inverse complication relationship is presented as a feature of the score but has a simpler explanation the paper does not address: patients with benign pathology had soft, non-atrophic glands and non-dilated ducts because they had no obstructing cancer, and fistula risk follows gland texture and duct size. Adjusting for duct size and texture in the final model does not remove this, because the same obstruction physiology that lowers fistula risk is what the score is detecting","The complication finding only becomes significant after the three prespecified strata are collapsed at score 3 - across the strata as defined it was non-significant (p = 0.11) with the intermediate and high groups indistinguishable (27.1% vs 29.4%). Choosing the dichotomy that yields p = 0.047 after the three-group comparison failed is a post hoc cut-point","Preoperative dysplasia grade carries 2 of the 6 points but was read by local pathologists at 8 centres over 12 years, with no central review and no interobserver data - and the invited discussants specifically questioned whether a pathologist seeing roughly one such case per year can reliably separate high- from low-grade dysplasia","Volume was extremely low: 127 patients across 8 institutions over 12 years, about 1.3 cases per centre per year, so biopsy technique, number of biopsies, prior attempted endoscopic resection and pathology interpretation almost certainly varied in ways that cannot be modelled - a point the discussants raised and the authors do not rebut with data","EUS findings are absent from the entire paper despite both discussants noting that these are major centres where EUS would be routine; omitting the modality that best assesses intraductal extension and depth from a preoperative risk score is a substantial gap, and no explanation is given","Lesion size was missing for 27 of 127 patients (21%) and was then excluded from the score on the grounds that it did not differ between groups - a conclusion drawn from data with a fifth missing and no imputation","Black race was associated with benign final pathology (26.5% vs 11.9%) and with a different risk profile, in a cohort where race also tracked with symptoms and stenting; no analysis addresses whether differential access to earlier endoscopic diagnosis is embedded in the score's components","The 46.4% malignancy rate is compared with the same group's earlier single-centre figure of 29%, with no explanation for the difference other than cohort composition - which again points to the selection the score cannot escape"],"n":"127 patients of 189 reviewed; median age 65 years (34-89), 57 men (44.9%); 82 (64.6%) preoperative duodenal adenoma and 45 (35.4%) ampullary adenoma, with ampullary involvement in 84 of 119 (70.6%); 59 (46.4%) had malignancy on final pathology","bottom_line":"Confirms in the largest surgical series that nearly half of sporadic periampullary adenomas taken to pancreatoduodenectomy harbour cancer and that patients with benign final pathology paradoxically suffer threefold more major complications, and proposes a 0-6 malignancy risk score from age, bile duct diameter, symptoms and high-grade dysplasia; but the score is derived and tested in the same 127 already-resected patients with no validation, its published strata carry three inconsistent sets of numbers, and two of its four components are proxies for biliary obstruction.","funding":"National Cancer Institute of the NIH award K12 CA237806 (Emory K12 Clinical Oncology Training Program, Dr Shah); Contardi Research Fellowship; Georgia Clinical and Translational Science Awards UL1 TR002378. Nothing to disclose for the study; disclosures outside its scope include grant funding from Cantargia AB and consultancies with Intera Oncology, Stryker Medical and Intuitive Surgical."},"40729532":{"kind":"consensus","limitations":["The Delphi methodology, while the best option for reaching consensus, carries the difficulty of capturing all key issues in the literature during questionnaire development, depends on panellists' ongoing willingness to participate, and risks skewed data because those less confident about a topic may not participate","Although the stated aim was to cover all non-pancreatic cancers of the periampullary region, more recommendations relate to ampullary cancer than to common bile duct or duodenal cancer; the authors accept this imbalance as reflecting greater uncertainty and need for guidance about ampullary cancer","For a considerable proportion of the consensus questions there are fairly limited published data, so most recommendations are supported only by a low level of evidence, which the authors say highlights the early stage of knowledge about periampullary cancer","The authors state that the lack of consensus definitions and standardisation, together with high interobserver variability, has hindered consistent conclusions across studies - particularly regarding patient management including the efficacy of adjuvant chemotherapy, which remains highly controversial because of these inconsistencies"],"critique":["Almost every recommendation is graded low level of evidence with a weak form of recommendation, or rests on expert opinion alone. This is honest, but it means a document that will be used to standardise reporting worldwide is in substance a codification of the opinions of 43 experts, most of them from the pathology study groups that initiated it","THE PROCESS METRICS PROMISED ARE NOT REPORTED. The methods describe an independent Jury Committee calculating a 'Quality Score' using the AGREE II tool across 23 items and six domains, and an audience vote on each recommendation at the Brescia meeting. Neither result appears anywhere in the paper - no AGREE II score, no domain breakdown, no audience agreement percentages. The quality-assurance apparatus is described but its findings are withheld","The Delphi convergence is itself a weak signal: 33 of 57 recommendations reached 80% agreement in round one and the rest were revised by the responsible expert team according to the dissenting comments and re-voted until they passed. Revising a statement until it achieves consensus guarantees consensus; the final 50 of 51 figure measures iteration, not agreement on the original propositions","The 30% threshold for calling a tumour 'mixed' subtype has no stated derivation. It is a cut-point that will determine subtype assignment in a large fraction of cases - and the consensus itself cites that about 40% of ampullary carcinomas are mixed - yet no data, reproducibility study or sensitivity analysis is offered for choosing 30% over 10% or 50%","Renaming the hybrid category 'tubular-NOS' is a nomenclature change, not a solution. The underlying problem documented in this depot - that five pathologists agree on morphological subtype at kappa 0.39 with full agreement in 23% of cases - is unaddressed: no interobserver reproducibility study of the new definitions is reported or planned, so the consensus standardises the words without demonstrating that the categories can be applied consistently","The consensus states plainly that the prognostic and predictive role of subtype is unclear because of inconsistent historical definitions, yet it simultaneously retains subtyping as a required element of the pathology report and advises subtyping on biopsy where subtype 'may affect treatment'. If subtype has no established treatment implication, there is no situation in which that condition is met","Reflex MMR testing is recommended on the grounds that prevalence is 'comparable to that of colorectal cancer and is also independent on the subtype', but the supporting evidence is graded low and the two papers in this depot give prevalences of 15% in unselected non-medullary ampullary carcinoma and 4.3% in early-onset ampullary cancer - neither of which is clearly comparable to colorectal, and neither of which is cited as a prevalence estimate in the recommendation","Tumour budding is recommended as prognostically stronger than T stage and nodal metastasis, a strong empirical claim resting largely on work from the same institutional tradition that produced the ampullary classifications, with no multi-institutional validation, no reproducibility data for the 3-foci-per-200x-field threshold, and the acknowledged problem that biopsies may not contain the invasive front where budding must be assessed","229 of 37061 screened articles (0.6%) were selected, with allocation of articles to anonymous expert teams but no stated inclusion criteria, no risk-of-bias appraisal of the 229, no PRISMA flow diagram in the main text and no evidence tables - so the SIGN framework is invoked without the apparatus that makes it auditable","The anatomic definitions, which are the document's most valuable contribution, are operationalised in terms of tumour 'epicentre' and 'minimal involvement' without quantitative thresholds except in the earlier Adsay scheme they derive from; given that this literature's own data show that 21% of cases labelled ampullary are reclassified on strict review, the definitions need a reproducibility study more than they need wider adoption","The panel is heavily weighted towards pathology (initiated by ISGACA with ISGPP as steering committee), and the multidisciplinary part generated only 17 of 51 recommendations; the oncological questions that clinicians most need settled - whether subtype should guide adjuvant therapy, what to do with a T1 cancer after papillectomy - are declared unresolved rather than addressed","The consensus correctly identifies that inconsistent definitions have made the adjuvant chemotherapy literature uninterpretable, which is the strongest argument in this depot against acting on the Bolm-versus-Ecker dispute; but it stops at saying standardised future studies are needed and offers no interim guidance"],"bottom_line":"The first international consensus to define precisely what counts as ampullary carcinoma, to retire the term 'periampullary' as a diagnosis, to set a 30% threshold for the mixed subtype and rename the hybrid group 'tubular-NOS', to make mismatch repair testing reflex, and to state explicitly that the prognostic and predictive value of intestinal-versus-pancreatobiliary subtype remains unclear because the historical literature used inconsistent definitions - which is the key caveat for any pathway claiming subtype should guide adjuvant therapy; but almost every recommendation is low-evidence or expert opinion, the promised AGREE II quality score and audience vote are never reported, and no reproducibility study accompanies the new definitions.","funding":"Amsterdam Gastroenterology Endocrinology Metabolism (AGEM), Amsterdam, The Netherlands; the authors declare no conflicts of interest"},"41192607":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design over a 10-year period across 22 institutions, which may introduce missing data and selection bias","Treatment strategies - papillectomy technique, surveillance intervals and argon plasma coagulation use - varied by institution and over time because standardised guidelines were not consistently available; the authors stratified analysis by treatment period to address this","Only high-volume centres with expert teams were included, limiting generalisability","R0 margin status was assessed locally at each institution rather than centrally, which may introduce variability, although recurrence rates after R0 were comparable to other large studies","T1a and T1b adenocarcinomas were not differentiated, so prognosis by tumour stage could not be examined"],"critique":["The hazard ratios differ between the abstract/discussion and Table 2 for the same comparisons (Rx 2.30 [1.44-3.68] versus 2.38 [1.49-3.81]; R1 2.95 [1.85-4.71] versus 2.95 [1.87-4.66]). The discrepancy is small but it means two different models or datasets were in play and neither is identified","The central finding - recurrence after R0 - is partly a definitional artefact of Japanese pathological practice, which the paper itself flags: non-invasive intraepithelial neoplasia is diagnosed as carcinoma in Japan but as high-grade dysplasia in the West, so 'adenocarcinoma' in the 92 cases here is not equivalent to adenocarcinoma in the Western series alongside it, and the adenocarcinoma hazard ratio cannot be transferred","Recurrence is defined as histologic confirmation of neoplastic tissue with no requirement for a prior negative surveillance endoscopy, and the median time to recurrence was 6 months (3 months after R1). That makes a large fraction of 'recurrences' residual disease, as the pattern by margin status shows - which is consistent but means the 18.3% figure is not comparable with series that excluded residual disease, including Han 2024 in this same depot","The later treatment era (2015-2020) independently predicted recurrence (HR 1.57), which the authors attribute to more procedures by operators with fewer than 20 prior cases (26.4% rising to 44.0%). Since operator experience was not itself significant, this is an unexplained period effect that could equally reflect intensified surveillance in later years - a detection artefact that would inflate the headline recurrence rate","Margin assessment was local across 22 centres with no central pathology review and no interobserver data, yet R0/R1/Rx is the paper's principal exposure; a quarter of the cohort was Rx precisely because margins could not be read, and Rx behaved almost identically to R1 at 5 years (34% each), suggesting Rx is largely undetected R1","The R0 subgroup analysis generates the paper's most quotable new risk factors from very few events, with wildly unstable estimates: argon plasma coagulation HR 6.26 (1.44-27.1) rests on 69 of 396 R0 patients having received APC, and bile duct invasion HR 4.86 (1.08-21.8) on a handful of cases. The authors correctly reinterpret APC as a marker of endoscopically suspected residual disease rather than a cause, but the abstract-level framing does not carry that caveat","The pancreatic duct invasion estimate is reported as 0.00 (0.00-infinity) - a non-estimate from a zero cell - and is then used to argue that bile duct but not pancreatic duct invasion matters, an inference the data cannot support","Patients censored at 5 years and 21 patients removed for post-papillectomy surgery for residual cancer are exactly the group at highest risk of a bad outcome; removing them from the recurrence denominator while keeping them in the 798-patient resection-status analysis means the two headline numbers (52.1% R0, 18.3% recurrence) have different populations behind them","Female sex emerged as an independent predictor in both models (HR 1.48 and 2.09) with no mechanism offered beyond one prior report; in a model with 13 covariates and 142 events this is as likely to be noise or a proxy for an unmeasured anatomical variable","Follow-up protocols 'varied by center and clinical context' with only a typical interval of 6-12 months stated, so recurrence ascertainment is non-uniform across 22 centres and 12 years - the single most important determinant of a cumulative recurrence estimate is left undocumented","The 32.5% adverse event rate with 19.4% bleeding is substantially higher than most Western series and reflects a Japanese practice of inpatient papillectomy with a 13-day median stay; the paper does not discuss whether this reflects more complete ascertainment or a different complication profile, which matters for anyone comparing the two approaches","Several authors declare lecture fees and research support from endoscope and device manufacturers, and the study was run with the national endoscopy society's guideline committee, in a paper whose conclusions support continued endoscopic surveillance and a redefinition of R0"],"n":"875 cases enrolled, 798 with pathologically confirmed ampullary adenoma or adenocarcinoma, 776 in the long-term recurrence analysis (21 excluded for surgery for confirmed or suspected residual adenocarcinoma, 1 for procedure-related death); median age 67 years, 320 women (40.1%), 53 with genetically confirmed FAP (6.6%); median follow-up 33 months (IQR 6.75-60)","bottom_line":"The largest papillectomy cohort to date (798 patients, 22 Japanese centres) shows that histologic R0 is achieved in only half of cases even when en bloc resection looks technically successful, and that recurrence reaches 20% at 3 years overall and still 11% after R0 - so surveillance is needed regardless of margin status; but recurrence here includes early residual disease, the adenocarcinoma category follows Japanese rather than Western criteria, and the R0-subgroup risk factors come from too few events to act on.","funding":"Not stated; study registered UMIN000040288 and approved by the Keio University Hospital ethics committee. Multiple author financial relationships declared, including lecture fees and research support from Boston Scientific Japan, Fujifilm, Olympus Marketing, Gadelius Medical and others."}}
files.new: {"16111953":{"kind":"RCT","limitations":["The authors state only that the findings 'suggest' a protective effect and that future large-scale studies are required to confirm the benefit","They note there are no data on how long the duct should be stented"],"critique":["Nineteen patients and three events cannot establish an effect. The nominally significant p = 0.02 comes from a 3-versus-0 comparison, and the intention-to-treat analysis the authors themselves perform is frankly negative (p = 0.3) - a result that should have been the headline rather than a mid-paper aside","Stopping early at an interim look triggered by a high event rate in the control arm is the classic route to an overestimated treatment effect; no alpha adjustment is applied, and the trial has roughly a fifth of its planned sample","The three analyses presented (per protocol excluding the failed placement, as-treated, intention-to-treat) give p = 0.05, 0.02 and 0.3 from 19 patients; reporting the most favourable as the result is selective","Single endoscopist, single centre, single operator technique - specifically en bloc snare without a submucosal cushion so as to include the sphincteric musculature - which the authors argue reduces later cannulation-related pancreatitis. The exclusion analysis compares only age, sex, comorbidities and lesion size - not stage, margin or outcome - so it cannot rule out that outcome-related data were differentially missing","The R0 definition is applied to specimens handled by local pathologists at 58 centres over 14 years with no central review, no interobserver assessment and no standard protocol; given that the adjacent literature shows 26% of en bloc papillectomy specimens cannot even be margin-assessed, R0 is being compared between a fragmented endoscopic specimen and an intact surgical one, which structurally favours surgery independent of oncological completeness","Attributing additional ablation at the index procedure to presumed visible residual tissue and therefore reclassifying it as R2 is a reasonable assumption, but it is an assumption made retrospectively by the authors; the 65.9% figure that results is then used as the real papillectomy success rate, and both 80.2% and 65.9% appear in the paper without a single preferred estimate","T1a and T1b cancers are pooled in most analyses despite the authors noting these carry significantly different nodal metastasis risk, and the 13 T1b patients treated endoscopically are precisely the group in whom local resection is most questionable","The matched-cohort severe complication counts are 1 versus 2 events, yet the paper concludes 'both procedures were safe'; with these numbers a two- or threefold difference in serious morbidity would be undetectable","Overall survival is reported as comparable in a study the authors concede was not designed to analyse survival, with median follow-up 21 months in a disease whose resected median survival exceeds 4 years - the survival curves carry essentially no information and should not be used to support equivalence","Procedures spanning 2007-2020 include the pre-ESGE-guideline era, submucosal injection in a quarter of matched endoscopic cases, and the introduction of endobiliary radiofrequency ablation; no era stratification is performed despite technique having changed materially"],"n":"From 2862 patients in the ESAP database (1189 pancreatoduodenectomies excluded first), 1673 remained (1422 papillectomy, 251 surgical ampullectomy); after exclusions 569 papillectomy (40.0% of database papillectomies) and 63 surgical ampullectomy (25.1%) were analysed, with 62 matched pairs; median follow-up 21 months (IQR 10-47)","bottom_line":"The largest comparison of endoscopic papillectomy with transduodenal surgical ampullectomy shows that a third of procedures in both arms were done for the wrong indication (non-neoplastic histology or advanced cancer), that surgery achieves higher initial R0 (90% vs 73%) with far lower recurrence after R0 (3.2% vs 16%) but at 7 times the procedure time and 11 extra hospital days, and that papillectomy fails in two-thirds of T1 cancers; but the matched analysis pairs the entire surgical population with a 1-in-9 selection of endoscopic patients, follow-up was twice as long in the surgical arm, and surveillance intensity differed, so the recurrence gap is inflated by design.","funding":"The authors have not declared a specific grant for this research from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors. Multiple author disclosures including honoraria from FUJIFILM and Falk Foundation and institutional consultancies with Boston Scientific, Cook Medical and Pentax Medical. Ethics approval from the University of Leipzig (455/18-ek)."},"39831703":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective multi-institutional data with the usual biases; overall statistical power remained low because of disease rarity despite multiple centres","The small sample prevented splitting into derivation and validation cohorts, so the proposed score has not undergone formal validation","Ampullary lesions were not separated from duodenal lesions involving the periampullary region, although no outcome difference was found between them","Not every patient was tested genetically for FAP, MUTYH-associated polyposis or other mutations, though all underwent colonoscopy and family history assessment","Sampling bias is acknowledged because the cohort consists only of non-FAP periampullary adenomas that went on to pancreatoduodenectomy; the high malignancy rate reflects selection of high-risk cases by tumour size and location, and the true denominator - including patients managed by endoscopic mucosal resection or transduodenal resection - is unclear","A prospective study to identify the true denominator may not be feasible given the low incidence"],"critique":["The three risk strata are reported with mutually inconsistent numbers: the abstract gives low risk n = 26, intermediate n = 59, high n = 26 with rates 10.3%, 44.1% and 88.2%; the results text gives 11.5%, 41.7% and 84.6%; Table 4 gives 3/29, 26/59 and 30/34. Three different sets of denominators for the paper's central output means the score's calibration cannot be verified from the published data","The score was derived and evaluated in the same 127 patients with no split-sample, bootstrap or cross-validation, no c-statistic, no calibration plot and no sensitivity or specificity at any threshold. An OR of 77.5 for the high-risk group (CI 15.9-375.9) is the signature of an in-sample fit, and the paper's own concession that validation was impossible should preclude clinical use","The denominator problem the authors acknowledge is fatal to the score's intended purpose: everyone in the cohort had a Whipple, so the score is calibrated on the subset already judged to need resection. A patient weighing resection against endoscopic surveillance is by definition outside this population, and applying a 46% baseline malignancy rate to them would badly overestimate risk - exactly the misuse the shared-decision framing invites","Two of the four score components are proxies for obstruction, not for neoplastic progression: 'any preoperative symptom' (worth 2 points) is a list including fatigue, nausea and dark urine, and common bile duct dilation of 9 mm or more. Jaundice and biliary stenting were dropped from the model as redundant with symptoms, which concedes the point - the score largely measures whether the lesion is obstructing, and the discussant at the meeting objected that a jaundiced patient with no other factor scores only 1-2","The inverse complication relationship is presented as a feature of the score but has a simpler explanation the paper does not address: patients with benign pathology had soft, non-atrophic glands and non-dilated ducts because they had no obstructing cancer, and fistula risk follows gland texture and duct size. Adjusting for duct size and texture in the final model does not remove this, because the same obstruction physiology that lowers fistula risk is what the score is detecting","The complication finding only becomes significant after the three prespecified strata are collapsed at score 3 - across the strata as defined it was non-significant (p = 0.11) with the intermediate and high groups indistinguishable (27.1% vs 29.4%). Choosing the dichotomy that yields p = 0.047 after the three-group comparison failed is a post hoc cut-point","Preoperative dysplasia grade carries 2 of the 6 points but was read by local pathologists at 8 centres over 12 years, with no central review and no interobserver data - and the invited discussants specifically questioned whether a pathologist seeing roughly one such case per year can reliably separate high- from low-grade dysplasia","Volume was extremely low: 127 patients across 8 institutions over 12 years, about 1.3 cases per centre per year, so biopsy technique, number of biopsies, prior attempted endoscopic resection and pathology interpretation almost certainly varied in ways that cannot be modelled - a point the discussants raised and the authors do not rebut with data","EUS findings are absent from the entire paper despite both discussants noting that these are major centres where EUS would be routine; omitting the modality that best assesses intraductal extension and depth from a preoperative risk score is a substantial gap, and no explanation is given","Lesion size was missing for 27 of 127 patients (21%) and was then excluded from the score on the grounds that it did not differ between groups - a conclusion drawn from data with a fifth missing and no imputation","Black race was associated with benign final pathology (26.5% vs 11.9%) and with a different risk profile, in a cohort where race also tracked with symptoms and stenting; no analysis addresses whether differential access to earlier endoscopic diagnosis is embedded in the score's components","The 46.4% malignancy rate is compared with the same group's earlier single-centre figure of 29%, with no explanation for the difference other than cohort composition - which again points to the selection the score cannot escape"],"n":"127 patients of 189 reviewed; median age 65 years (34-89), 57 men (44.9%); 82 (64.6%) preoperative duodenal adenoma and 45 (35.4%) ampullary adenoma, with ampullary involvement in 84 of 119 (70.6%); 59 (46.4%) had malignancy on final pathology","bottom_line":"Confirms in the largest surgical series that nearly half of sporadic periampullary adenomas taken to pancreatoduodenectomy harbour cancer and that patients with benign final pathology paradoxically suffer threefold more major complications, and proposes a 0-6 malignancy risk score from age, bile duct diameter, symptoms and high-grade dysplasia; but the score is derived and tested in the same 127 already-resected patients with no validation, its published strata carry three inconsistent sets of numbers, and two of its four components are proxies for biliary obstruction.","funding":"National Cancer Institute of the NIH award K12 CA237806 (Emory K12 Clinical Oncology Training Program, Dr Shah); Contardi Research Fellowship; Georgia Clinical and Translational Science Awards UL1 TR002378. Nothing to disclose for the study; disclosures outside its scope include grant funding from Cantargia AB and consultancies with Intera Oncology, Stryker Medical and Intuitive Surgical."},"40729532":{"kind":"consensus","limitations":["The Delphi methodology, while the best option for reaching consensus, carries the difficulty of capturing all key issues in the literature during questionnaire development, depends on panellists' ongoing willingness to participate, and risks skewed data because those less confident about a topic may not participate","Although the stated aim was to cover all non-pancreatic cancers of the periampullary region, more recommendations relate to ampullary cancer than to common bile duct or duodenal cancer; the authors accept this imbalance as reflecting greater uncertainty and need for guidance about ampullary cancer","For a considerable proportion of the consensus questions there are fairly limited published data, so most recommendations are supported only by a low level of evidence, which the authors say highlights the early stage of knowledge about periampullary cancer","The authors state that the lack of consensus definitions and standardisation, together with high interobserver variability, has hindered consistent conclusions across studies - particularly regarding patient management including the efficacy of adjuvant chemotherapy, which remains highly controversial because of these inconsistencies"],"critique":["Almost every recommendation is graded low level of evidence with a weak form of recommendation, or rests on expert opinion alone. This is honest, but it means a document that will be used to standardise reporting worldwide is in substance a codification of the opinions of 43 experts, most of them from the pathology study groups that initiated it","THE PROCESS METRICS PROMISED ARE NOT REPORTED. The methods describe an independent Jury Committee calculating a 'Quality Score' using the AGREE II tool across 23 items and six domains, and an audience vote on each recommendation at the Brescia meeting. Neither result appears anywhere in the paper - no AGREE II score, no domain breakdown, no audience agreement percentages. The quality-assurance apparatus is described but its findings are withheld","The Delphi convergence is itself a weak signal: 33 of 57 recommendations reached 80% agreement in round one and the rest were revised by the responsible expert team according to the dissenting comments and re-voted until they passed. Revising a statement until it achieves consensus guarantees consensus; the final 50 of 51 figure measures iteration, not agreement on the original propositions","The 30% threshold for calling a tumour 'mixed' subtype has no stated derivation. It is a cut-point that will determine subtype assignment in a large fraction of cases - and the consensus itself cites that about 40% of ampullary carcinomas are mixed - yet no data, reproducibility study or sensitivity analysis is offered for choosing 30% over 10% or 50%","Renaming the hybrid category 'tubular-NOS' is a nomenclature change, not a solution. The underlying problem documented in this depot - that five pathologists agree on morphological subtype at kappa 0.39 with full agreement in 23% of cases - is unaddressed: no interobserver reproducibility study of the new definitions is reported or planned, so the consensus standardises the words without demonstrating that the categories can be applied consistently","The consensus states plainly that the prognostic and predictive role of subtype is unclear because of inconsistent historical definitions, yet it simultaneously retains subtyping as a required element of the pathology report and advises subtyping on biopsy where subtype 'may affect treatment'. If subtype has no established treatment implication, there is no situation in which that condition is met","Reflex MMR testing is recommended on the grounds that prevalence is 'comparable to that of colorectal cancer and is also independent on the subtype', but the supporting evidence is graded low and the two papers in this depot give prevalences of 15% in unselected non-medullary ampullary carcinoma and 4.3% in early-onset ampullary cancer - neither of which is clearly comparable to colorectal, and neither of which is cited as a prevalence estimate in the recommendation","Tumour budding is recommended as prognostically stronger than T stage and nodal metastasis, a strong empirical claim resting largely on work from the same institutional tradition that produced the ampullary classifications, with no multi-institutional validation, no reproducibility data for the 3-foci-per-200x-field threshold, and the acknowledged problem that biopsies may not contain the invasive front where budding must be assessed","229 of 37061 screened articles (0.6%) were selected, with allocation of articles to anonymous expert teams but no stated inclusion criteria, no risk-of-bias appraisal of the 229, no PRISMA flow diagram in the main text and no evidence tables - so the SIGN framework is invoked without the apparatus that makes it auditable","The anatomic definitions, which are the document's most valuable contribution, are operationalised in terms of tumour 'epicentre' and 'minimal involvement' without quantitative thresholds except in the earlier Adsay scheme they derive from; given that this literature's own data show that 21% of cases labelled ampullary are reclassified on strict review, the definitions need a reproducibility study more than they need wider adoption","The panel is heavily weighted towards pathology (initiated by ISGACA with ISGPP as steering committee), and the multidisciplinary part generated only 17 of 51 recommendations; the oncological questions that clinicians most need settled - whether subtype should guide adjuvant therapy, what to do with a T1 cancer after papillectomy - are declared unresolved rather than addressed","The consensus correctly identifies that inconsistent definitions have made the adjuvant chemotherapy literature uninterpretable, which is the strongest argument in this depot against acting on the Bolm-versus-Ecker dispute; but it stops at saying standardised future studies are needed and offers no interim guidance"],"bottom_line":"The first international consensus to define precisely what counts as ampullary carcinoma, to retire the term 'periampullary' as a diagnosis, to set a 30% threshold for the mixed subtype and rename the hybrid group 'tubular-NOS', to make mismatch repair testing reflex, and to state explicitly that the prognostic and predictive value of intestinal-versus-pancreatobiliary subtype remains unclear because the historical literature used inconsistent definitions - which is the key caveat for any pathway claiming subtype should guide adjuvant therapy; but almost every recommendation is low-evidence or expert opinion, the promised AGREE II quality score and audience vote are never reported, and no reproducibility study accompanies the new definitions.","funding":"Amsterdam Gastroenterology Endocrinology Metabolism (AGEM), Amsterdam, The Netherlands; the authors declare no conflicts of interest"},"41192607":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design over a 10-year period across 22 institutions, which may introduce missing data and selection bias","Treatment strategies - papillectomy technique, surveillance intervals and argon plasma coagulation use - varied by institution and over time because standardised guidelines were not consistently available; the authors stratified analysis by treatment period to address this","Only high-volume centres with expert teams were included, limiting generalisability","R0 margin status was assessed locally at each institution rather than centrally, which may introduce variability, although recurrence rates after R0 were comparable to other large studies","T1a and T1b adenocarcinomas were not differentiated, so prognosis by tumour stage could not be examined"],"critique":["The hazard ratios differ between the abstract/discussion and Table 2 for the same comparisons (Rx 2.30 [1.44-3.68] versus 2.38 [1.49-3.81]; R1 2.95 [1.85-4.71] versus 2.95 [1.87-4.66]). The discrepancy is small but it means two different models or datasets were in play and neither is identified","The central finding - recurrence after R0 - is partly a definitional artefact of Japanese pathological practice, which the paper itself flags: non-invasive intraepithelial neoplasia is diagnosed as carcinoma in Japan but as high-grade dysplasia in the West, so 'adenocarcinoma' in the 92 cases here is not equivalent to adenocarcinoma in the Western series alongside it, and the adenocarcinoma hazard ratio cannot be transferred","Recurrence is defined as histologic confirmation of neoplastic tissue with no requirement for a prior negative surveillance endoscopy, and the median time to recurrence was 6 months (3 months after R1). That makes a large fraction of 'recurrences' residual disease, as the pattern by margin status shows - which is consistent but means the 18.3% figure is not comparable with series that excluded residual disease, including Han 2024 in this same depot","The later treatment era (2015-2020) independently predicted recurrence (HR 1.57), which the authors attribute to more procedures by operators with fewer than 20 prior cases (26.4% rising to 44.0%). Since operator experience was not itself significant, this is an unexplained period effect that could equally reflect intensified surveillance in later years - a detection artefact that would inflate the headline recurrence rate","Margin assessment was local across 22 centres with no central pathology review and no interobserver data, yet R0/R1/Rx is the paper's principal exposure; a quarter of the cohort was Rx precisely because margins could not be read, and Rx behaved almost identically to R1 at 5 years (34% each), suggesting Rx is largely undetected R1","The R0 subgroup analysis generates the paper's most quotable new risk factors from very few events, with wildly unstable estimates: argon plasma coagulation HR 6.26 (1.44-27.1) rests on 69 of 396 R0 patients having received APC, and bile duct invasion HR 4.86 (1.08-21.8) on a handful of cases. The authors correctly reinterpret APC as a marker of endoscopically suspected residual disease rather than a cause, but the abstract-level framing does not carry that caveat","The pancreatic duct invasion estimate is reported as 0.00 (0.00-infinity) - a non-estimate from a zero cell - and is then used to argue that bile duct but not pancreatic duct invasion matters, an inference the data cannot support","Patients censored at 5 years and 21 patients removed for post-papillectomy surgery for residual cancer are exactly the group at highest risk of a bad outcome; removing them from the recurrence denominator while keeping them in the 798-patient resection-status analysis means the two headline numbers (52.1% R0, 18.3% recurrence) have different populations behind them","Female sex emerged as an independent predictor in both models (HR 1.48 and 2.09) with no mechanism offered beyond one prior report; in a model with 13 covariates and 142 events this is as likely to be noise or a proxy for an unmeasured anatomical variable","Follow-up protocols 'varied by center and clinical context' with only a typical interval of 6-12 months stated, so recurrence ascertainment is non-uniform across 22 centres and 12 years - the single most important determinant of a cumulative recurrence estimate is left undocumented","The 32.5% adverse event rate with 19.4% bleeding is substantially higher than most Western series and reflects a Japanese practice of inpatient papillectomy with a 13-day median stay; the paper does not discuss whether this reflects more complete ascertainment or a different complication profile, which matters for anyone comparing the two approaches","Several authors declare lecture fees and research support from endoscope and device manufacturers, and the study was run with the national endoscopy society's guideline committee, in a paper whose conclusions support continued endoscopic surveillance and a redefinition of R0"],"n":"875 cases enrolled, 798 with pathologically confirmed ampullary adenoma or adenocarcinoma, 776 in the long-term recurrence analysis (21 excluded for surgery for confirmed or suspected residual adenocarcinoma, 1 for procedure-related death); median age 67 years, 320 women (40.1%), 53 with genetically confirmed FAP (6.6%); median follow-up 33 months (IQR 6.75-60)","bottom_line":"The largest papillectomy cohort to date (798 patients, 22 Japanese centres) shows that histologic R0 is achieved in only half of cases even when en bloc resection looks technically successful, and that recurrence reaches 20% at 3 years overall and still 11% after R0 - so surveillance is needed regardless of margin status; but recurrence here includes early residual disease, the adenocarcinoma category follows Japanese rather than Western criteria, and the R0-subgroup risk factors come from too few events to act on.","funding":"Not stated; study registered UMIN000040288 and approved by the Keio University Hospital ethics committee. Multiple author financial relationships declared, including lecture fees and research support from Boston Scientific Japan, Fujifilm, Olympus Marketing, Gadelius Medical and others."}}

   "rationale": "EASL reserves embolisation for poor surgical candidates. "divergence": "NANETS and the MEN1 recommendations do not require tissue while ENETS 2023 asks for it under 2 cm, no outcome evidence separates them, and cytology under-grades while observation without tissue leaves grade unknown.",
     "proposal": "Biopsy is not obligatory to observe a sub-centimetre lesion with a characteristic phenotype when surveillance is planned whatever the grade (Reasonable, grade D); obtain tissue when the diagnosis is in doubt, grade would change the plan, or a 1–2 cm observe-or-resect decision is live, treating needle grade as a floor. One programme answer is pending.",
     "proposal_locator": "Gate 1 · Reasonable 'Biopsy is not obligatory…' · pref and caveat; Gate 1 · Standard 'Treat a grade obtained from a needle biopsy as a floor…'; What we are not sure about #14",
     "rationale": "NANETS says biopsy is not routinely necessary before deciding to observe a sub-centimetre lesion with a characteristic imaging phenotype. ENETS 2023, read in full, says a suspected nonfunctioning tumour under 2 cm with positive receptor imaging should be confirmed histologically or cytologically where possible (level 3, grade B). The 2025 MEN1 recommendations find no role for routine EUS-guided biopsy in that syndrome. There is no outcome evidence separating the three, and both options carry a real cost: EUS-FNA cytology called 71% of histological G2 tumours G1, while two thirds of ASPEN's surveillance arm had no evaluable histology at all. The programme needs one answer, and a stated reason.",
     "audit": "Registry: for every observed lesion, whether tissue was obtained, by what route, the cytological grade where available, and the resection grade in every patient who later crossed over.",

    },

     "proposal": "Define growth before using it and compute it only against a recorded baseline on the same modality. The draft uses Kyoto's 2.5 mm a year as the spine's worrisome feature while labelling it a frequency-chosen consensus value, and argues that duct diameter growth should be recorded under a consistent protocol; adoption is left to the programme.",
     "proposal_locator": "Gate 3 · Standard 'Define growth rate before using it…'; Gate 1 · Avoid 'Do not enter a cyst into surveillance without a baseline…'; Gate 8 · Standard 'Use MRI with MRCP…'; Practice choices with limited evidence · item 5",
     "rationale": "There are four definitions, not three: Kyoto 2.5 mm per year, ACG more than 3 mm per year, Fukuoka 2017 5 mm over 2 years, the European guideline 5 mm per year. Kyoto adopted 2.5 because it was the value most frequently reported among candidates spanning 0.96 to 3.5 mm per year, which is a choice by vote frequency rather than performance. None has published measurement reproducibility and 2.5 mm is inside the range over which two readers can disagree. files.old: {"16432361":{"kind":"registry","limitations":["There is wide overlap in tumour size between patients who had curative surgery and those who did not - one patient with an 8 mm tumour was resected while a patient with a 30 mm tumour and no metastasis was not - so the two groups are probably not comparable","Follow-up duration differed between the groups and patients were not randomly assigned to conservative or aggressive treatment","Classification of surgery as curative or non-curative was made retrospectively from intraoperative findings rather than on an intention-to-treat basis, which probably overestimates survival after curative surgery","The actual metastasis rate may be underestimated because only 40% had an operation and 60% of metastases were identified by imaging alone; CT has low sensitivity for small pancreatic tumours and metastases in MEN1, and a cited study found 26% of patients with radiographically demonstrated lesions had preoperatively unidentified metastases at operation","Because follow-up after diagnosis was relatively short, the rate of growth could not be predicted and the rate at which tumours migrate from one size group to another could not be evaluated"],"critique":["The 20 mm threshold the paper recommends is inferred from a metastasis gradient whose lowest two strata are 1 of 25 and 4 of 40 patients - rates whose confidence intervals overlap entirely - and the authors themselves report that survival in the 11-30 mm band was only slightly and non-significantly worse than at 10 mm or less, so the data support 'larger is worse' but not the specific cut point that subsequently entered international guidelines","The cohort spans 1956 to 2003 with prospective registration only from 1997, and the authors use the post-1997 subset for penetrance while using the whole cohort for metastasis and survival, so the two central estimates come from different populations imaged with different technology","Metastasis was imaging-defined in 60% of cases, and the authors cite evidence that a quarter of radiographically node-negative MEN1 patients have occult metastases at operation - which means the risk being weighed against the morbidity of surgery is systematically understated in the same analysis that recommends against surgery","Mean follow-up after diagnosis is 4.3 years in a disease whose victims die at a mean age of 43, so most of the hazard being adjudicated lies beyond the observation window; the 8-year survival estimates in the metastatic group have confidence intervals from 6% to 62%","The mortality argument is partly circular: life expectancy with a nonfunctioning tumour is compared against MEN1 patients without any pancreatic tumour, who differ systematically in age at diagnosis, screening intensity and era, and who by definition lack the lesion that defines the comparison","In MEN1 the pancreas carries a field defect with a mean of 2.9 tumours per patient, so a size threshold applied to the largest lesion ignores the remaining disease, and the authors' own data show 2 of 32 curatively resected patients needed reoperation for new tumours within 6 years","Thirty-two curatively operated patients and 66 unoperated patients with non-significant differences in metastasis, progression and death is an underpowered null, not evidence of equivalence; no power calculation or equivalence margin is offered"],"n":"108 MEN1 patients with isolated nonfunctioning pancreatic tumours, drawn from 579 registered MEN1 patients","bottom_line":"In the largest population-based MEN1 series, nonfunctioning pancreatic tumours are the commonest pancreaticoduodenal lesion, reach 34% penetrance by age 50 and shorten life expectancy by about nine years, with metastasis rising from 4% below 10 mm to 43% above 30 mm - the basis for not operating below 20 mm, although that specific threshold rests on single-digit event counts, imaging-defined metastasis and 4 years of follow-up.","funding":"Supported in part by a grant from the University Hospital of Geneva, Switzerland, to F. Triponez."},"16926567":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["The study is not randomised; this is the authors' stated principal limitation","The 35 non-surgical patients did not have surgery for a mixture of reasons - refusal after discussion with the referring physician in 55%, concurrent illness, inability to consent, and the MEN1 size rule","The authors defend comparability by showing no significant difference in any clinical, laboratory or imaging parameter, including the factors previously shown to predict aggressive disease (sex, MEN1 status, disease duration, fasting gastrin, imaging results), and no difference in follow-up duration"],"critique":["This is a gastrinoma study and almost all primaries were duodenal or nodal; it bears on functioning duodenopancreatic NET and not at all on incidental non-functioning pancreatic NET, yet it is the usual citation for the proposition that surgery prolongs survival in pancreatic NET","Thirty-five controls, of whom 10 were excluded from surgery by the MEN1 size rule and 5 by comorbidity, cannot be assumed exchangeable with 160 operated patients however many baseline variables match; refusing surgery after consulting one's own doctor is itself a marker of health behaviour, health literacy and access","Disease-related death in the surgical arm is 2 events, so the 23-fold difference and the 98% figure rest on single digits with no confidence interval reported for the ratio","Non-disease-related mortality was numerically higher in the controls (31% vs 20%), which is the expected signature of a sicker comparison group and undercuts the claim that the arms differed only in disease-specific risk; this is reported as non-significant rather than interpreted","Cause of death was adjudicated by the treating and operating investigators without blinding, in a study whose central endpoint is cause-specific","Controls were imaged every 6-12 months whereas operated patients were evaluated yearly, and controls less often had functional localisation studies, so ascertainment of liver metastases differed by arm in both direction and intensity","Accrual spans 1980 to the mid-2000s across three institutions while the operation itself changed mid-study - routine duodenotomy and intraoperative endoscopic transillumination from 1987, somatostatin receptor scintigraphy from 1994 - and all 10 patients in whom no tumour was found were operated before duodenotomy, so the arms are not method-contemporaneous","With 20-31% non-disease mortality over two decades, competing risk is substantial and no competing-risk analysis was performed; Kaplan-Meier censoring inflates the disease-specific separation"],"n":"195 ZES patients: 160 who underwent surgical exploration and 35 who did not","bottom_line":"Over a mean 12 years of follow-up, routine exploration for gastrinoma was associated with far fewer liver metastases and a 15-year disease-related survival of 98% versus 74% without surgery, but the comparison is non-randomised with 35 self-selected controls, 2 disease-related deaths in the surgical arm, and no bearing on non-functioning pancreatic NET."},"18063061":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["The pathology was not reviewed for this study, so Ki-67 or proliferative staining was not examined and could not be related to doubling time","Chromogranin A and other biomarkers were not examined and no marker data correlate with metastatic disease","Cut-offs of 1 cm and 2 cm were not analysed; only the 3 cm threshold carried over from the group's earlier work was tested","Some non-operated lesions diagnosed on radiographic criteria could on pathology turn out to be microcystic adenomas, although the authors state they do not look classic for that on imaging","The ultimate impact of this management approach on metastatic risk will only be known as the patients continue to be followed"],"critique":["The three-criterion algorithm is derived from 9 metastatic events and then declared to capture all 9, so its perfect sensitivity is a tautology of the derivation rather than a finding, and no independent or temporal validation is attempted","Doubling time, the criterion with the largest apparent separation, could be calculated in all 9 metastatic patients but only 54 of 99 non-metastatic ones; patients with visibly growing lesions are imaged more often, so the exposure and the ability to measure it are entangled, and the missing 45 patients are simply absent from the stratification table","Sixty-nine of 108 lesions were never resected and their diagnosis rests on CT or MRI appearance alone - which the senior author concedes in the floor discussion could include microcystic adenomas - so a substantial part of the denominator is unverified, and any benign lesions in it dilute the metastasis rate downward","The study dates are internally inconsistent, December 1998 in the abstract against December 1988 in the methods, an eight-fold difference in accrual window that is never reconciled","The 3 cm threshold was carried over from the group's own prior publications rather than tested against 1 or 2 cm; a discussant asked precisely this and the author replied that the analysis had not been done, so the cut point in the resulting algorithm is untested within this dataset","No Ki-67, grade or differentiation data exist anywhere in the series, which in 2007 was already the strongest known prognostic axis in pancreatic NET","VHL PNETs are always nonfunctional, often multifocal and set against competing renal and CNS disease; with 2 PNET deaths among 633 screened patients, the algorithm is calibrated against a risk that is an order of magnitude smaller than the patient's renal risk, which the authors state but which also means the algorithm's clinical value is largely unmeasurable","The exon 3 association rests on 7 of 9 metastatic patients and is a single test in a cohort where exon 3 is already the commonest mutation site (50%), with no correction for the other exons examined"],"n":"108 VHL patients with PNETs among 633 VHL patients screened; 39 resected and 9 with metastatic disease","bottom_line":"In the largest single-centre VHL series, 17% of patients had a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour and only 8.3% of those metastasised; lesion size of 3 cm or more, an exon 3 germline mutation and a doubling time under 500 days together identified every metastatic case - but the rule was derived and tested on the same 9 events, doubling time was measurable in only half the non-metastatic patients, and two thirds of lesions were never histologically confirmed."},"18376195":{"kind":"registry","limitations":["Functionality of islet cell tumours is not explicitly recorded in cancer registries, so functional status is probably under-reported; the authors note the functional versus nonfunctional survival difference would likely widen if all benign functional tumours were reported","US cancer registries collect data only on malignant pancreatic tumours; some hospitals in some periods were reporting tumours with benign behaviour and these were excluded for lack of uniformity","Tumour grade is substantially underreported for PNET (56.5% complete, versus 22.8% missing for pancreatic adenocarcinoma), and widespread applicability of the score requires better grade reporting","As with all large administrative datasets there may be miscoding, missing or inaccurate data, and pathological review of all specimens was impossible","The NCDB does not record MEN-1 status, the number of tumours within the pancreas, secretory hormone levels or the specific type of systemic therapy","Survival analyses based on retrospective data should be interpreted cautiously because of potential patient selection bias, particularly for surgery and adjuvant treatment, and the analysis of prognostic factors demonstrates association rather than causation","For patients who had enucleation and were reported node negative, nodal status was recoded as missing unless the number of nodes examined was explicitly reported"],"critique":["The result most often lifted from this paper - that tumour size does not predict survival after resection - comes from a cohort in which only 19% of tumours were 2 cm or less and from which the registry had already removed every lesion a pathologist called benign, so the small-tumour end of the distribution is both thin and skewed toward the aggressive; the paper cannot be used to argue that size is irrelevant to the decision whether to resect a 1 cm incidental lesion","The score is derived and evaluated in the same 836 patients, with bootstrapping for optimism but no external or temporal validation, and a concordance index of 0.63 is barely above the 0.5 of chance; the authors defend it by comparison with a pancreatic adenocarcinoma staging system rather than against any threshold of clinical usefulness","Grade was missing in 43.5% of the cohort and nodal status was deliberately recoded as missing for enucleation patients, so the two variables that carry most of the score's discrimination are the two most incompletely recorded - and the 836-patient complete-case subset is by construction the best-documented 22% of the cohort","Pancreaticoduodenectomy emerging as an independent adverse predictor is far more plausibly perioperative mortality and tumour location than any effect of the operation, which the authors concede in the discussion while retaining it in the model and in the abstract's list of predictors","The cohort spans 1985-2004, during which WHO grading was introduced (2000) and 'neuroendocrine carcinoma' absorbed 'islet cell tumour' in registry reporting, so the exposure definitions shift within the study period","Disease-specific survival is unavailable, so relative survival adjusted for age, sex and race stands in for it; in a disease with a median age of 56 and 10-year survival of 38%, that substitution does substantial work and is not validated here","Only 1464 of 3851 patients had tumours over 4 cm recorded and size was missing for about 22%, so the null result for size is also a null result in the presence of considerable missingness, with no sensitivity analysis"],"n":"3851 patients who underwent pancreatectomy for PNET;
