results from new clinical studies, which set new ways of proceeding","Treatment of NF-Pan-NEN still requires the decision of a multidisciplinary team of neuroendocrine neoplasm specialists, and ENETS Centres of Excellence should be strongly considered","Further studies are needed to fulfil unmet needs, focusing on prognostic molecular markers, the selection of a therapeutic approach and the sequence of treatments","Data sharing is not applicable as no new data were created or analysed","Specific uncertainties acknowledged in the text: no validated consensus on the definition of resectability; no preoperative examination accurately predicts nodal involvement; robust data on radiofrequency ablation and on minimally invasive pancreaticoduodenectomy are lacking; no evidence supports somatostatin analogues for controlling progression of small NF-Pan-NET under surveillance; the role of chemotherapy as adjuvant therapy is unknown; limited data exist on PRRT for G3"],"critique":["The two recommendations that most change practice - surveillance for lesions of 1 cm or less and surgery for everything above 2 cm - both carry level 3 evidence and grade B, yet the second is written in the imperative ('strongly recommended'), and the 1-2 cm band into which most incidental lesions fall is handed back to the clinician with no decision rule at all","The follow-up schedule and the recommendation to surveil for at least 20 years and possibly lifelong rest on level 5 evidence - expert opinion without explicit critical appraisal, by the paper's own table - while being assigned grade B, an inversion the GRADE framework the paper claims to follow would not permit","PANDORA and the ASPEN interim analysis are cited as the prospective basis for surveillance at median follow-ups of 17 and 25 months, without the document noting that both are far shorter than the 7-year median time to pancreatic recurrence and the 12-18% recurrence rate it reports elsewhere in the same text","The ASPEN principal investigator and the author of the ENETS surgical guideline being operationalised are among the authors, so the guidance grades evidence its own authors generated, and ASPEN was itself funded by ENETS","CLARINET's hazard ratio in the pancreatic subgroup crosses unity (0.58, 95% CI 0.32-1.04) and is cited in support of a grade A recommendation for upfront somatostatin analogues - a confidence interval that does not exclude no effect supporting the strongest grade available","Belzutifan's 90.9% response figure is imported from a single-arm 22-patient secondary endpoint in VHL disease and placed in a nonfunctioning sporadic pancreatic NET guideline, with the caveat about metastatic disease but not about the design","The E2211 chemotherapy recommendation is built on a PFS advantage with non-significant response and overall survival, in a trial limited to Ki-67 up to 20%, and is then extended to G3 disease on the strength of one retrospective series (evidence 3b, grade B)","There is no systematic search, no evidence table and no description of how the literature informing each question was selected, so the level-of-evidence labels cannot be audited","Eleven of the thirteen authors declare consultancy, speaker or advisory relationships with the manufacturers of the recommended agents - Ipsen, Novartis, AAA, Pfizer, MSD among them - and one holds intellectual property on 64Cu-DOTATATE, the tracer whose superior lesion detection the imaging section endorses"],"bottom_line":"The current ENETS position on nonfunctioning pancreatic NET: observe lesions of 1 cm or less, individualise 1-2 cm, operate above 2 cm or with duct dilation, stage with SSTR-PET/CT and surveil for twenty years or more - sensible, practical and widely followed, but the pivotal surgical thresholds carry level 3 evidence, the follow-up schedule carries level 5, and the prospective studies invoked have two years of follow-up."},"40523372":{"kind":"consensus","limitations":["The recommendations are limited by the varying methodological quality of available data, derived primarily from retrospective series and insufficient to provide high or moderate certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach","Only 37 of 3048 publications (1.2%) met the inclusion criteria for the systematic reviews","Confounding could have arisen in the surgery versus surveillance comparison because surgery for tumours of 2 cm or less was indicated by growth on serial imaging, so the effects of surgery may have been underestimated; given that the implications of surveillance for morbidity, metastasis and mortality are important and irreversible, a more cautious approach might be prudent","Further studies are required to validate and optimise the proposed screening protocols and to develop shared decision-making tools","A similar evidence-based and consensus-based approach is still required for adrenal tumours, which are frequently found as incidentalomas on surveillance MRI","Biomarkers are lacking for accurate risk stratification of neuroendocrine tumours, for predicting aggressive pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, for personalised risk-based management and for early detection of thymic neuroendocrine tumours","Better variant-of-uncertain-significance prediction tools and high-throughput functional assays are needed for genetic testing; prospective, well-annotated cohorts with clinical biobanks and global collaboration are needed to enable the research"],"critique":["The systematic review found no difference between surgery and surveillance for lesions of 2 cm or less, and the panel then declines to follow its own finding, writing that 'a more cautious approach might be prudent' - a defensible clinical judgement, but it means the resulting operative posture is expert preference overriding the evidence the exercise was convened to produce, and should not be cited as evidence-based","1814 patients across 37 mostly retrospective studies for an entire multi-organ syndrome means every pancreatic statement rests on very few events; the panel's own GRADE rating is low or very low throughout while the statements are worded as recommendations carrying 92-100% agreement","A Delphi percentage measures how many experts agree, not how likely they are to be right; the paper's own scale calls 51% agreement a 'consider', so the apparatus systematically converts low-certainty evidence into high-confidence prose, and the agreement figure is the only number most readers will carry away","The 1 mm per year growth criterion in statements 28 and 39 has no cited derivation and lies below the measurement reproducibility of serial MRI of a multifocal pancreas across different scanners and readers, so it will generate both false stability and false progression","Panel selection was by recognised standing within the same societies that issued the 2001 and 2012 guidelines, and several authors wrote those, so the 'new or now explicit' labels partly re-endorse the panel's own prior positions","Recommending pancreatic MRI from age 10-15 commits asymptomatic children to lifelong imaging on the strength of penetrance data alone, with no outcome evidence that earlier detection reduces mortality and no analysis of the harms - incidental adrenal findings, which the paper separately flags as a growing problem, or the psychological burden of surveillance from childhood","The screening recommendations deliberately aim to detect 'clinically relevant disease, and not necessarily the earliest onset of disease', yet the interval recommendations are set by expert vote with no modelling of what interval achieves that distinction","Nothing in this document transfers to sporadic nonfunctioning pancreatic NET: in MEN1 the gland carries a field defect, lesions are multiple, patients are decades younger, and competing parathyroid, pituitary and thymic disease dominates the risk calculus - so the MEN1 2 cm threshold and the sporadic 2 cm threshold happen to share a number but not an evidence base"],"n":"55 recommendations, comprising 52 Delphi consensus statements plus 3 from systematic reviews of 37 of 3048 publications covering 1814 patients","bottom_line":"The most rigorous MEN1 guidance yet assembled, and its most important finding for a pancreatic pathway is negative: across 37 usable studies, surgery and active surveillance for nonfunctioning pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours of 2 cm or less produced no difference in metastasis or mortality at low or very low GRADE certainty - after which the panel recommends caution anyway, on expert judgement rather than data."}}
files.new: {"16432361":{"kind":"registry","limitations":["There is wide overlap in tumour size between patients who had curative surgery and those who did not - one patient with an 8 mm tumour was resected while a patient with a 30 mm tumour and no metastasis was not - so the two groups are probably not comparable","Follow-up duration differed between the groups and patients were not randomly assigned to conservative or aggressive treatment","Classification of surgery as curative or non-curative was made retrospectively from intraoperative findings rather than on an intention-to-treat basis, which probably overestimates survival after curative surgery","The actual metastasis rate may be underestimated because only 40% had an operation and 60% of metastases were identified by imaging alone; CT has low sensitivity for small pancreatic tumours and metastases in MEN1, and a cited study found 26% of patients with radiographically demonstrated lesions had preoperatively unidentified metastases at operation","Because follow-up after diagnosis was relatively short, the rate of growth could not be predicted and the rate at which tumours migrate from one size group to another could not be evaluated"],"critique":["The 20 mm threshold the paper recommends is inferred from a metastasis gradient whose lowest two strata are 1 of 25 and 4 of 40 patients - rates whose confidence intervals overlap entirely - and the authors themselves report that survival in the 11-30 mm band was only slightly and non-significantly worse than at 10 mm or less, so the data support 'larger is worse' but not the specific cut point that subsequently entered international guidelines","The cohort spans 1956 to 2003 with prospective registration only from 1997, and the authors use the post-1997 subset for penetrance while using the whole cohort for metastasis and survival, so the two central estimates come from different populations imaged with different technology","Metastasis was imaging-defined in 60% of cases, and the authors cite evidence that a quarter of radiographically node-negative MEN1 patients have occult metastases at operation - which means the risk being weighed against the morbidity of surgery is systematically understated in the same analysis that recommends against surgery","Mean follow-up after diagnosis is 4.3 years in a disease whose victims die at a mean age of 43, so most of the hazard being adjudicated lies beyond the observation window; the 8-year survival estimates in the metastatic group have confidence intervals from 6% to 62%","The mortality argument is partly circular: life expectancy with a nonfunctioning tumour is compared against MEN1 patients without any pancreatic tumour, who differ systematically in age at diagnosis, screening intensity and era, and who by definition lack the lesion that defines the comparison","In MEN1 the pancreas carries a field defect with a mean of 2.9 tumours per patient, so a size threshold applied to the largest lesion ignores the remaining disease, and the authors' own data show 2 of 32 curatively resected patients needed reoperation for new tumours within 6 years","Thirty-two curatively operated patients and 66 unoperated patients with non-significant differences in metastasis, progression and death is an underpowered null, not evidence of equivalence; no power calculation or equivalence margin is offered"],"n":"108 MEN1 patients with isolated nonfunctioning pancreatic tumours, drawn from 579 registered MEN1 patients","bottom_line":"In the largest population-based MEN1 series, nonfunctioning pancreatic tumours are the commonest pancreaticoduodenal lesion, reach 34% penetrance by age 50 and shorten life expectancy by about nine years, with metastasis rising from 4% below 10 mm to 43% above 30 mm - the basis for not operating below 20 mm, although that specific threshold rests on single-digit event counts, imaging-defined metastasis and 4 years of follow-up.","funding":"Supported in part by a grant from the University Hospital of Geneva, Switzerland, to F. Triponez."},"16926567":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["The study is not randomised; this is the authors' stated principal limitation","The 35 non-surgical patients did not have surgery for a mixture of reasons - refusal after discussion with the referring physician in 55%, concurrent illness, inability to consent, and the MEN1 size rule","The authors defend comparability by showing no significant difference in any clinical, laboratory or imaging parameter, including the factors previously shown to predict aggressive disease (sex, MEN1 status, disease duration, fasting gastrin, imaging results), and no difference in follow-up duration"],"critique":["This is a gastrinoma study and almost all primaries were duodenal or nodal; it bears on functioning duodenopancreatic NET and not at all on incidental non-functioning pancreatic NET, yet it is the usual citation for the proposition that surgery prolongs survival in pancreatic NET","Thirty-five controls, of whom 10 were excluded from surgery by the MEN1 size rule and 5 by comorbidity, cannot be assumed exchangeable with 160 operated patients however many baseline variables match; refusing surgery after consulting one's own doctor is itself a marker of health behaviour, health literacy and access","Disease-related death in the surgical arm is 2 events, so the 23-fold difference and the 98% figure rest on single digits with no confidence interval reported for the ratio","Non-disease-related mortality was numerically higher in the controls (31% vs 20%), which is the expected signature of a sicker comparison group and undercuts the claim that the arms differed only in disease-specific risk; this is reported as non-significant rather than interpreted","Cause of death was adjudicated by the treating and operating investigators without blinding, in a study whose central endpoint is cause-specific","Controls were imaged every 6-12 months whereas operated patients were evaluated yearly, and controls less often had functional localisation studies, so ascertainment of liver metastases differed by arm in both direction and intensity","Accrual spans 1980 to the mid-2000s across three institutions while the operation itself changed mid-study - routine duodenotomy and intraoperative endoscopic transillumination from 1987, somatostatin receptor scintigraphy from 1994 - and all 10 patients in whom no tumour was found were operated before duodenotomy, so the arms are not method-contemporaneous","With 20-31% non-disease mortality over two decades, competing risk is substantial and no competing-risk analysis was performed; Kaplan-Meier censoring inflates the disease-specific separation"],"n":"195 ZES patients: 160 who underwent surgical exploration and 35 who did not","bottom_line":"Over a mean 12 years of follow-up, routine exploration for gastrinoma was associated with far fewer liver metastases and a 15-year disease-related survival of 98% versus 74% without surgery, but the comparison is non-randomised with 35 self-selected controls, 2 disease-related deaths in the surgical arm, and no bearing on non-functioning pancreatic NET."},"18063061":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["The pathology was not reviewed for this study, so Ki-67 or proliferative staining was not examined and could not be related to doubling time","Chromogranin A and other biomarkers were not examined and no marker data correlate with metastatic disease","Cut-offs of 1 cm and 2 cm were not analysed; only the 3 cm threshold carried over from the group's earlier work was tested","Some non-operated lesions diagnosed on radiographic criteria could on pathology turn out to be microcystic adenomas, although the authors state they do not look classic for that on imaging","The ultimate impact of this management approach on metastatic risk will only be known as the patients continue to be followed"],"critique":["The three-criterion algorithm is derived from 9 metastatic events and then declared to capture all 9, so its perfect sensitivity is a tautology of the derivation rather than a finding, and no independent or temporal validation is attempted","Doubling time, the criterion with the largest apparent separation, could be calculated in all 9 metastatic patients but only 54 of 99 non-metastatic ones; patients with visibly growing lesions are imaged more often, so the exposure and the ability to measure it are entangled, and the missing 45 patients are simply absent from the stratification table","Sixty-nine of 108 lesions were never resected and their diagnosis rests on CT or MRI appearance alone - which the senior author concedes in the floor discussion could include microcystic adenomas - so a substantial part of the denominator is unverified, and any benign lesions in it dilute the metastasis rate downward","The study dates are internally inconsistent, December 1998 in the abstract against December 1988 in the methods, an eight-fold difference in accrual window that is never reconciled","The 3 cm threshold was carried over from the group's own prior publications rather than tested against 1 or 2 cm; a discussant asked precisely this and the author replied that the analysis had not been done, so the cut point in the resulting algorithm is untested within this dataset","No Ki-67, grade or differentiation data exist anywhere in the series, which in 2007 was already the strongest known prognostic axis in pancreatic NET","VHL PNETs are always nonfunctional, often multifocal and set against competing renal and CNS disease; with 2 PNET deaths among 633 screened patients, the algorithm is calibrated against a risk that is an order of magnitude smaller than the patient's renal risk, which the authors state but which also means the algorithm's clinical value is largely unmeasurable","The exon 3 association rests on 7 of 9 metastatic patients and is a single test in a cohort where exon 3 is already the commonest mutation site (50%), with no correction for the other exons examined"],"n":"108 VHL patients with PNETs among 633 VHL patients screened; 39 resected and 9 with metastatic disease","bottom_line":"In the largest single-centre VHL series, 17% of patients had a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour and only 8.3% of those metastasised; lesion size of 3 cm or more, an exon 3 germline mutation and a doubling time under 500 days together identified every metastatic case - but the rule was derived and tested on the same 9 events, doubling time was measurable in only half the non-metastatic patients, and two thirds of lesions were never histologically confirmed."},"18376195":{"kind":"registry","limitations":["Functionality of islet cell tumours is not explicitly recorded in cancer registries, so functional status is probably under-reported; the authors note the functional versus nonfunctional survival difference would likely widen if all benign functional tumours were reported","US cancer registries collect data only on malignant pancreatic tumours; some hospitals in some periods were reporting tumours with benign behaviour and these were excluded for lack of uniformity","Tumour grade is substantially underreported for PNET (56.5% complete, versus 22.8% missing for pancreatic adenocarcinoma), and widespread applicability of the score requires better grade reporting","As with all large administrative datasets there may be miscoding, missing or inaccurate data, and pathological review of all specimens was impossible","The NCDB does not record MEN-1 status, the number of tumours within the pancreas, secretory hormone levels or the specific type of systemic therapy","Survival analyses based on retrospective data should be interpreted cautiously because of potential patient selection bias, particularly for surgery and adjuvant treatment, and the analysis of prognostic factors demonstrates association rather than causation","For patients who had enucleation and were reported node negative, nodal status was recoded as missing unless the number of nodes examined was explicitly reported"],"critique":["The result most often lifted from this paper - that tumour size does not predict survival after resection - comes from a cohort in which only 19% of tumours were 2 cm or less and from which the registry had already removed every lesion a pathologist called benign, so the small-tumour end of the distribution is both thin and skewed toward the aggressive; the paper cannot be used to argue that size is irrelevant to the decision whether to resect a 1 cm incidental lesion","The score is derived and evaluated in the same 836 patients, with bootstrapping for optimism but no external or temporal validation, and a concordance index of 0.63 is barely above the 0.5 of chance; the authors defend it by comparison with a pancreatic adenocarcinoma staging system rather than against any threshold of clinical usefulness","Grade was missing in 43.5% of the cohort and nodal status was deliberately recoded as missing for enucleation patients, so the two variables that carry most of the score's discrimination are the two most incompletely recorded - and the 836-patient complete-case subset is by construction the best-documented 22% of the cohort","Pancreaticoduodenectomy emerging as an independent adverse predictor is far more plausibly perioperative mortality and tumour location than any effect of the operation, which the authors concede in the discussion while retaining it in the model and in the abstract's list of predictors","The cohort spans 1985-2004, during which WHO grading was introduced (2000) and 'neuroendocrine carcinoma' absorbed 'islet cell tumour' in registry reporting, so the exposure definitions shift within the study period","Disease-specific survival is unavailable, so relative survival adjusted for age, sex and race stands in for it; in a disease with a median age of 56 and 10-year survival of 38%, that substitution does substantial work and is not validated here","Only 1464 of 3851 patients had tumours over 4 cm recorded and size was missing for about 22%, so the null result for size is also a null result in the presence of considerable missingness, with no sensitivity analysis"],"n":"3851 patients who underwent pancreatectomy for PNET; 836 with complete data for all three score variables","bottom_line":"The largest resected PNET series ever assembled established age, tumour grade and distant metastasis as the dominant determinants of postresection survival and found no independent effect of tumour size, nodal status or margins - but the registry excluded benign-coded tumours, grade was missing in over 40%, and the resulting score discriminates only marginally better than chance.","funding":"K.Y. Bilimoria was supported by the American College of Surgeons Clinical Scholars in Residence program and the Department of Surgery, Feinberg School of Medicine, Northwestern University. No industry funding reported."},"22967994":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design with its inherent limitations","The exceedingly low median survival of untreated patients may be biased by late referral and more advanced disease stage, as the worse performance status, white cell count and CRP suggest, or by conditions such as age that precluded chemotherapy","Ki-67 was assessed by many different pathologists in different countries, so the 55% analysis may be biased by methodology, pathologist experience and Ki-67 heterogeneity, and the cut-off should be interpreted with some caution","Patients were not specifically reclassified according to the new WHO 2010 criteria","Response rates were evaluated by RECIST 1.0 from radiological reports rather than from measured scans","There are limited data explaining why the abnormal laboratory values evolve and what they reflect"],"critique":["The 11-month versus 1-month contrast between chemotherapy and best supportive care is the paper's most quoted figure and is almost pure selection: the untreated group was twelve years older and half of it was PS 3-4, and a median survival of one month identifies patients referred at the point of death - the authors note this and still frame it as a reason to treat without delay","The Ki-67 threshold of 55% was derived by ROC in 42 randomly selected patients and then applied to the rest of the same cohort, so it is an internally generated cut-off with no external validation, and it disappears entirely from the multivariable model - meaning the paper's signature prognostic marker is not independently prognostic in its own analysis, a point the abstract does not convey","The regression that produces the final prognostic model runs on 170 of 252 chemotherapy patients after excluding the ROC derivation set and incomplete cases, which is not stated in the abstract","GI-NEC here pools oesophagus to rectum with 32% unknown primary; pancreatic NEC, the only portion relevant to a pancreatic pathway, is 71 patients analysed as a site subgroup with no multiplicity correction across seven sites","Small-cell versus non-small-cell morphology was taken from pathology report wording with no central review and no re-review of slides, which is the most likely explanation for the null result on morphology, yet the paper concludes the morphological classification is of uncertain clinical relevance","Response was assessed from radiological reports, not from measured target lesions, so the 31% response rate and the Ki-67 response gradient rest on unstandardised radiology narrative","Treatment choice between cisplatin and carboplatin was 'mainly due to different center policy', which makes the equivalence claim a comparison between centres rather than between drugs, confounded by everything else those centres did differently","The favourable 26-month survival in 36 patients with PS 0 and normal platelets and LDH is a post hoc subgroup defined by the model fitted to the same data"],"n":"305 patients with advanced GI-NEC (71 pancreatic primaries, 23%): 252 given palliative chemotherapy and 53 best supportive care only","bottom_line":"The largest advanced GI-NEC cohort ever reported establishes performance status, primary site and raised platelets or LDH as the dominant prognostic factors and shows that tumours with Ki-67 below 55% respond less to platinum yet survive longer - but the untreated comparison group is a late-referral artefact, the 55% cut-off is internally derived and drops out of the multivariable model, and pancreatic NEC is a 71-patient subgroup.","funding":"Nordic Cancer Union and Eckbo Foundations; H. Sorbye funded by the Norwegian Cancer Society, H. Gronbaek by the NOVO Nordisk Foundation, N. Holt by the Danish Research Council, E.T. Janson by the Swedish Cancer Society and I.H. Olsen by a Rigshospitalet research grant. The authors declared no conflicts of interest."},"24253141":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective data collection and a single-institution experience","Patients selected for observation of their tumours were not included, because the cohort was drawn from a surgical database","Reported complication rates were lower than the unit's own previously published rates and lower than the literature, and because they were collected retrospectively over two decades they are likely an incomplete picture of the morbidity of oncological resection","Ki-67 can be obtained on biopsy but biopsy is not always reliable because these tumours are heterogeneous, and the procedure carries its own risks; the two node-positive patients with tumours 1 cm or smaller both had Ki-67 under 20%","Given the indolent nature of many PNET, it will take several decades to determine whether limited local treatments compromise long-term outcomes"],"critique":["The central claim - that no preoperative variable defines a group with nodal risk below about 12-20% - is generated from a resected cohort in a unit that states its own bias toward oncological resection, so the small, favourable, observed lesions that would populate the low-risk tail are structurally absent from the dataset; the authors acknowledge the omission but draw a management conclusion from it anyway","The headline 12% nodal rate in tumours 1 cm or smaller is 2 of 17 patients, a confidence interval running from roughly 2% to 36%, which cannot support or refute any size threshold","Nodes examined differed two-fold between head (median 15) and body-tail (median 8), and nodal positivity in this disease tracks with nodes examined, so the location effect is in part a detection effect even after statistical adjustment","Nodal status predicted disease-free but not overall survival (log-rank 0.1); the authors argue the OS result will become significant with longer follow-up rather than reporting the result they obtained, and then use the DFS finding to justify routine lymphadenectomy","Key predictors were fitted on incomplete data - lymphovascular invasion was known in 97 of 136, Ki-67 in 121, perineural invasion in 69, grade in 112 - so the odds ratios come from varying and unstated subsets","MEN-1 and functional tumours were retained on the basis of a non-significance test in a cohort containing only 13 and 8 such patients, which is far too small to exclude an effect","The complication rate (39%, 7% leak) is conceded to be implausibly low and incomplete, which matters because the whole argument weighs nodal yield against the morbidity of a larger operation","The recommendation that oncological resection be the standard operation for most patients cannot be derived from a dataset in which no patient was observed and no patient underwent enucleation without nodes except in 3 cases"],"n":"136 patients with locoregional PNET; 133 (98%) had nodal resection, of whom 50 (37.6%) were N1","bottom_line":"Among 136 resected locoregional PNET, nodal metastasis was present in 38% overall and still 12-13% in tumours of 1-1.5 cm, and nothing available before surgery reliably identified a low-risk group - but the cohort contains only operated patients from a unit committed to oncological resection, the small-tumour estimates rest on single-digit event counts, and nodal status did not reach significance for overall survival.","funding":"Statistical support from the Biostatistics Core, Siteman Comprehensive Cancer Center, NCI Cancer Center Support grant P30 CA091842; salary support for Y. Hashim from the Washington University Surgical Oncology Training grant 5T32CA00962124. Authors declare no conflicts of interest."},"24750272":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Cytology tends to underestimate the grade obtained on the resection specimen, so a low cytological Ki-67 should not be taken as proof of a low-grade tumour","EUS-FNA cellularity is variable and the needle may not sample the most mitotically active region, which the authors attribute to genuine intratumoural heterogeneity of proliferation","Only one resected tumour was cytological G3, which weakens the survival separation at the top of the scale","Neither a 2% nor a 5% cytological cut-off gave acceptable correlation with histological grade","Identifying that counted cells are genuinely neuroendocrine is difficult on dispersed cytological material"],"critique":["The title advertises 'high reproducibility and inter-observer agreement', which is true only of two readers scoring the same slide; the clinically relevant question - does cytology predict resection grade - returned a kappa of 0.21 that the authors themselves call very low, and that result is not in the title","The concordance analysis can only include the 33 resected tumours, so the denominator is a resected population and nothing here tells you how cytology performs in the small lesions actually being watched","PFS was calculated 'independently from surgery', mixing resected and unresected patients in the same curves, so the cytological grade effect is confounded by whether the tumour was removed","The cG3 group that drives the significant PFS separation consists of 4 patients, all of whom the authors state were locally advanced, node-positive or metastatic at diagnosis, so cytological G3 may be a marker of stage rather than an independent grading achievement","The second cytology reader was a gastroenterologist, not a pathologist, while the histology arm used two pathologists, so the two inter-observer coefficients are not comparable","Fourteen years of accrual spans the 2000, 2004 and 2010 WHO classifications; the cases were retrospectively reclassified to WHO 2010 without re-review of the original diagnostic material","No adjustment for multiple comparisons across several cut-offs, subgroups and endpoints in 46 tumours"],"n":"46 pNETs in 45 patients; 33 tumours in 32 patients resected and available for histological comparison","bottom_line":"EUS-FNA Ki-67 is highly reproducible between readers and a cytological G3 result reliably marks aggressive disease, but it under-grades G2 tumours in about 70% of cases, so a low cytological Ki-67 cannot be used to certify a small pancreatic NET as low grade."},"24841347":{"kind":"registry","limitations":["The NCDB collects data only on tumours with ICD-O-3 codes corresponding to malignant disease, so these data may overestimate the malignant potential of small PNET","There is no explicit way to determine tumour functionality, so some functional tumours may inadvertently have been included","Multifocality is not reported in the database, so patients who had total pancreatectomy - suspected to have multifocal disease - had to be analysed as a separate surgical group","The reduced survival of the no-surgery group should be interpreted with caution because those patients may not have been offered surgery for unreported reasons that increased their mortality; the authors attempted to control for this by exclusions but call for prospective studies","Coding errors, missing data and the absence of key variables - mitotic rate, Ki-67, disease-specific survival and recurrence - all limit the analysis","Lymphadenectomy results may reflect inadequate nodal sampling, with a median of only 8 nodes examined and 27% of resected patients having none"],"critique":["This is a National Cancer Data Base analysis, not SEER, and the registry by design captures only tumours assigned a malignant behaviour code - which removes the indolent small lesions a surveillance policy is about, so 29% nodal and 10% distant metastasis are a ceiling for a selected malignant subset rather than estimates for incidental sub-2 cm tumours","The arresting claim that 33% of tumours 5 mm or smaller have nodal metastases rests on a band of 94 patients in a variable that is missing in 45% of the cohort, with no confidence interval given; a handful of events in a selectively recorded field cannot adjudicate a size threshold","The survival analysis collapses 1854 patients to 366 by requiring diagnosis before 2006 and known surgery type, and then compares a no-surgery group that is older, far more often poorly differentiated and less often treated at academic centres against resected patients; the 27.6% versus 83.0% contrast is selection, which the authors concede in the discussion but still place in the abstract and conclusions","A 15% relative reduction in the risk of death for every later calendar year, during a window in which the authors themselves found no change in resection rates, hospital type or distant metastasis rates, is far more plausibly stage migration from incidental detection than improving care","The same calendar-year effect was not significant for 2004-2006 on Kaplan-Meier analysis, so the Cox finding is fragile and is explained away by appeal to greater model granularity rather than treated as the discrepant result it is","Nodes examined differ systematically by operation (63% vs 89%), so the finding that lymphadenectomy does not affect survival compares groups with structurally different staging completeness and is uninformative either way","The conclusion - that nonfunctional PNET of all sizes should be considered potentially malignant and resection considered - is drawn from a registry that cannot see the observed patients, cannot see Ki-67, and reports no disease-specific survival"],"n":"1854 patients with nonfunctional PNET 2 cm or less; 1367 with known extent of resection; 366 in the survival analysis","bottom_line":"In a registry restricted to tumours coded as malignant, nonfunctional PNET of 2 cm or less carried a 29% nodal and 10% distant metastasis rate with no fall at the smallest sizes, and extent of resection and lymphadenectomy made no difference to survival - but the apparent survival benefit of any surgery over none is selection, and the metastasis rates cannot be transferred to incidentally found lesions."},"26041666":{"kind":"meta-analysis","limitations":["The review is compromised by the moderate methodological quality of most primary studies","Most studies did not define delayed gastric emptying and only one applied the ISGPS definition, so differing endpoint definitions may have compromised the results","Selection bias cannot be ruled out given the absence of randomisation and the scarcity of baseline data in some studies; for most studies it is unclear whether the standard-resection patients would also have been suitable for enucleation","Long-term disease-specific outcomes such as disease-free survival could not be compared because most primary studies focused on short-term surgical outcomes","A planned subgroup analysis of enucleation in the body/tail versus distal pancreatectomy and enucleation in the head/uncinate versus pancreaticoduodenectomy could not be performed because the primary data did not separate fistula rates by location","All data come from non-randomised studies, so results must be interpreted with caution; a randomised trial of disease-specific outcome would be relevant but difficult because suitable lesions are rare, multicentre recruitment would be needed, learning-curve bias would intrude, and patient and surgeon preferences would impair recruitment"],"critique":["The analysis most likely to change practice - that enucleation carries no excess fistula risk in high-volume centres - rests on 4 of 22 studies with I2 = 49%, and the volume threshold was defined by the authors themselves and inserted as a modified item into the Downs and Black checklist, so the least robust and least pre-specified result is the one carried into the conclusion","The primary comparison is between operations chosen for anatomically different lesions, and the review explicitly concedes it cannot tell whether the resected patients were ever enucleation candidates - which makes every difference in blood loss, operating time and pancreatic insufficiency partly an artefact of lesion size and location rather than of the operation","Means and standard deviations were back-calculated from medians and ranges by the Hozo uncontrolled secondary endpoint in a single-arm industry trial of 61 unusually fit patients, with universal anaemia and no data on durability or on sporadic disease.","funding":"Merck Sharp and Dohme, a subsidiary of Merck; the Intramural Research Program of the NIH National Cancer Institute Center for Cancer Research; and NCI grant UO1 CA236489. Three authors are Merck employees; medical writing by ApotheCom was paid for by the sponsor."},"35380181":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["The retrospective nature makes unintentional contributions of bias likely","Individual patients may be represented in both datasets because institutions in the USNETSG also submit reports to the NCDB","The NCDB does not report WHO grade, so exclusion of grade 3 relies on differentiation; the authors argue most grade 3 tumours are poorly differentiated so the analysis should still be weighted to lower grade","The indolent nature of PNET makes survival analysis difficult even with a median three-year follow-up","The low rate of recurrence in Black patients (3 events) limits meaningful comparison of disease-free survival between racial groups","Disease-free survival is not synonymous with overall survival, so no conclusions about patient mortality can be derived"],"critique":["The policy-relevant cell is 7 of 30 Black patients with sub-2 cm tumours and the sub-1 cm claim is 2 of 8 - counts from which a recommendation to resect more aggressively by race cannot responsibly be drawn, and the validation cohort fails to reproduce the sub-1 cm finding at all (10% vs 9%, p = 0.66), which the paper notes but does not let alter the conclusion","Every patient in both cohorts was resected and had nodes removed, so this measures the prevalence of nodal metastasis among people already selected for an oncological operation, not among the surveillance candidates the guideline addresses - the very selection the paper criticises in the guideline is reproduced in its own design","Race is treated as a biological variable with no measure of insurance, income, referral delay, time from symptom to diagnosis or access to imaging, any of which would produce the same size-independent association between Black race and nodal disease at resection","The authors acknowledge the two datasets overlap institutionally, which means the NCDB 'validation' partly re-analyses the same patients and is not independent","Grade is excluded from one dataset and unavailable in the other, so the observed nodal difference may track grade, which is a stronger determinant of nodal spread than size","The recommendation runs opposite to this group's own prior USNETSG finding that node-negative Black patients had better five-year recurrence-free survival than White patients - a contradiction that is quoted in the discussion and then left unreconciled","Six size strata are compared across two datasets with additional regressions and subanalyses, with no correction for multiple comparisons; several of the significant p values would not survive one","The title's framing question ('are we undertreating Black patients?') presupposes that more resection is the remedy, when the same data are equally consistent with Black patients reaching resection later in the disease course"],"n":"453 patients (388 or 389 White, 65 Black) in the initial dataset and 5532 (4772 White, 760 Black) in the NCDB validation dataset","bottom_line":"Among resected nonfunctional PNET, Black patients had roughly double the rate of nodal metastasis in tumours under 2 cm and tumour size did not predict nodal spread in them at all - a signal worth taking seriously, but it rests on 7 of 30 patients, does not replicate below 1 cm, comes entirely from an operated population, and offers no measure of access or delay to explain it.","funding":"National Cancer Institute of the NIH awards T32CA229102 and K08CA234209. Disclosures: C. Yates receives consulting fees from Amgen, QED Therapeutics and Riptide Biosciences and owns stock in Riptide; F. Rocha is a paid consultant to Medtronic."},"35923628":{"kind":"registry","limitations":["Inherent biases of a retrospective design could not be completely eliminated even with propensity score matching","SEER lacks important prognostic parameters including the Ki-67 index and surgery-related complications","The small number of patients remaining after propensity score matching may limit the generalisability of the results","Further prospective multicentric studies and more robust data are required to validate the conservative policy"],"critique":["The signature finding - surgery improves overall survival while cancer-specific survival is identical - is the classic pattern of confounding by comorbidity and selection, not a treatment effect, and the authors nevertheless report the OS difference as a survival advantage of surgery in the abstract","SEER cannot distinguish a patient enrolled in planned surveillance from one never offered an operation because of frailty, dementia or advanced age, so the 'observation' arm is a residual category of the unoperated; the pre-matching table shows it was older and had seven times the rate of liver involvement","Functional status, symptoms and incidental detection are not recorded in SEER, so 'nonfunctional' and 'asymptomatic' are assumed rather than established, and some functional tumours are certainly included","The 2.50 cm ROC cutoff is derived and reported in the same dataset with no validation, and 'aggressiveness' is a composite of poor differentiation, nodal involvement, liver involvement and advanced stage - variables mathematically entangled with size and with each other, so that size is guaranteed to predict the composite; specificity of 63% would be unusable clinically","The exploratory 407-patient subgroup was selected using the Cox model fitted to the same data, so its null result is circular rather than independent corroboration","Propensity matching left 259 per arm and could only balance the variables SEER records; what it cannot balance - performance status, comorbidity, Ki-67, reason for not operating - is exactly what drives the OS gap","There is no imaging follow-up, no growth rate, no crossover and no information on surveillance intensity, so the paper has no purchase at all on surveillance as a management strategy despite its title","The paper misspells the central reference it reinterprets ('Ssdot et al.') and attributes Cherenfant's findings to Gratian, which is a sign of how closely the source literature was read"],"n":"5172 patients with PanNEN, 1760 (34.0%) with tumours 2 cm or less; 1621 NF-PanNET of whom 1350 had surgery and 271 observation; 259 matched pairs after propensity matching","bottom_line":"A SEER analysis arguing that tumour size alone should not decide observation versus surgery for sub-2 cm non-functional pancreatic NET, but its central comparison is between operated patients and a residual unoperated group that was older and sicker, and the equal cancer-specific survival after matching points to selection rather than to any benefit of resection."},"35986682":{"kind":"prospective cohort","limitations":["These are preliminary results; the study will conclude one year after enrolment of the last patient","Only a very low rate of tumour growth was seen after a median of 2 years, so longer follow-up is probably needed before definitive conclusions can be reached","The detection of synchronous liver metastases in four patients demonstrates a real, if rare, potential for distant spread among lesions of 2 cm or less"],"critique":["The 20% rate of aggressive histology is the paper's most quoted and most consequential number, and it comes entirely from the 94 resected patients - a group selected for larger size, duct dilatation, younger age, anxiety and surgeon preference - so it cannot be read as the prevalence of aggressive biology among sub-2 cm lesions, and certainly not among the 406 who were watched","Conversely, the surveillance arm's reassuring course rests on 25 months of follow-up with only 2% crossover, so neither arm was observed long enough or exchanged enough patients for the two to be tested against the same risk; no outcome comparison between the arms was performed at all","Treatment was assigned by the referring centre rather than randomised, and enrolment at a surgical centre independently doubled the odds of resection, so a substantial part of what the study measures is local institutional culture","The conclusion that 'active surveillance is the preferred approach' is asserted in the same paragraph as the finding of measurable metastatic potential and aggressive histology in a fifth of resected tumours, without any analysis that could compare the two strategies","The metastasis rate is printed as 0.08 per cent when 4 of 500 is 0.8 per cent - a tenfold typographical understatement of the key safety signal, uncorrected","A third of patients never had an FNA and grade was not evaluable in a quarter of those who did, so there is no histological characterisation of the surveillance arm and the extent of under-staging there is unmeasurable","Anxiety (HADS 4-6) independently predicted surgery, which means some pancreatectomies in this cohort were treating distress rather than tumour - a finding the paper notes without pursuing","The study is funded by ENETS, whose own guideline recommending surveillance for lesions of 2 cm or less is the hypothesis under test, and the senior authors wrote that guideline"],"n":"500 patients (406 active surveillance, 94 surgical resection), from 540 assessed for eligibility","bottom_line":"The largest prospective series of sub-2 cm non-functioning pancreatic NEN shows that 81% are watched and almost none progress over two years, but the 20% rate of aggressive histology comes only from the selected patients who were resected, the two management strategies were never compared, and 25 months is far too short to settle the question the trial was designed to answer.","funding":"European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society; the authors declare no conflict of interest."},"36434154":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Retrospective design makes the study susceptible to bias, although consecutive series were identified at each centre","The scan interval of up to 90 days allows lesions to shift or grow, impeding accurate comparison, though the median interval was only 9 days against a median TTP of 17.1 months","The treatments individual patients received were not reported, which may bias both TTP and OS; in particular starting PRRT may confer a survival advantage on the P1-P4 cohort","The approach to determining progression was not standardised across centres","Findings should ideally be confirmed in a prospective trial using NETPET as an exploratory endpoint, although accrual in an uncommon disease would be difficult","Larger numbers and longer follow-up are needed before concluding that NETPET further stratifies within histological grade, and to test it within well- and poorly differentiated grade 3"],"critique":["The centres had published earlier series and re-queried their databases. Patient overlap with the original derivation and other earlier cohorts is unquantified; do not assert that two centres supplied the original derivation patients or that a known proportion is a re-analysis.","Only 36% of patients had pancreatic primaries and no pancreas-specific subgroup analysis is presented, so the score cannot be cited as evidence for managing pancreatic NET","Histological grade - the comparator the score is said to complement - was taken from whatever biopsy was available with no central pathology review across three countries, which biases the comparison in the index test's favour","The authors concede that treatment, including PRRT, was not modelled; since SSTR-positive/FDG-negative disease is the eligibility criterion for PRRT, the P1 advantage is confounded with access to an effective therapy","Time zero is the date of the second scan, which sits at an arbitrary and differing point in each patient's disease course and selects for patients who survived to be scanned, inviting left-truncation and immortal-time bias","The analysis again uses the pre-specified three-category collapse, so the 5-point scale the papers propose remains unvalidated at the level at which it is reported clinically","The finding that 59% of grade 1 patients were FDG-avid, well above published rates, is presented as a strength of dual imaging but is equally consistent with reader threshold drift or with grade misassignment, and is not resolved"],"n":"319 patients with metastatic or unresectable GEPNEN (114 pancreatic primaries, 36%)","bottom_line":"In 319 patients with metastatic GEP-NEN, NETPET and histological grade independently predicted overall survival and time to progression. Treatment was not adjusted for, earlier-series overlap is unquantified and only about a third had pancreatic primaries. The study does not validate a treatment threshold for localized pNET.","funding":"No specific funding for the research project; D.L. Chan funded by NHMRC Australia grant GNT1175788. Several authors report honoraria or research support from Ipsen, Novartis, AAA, Pfizer, Lexicon, EMD Serono and others outside the submitted work."},"36434481":{"kind":"retrospective cohort","limitations":["Only resected PNET were included, so the study is subject to the selection bias that led patients to undergo resection, and the authors could not retrospectively ascertain which PNET were managed non-operatively","Some cystic PNET under 3 cm with non-mucinous cyst fluid may have been misdiagnosed as serous cystic lesions, so the true proportion of cystic PNET is probably misrepresented - though the authors argue that including them would strengthen the findings since the most favourable lesions are the ones least likely to be operated","Given the multicentre design, variation in radiographic imaging and interpretation, data collection, pathology assessment and treatment across institutions may exist, offset in the authors' view by greater generalisability and adequate sample size"],"critique":["The multivariable hazard ratio for calcification is 11.5 with a confidence interval from 1.1 to 125.0 at p = 0.043 - a point estimate with essentially no precision - sitting in a model that also returns 25.2 and 33.0 for nodal and distant metastasis, the signature of an overfitted Cox model with far too few recurrence events for the covariates entered; no event count for the model is reported anywhere","Between 28% and 29% of the cohort has no data on the two exposures of interest and the analysis is complete-case with no imputation and no sensitivity analysis, so the effective sample is not 981 and may be differentially missing by centre and era","Table 1 is internally inconsistent, giving n = 167 cystic and 814 solid and 177 calcified and 804 non-calcified in one row against 120, 582, 122 and 575 in the column headers, with a garbled '305 (3)' cell - so the denominators underlying the percentages cannot be reconstructed from the paper","Imaging was classified from radiology report wording rather than by central re-read, across eight institutions and seventeen years of changing CT and MRI technique, which makes the exposure a measure of reporting practice as much as of tumour biology","The cystic-calcified cell that anchors the four-way survival comparison contains 16 patients, and that comparison carries p = 0.043 with no correction for the multiple pairwise contrasts implied","Median follow-up is 35 months in a disease whose recurrences arrive at a median of 4-7 years, so every 5-year recurrence-free survival figure is extrapolated from a thin risk set, and the stated last follow-up date of March 2017 is the same year the accrual window closes","The conclusion that these features could inform the decision to observe or resect a small asymptomatic PNET is drawn from a cohort in which no patient was observed - the authors acknowledge they cannot identify the non-operated patients and then make the recommendation anyway","Cystic morphology, one of the paper's two headline features, was not independently prognostic (p = 0.69), yet the abstract and conclusion present both features as usable for stratification"],"n":"981 patients resected for well-differentiated PNET; cystic morphology data missing in 279 (28%) and calcification data missing in 284 (29%)","bottom_line":"Across 981 resected well-differentiated pancreatic NET, radiographic calcification marked adverse pathology and shorter recurrence-free survival while a predominantly cystic appearance marked the opposite, but calcification's independent hazard ratio of 11.5 spans 1.1 to 125.0, cystic morphology was not independent at all, nearly 30% of the exposure data are missing, and nobody in the cohort was observed."},"36725249":{"kind":"guideline","limitations":["The preamble states that the standard is not an inflexible rule or requirement of practice, is not intended to establish a legal standard of care, and the societies caution against its use in litigation","Adherence to the standard will not ensure an accurate diagnosis or a successful outcome; all that should be expected is a reasonable course of action based on current knowledge","SUV measurements may not be reproducible across scanners and institutions without standardisation of imaging protocols, scanner qualification and cross-calibration, and SUV is affected by lesion size and uptake time","It is unclear how SSTR PET should be used for selecting patients for PRRT because NETTER-1 enrolled patients on the basis of 111In-pentetreotide rather than PET","It is currently unclear whether delayed imaging with 64Cu-DOTATATE offers benefit over standard times","It is difficult to generalise how much of 68Ga's greater positron range will affect quantification in small lesions because of the complex interplay of detector resolution, system diameter, reconstruction algorithm and spatial filtering"],"critique":["The document asserts that the three tracers can be considered equivalent for detecting SSTR-positive disease while in the same text quantifying a 10-20% SUV underestimation for 68Ga in 10-15 mm lesions and a five-fold count deficit for 64Cu; claims of equivalence and of measurable difference sit side by side with no head-to-head outcome data resolving them, which matters most for exactly the sub-centimetre pancreatic lesion a pathway is deciding about","There is no systematic review, no evidence grading and no strength-of-recommendation scheme, so a prospective trial, an expert opinion and an FDA package insert carry identical typographic authority, and the package inserts are cited repeatedly as primary sources for dosing and uptake timing","The instruction to discontinue long-acting somatostatin analogues 3-4 weeks before imaging is carried over from the EANM guideline while the adjacent text cites prospective evidence that this is unnecessary for lanreotide - leaving the reader with two contradictory instructions and no recommendation","Several authors hold intellectual property or consultancy relationships with the manufacturers of the tracers being standardised - one is named in a later ENETS document as inventor/IPR holder on 64Cu-DOTATATE - and the text of this version carries no individual disclosure statement, only a blanket line that no potential conflict was reported","Physiological uptake in the pancreatic head and uncinate process is the single largest source of false positives for any pancreatic pathway, and the standard acknowledges that its SUVs overlap with tumour but offers no decision rule beyond correlating with MRI or multiphase CT and following up","The standard is silent on whether SSTR PET should be performed at all for a sub-2 cm incidental pancreatic lesion under surveillance, and silent on whether serial SSTR PET has any role in surveillance - while simultaneously warning that change in uptake must not be read as response or progression, which removes the obvious use","The appropriate use criteria that define the indications are cited rather than reproduced, so the document that governs when to order the test does not itself contain the indications","Dosimetry is tabulated from four separate historical publications of varying vintage and method and presented as a single comparative table"],"bottom_line":"The authoritative technical standard for acquiring, interpreting and reporting somatostatin receptor PET, including tracer dosimetry, the modified Krenning score and the pancreatic head uptake trap - but it is consensus without evidence grading, it calls three physically unequal tracers equivalent, and it gives no guidance on whether or how to use SSTR PET in a small pancreatic lesion under surveillance."},"37877341":{"kind":"guideline","limitations":["The authors state only that their many years of experience in the field are still being verified in the light of results from new clinical studies, which set new ways of proceeding","Treatment of NF-Pan-NEN still requires the decision of a multidisciplinary team of neuroendocrine neoplasm specialists, and ENETS Centres of Excellence should be strongly considered","Further studies are needed to fulfil unmet needs, focusing on prognostic molecular markers, the selection of a therapeutic approach and the sequence of treatments","Data sharing is not applicable as no new data were created or analysed","Specific uncertainties acknowledged in the text: no validated consensus on the definition of resectability; no preoperative examination accurately predicts nodal involvement; robust data on radiofrequency ablation and on minimally invasive pancreaticoduodenectomy are lacking; no evidence supports somatostatin analogues for controlling progression of small NF-Pan-NET under surveillance; the role of chemotherapy as adjuvant therapy is unknown; limited data exist on PRRT for G3"],"critique":["The two recommendations that most change practice - surveillance for lesions of 1 cm or less and surgery for everything above 2 cm - both carry level 3 evidence and grade B, yet the second is written in the imperative ('strongly recommended'), and the 1-2 cm band into which most incidental lesions fall is handed back to the clinician with no decision rule at all","The follow-up schedule and the recommendation to surveil for at least 20 years and possibly lifelong rest on level 5 evidence - expert opinion without explicit critical appraisal, by the paper's own table - while being assigned grade B, an inversion the GRADE framework the paper claims to follow would not permit","PANDORA and the ASPEN interim analysis are cited as the prospective basis for surveillance at median follow-ups of 17 and 25 months, without the document noting that both are far shorter than the 7-year median time to pancreatic recurrence and the 12-18% recurrence rate it reports elsewhere in the same text","The ASPEN principal investigator and the author of the ENETS surgical guideline being operationalised are among the authors, so the guidance grades evidence its own authors generated, and ASPEN was itself funded by ENETS","CLARINET's hazard ratio in the pancreatic subgroup crosses unity (0.58, 95% CI 0.32-1.04) and is cited in support of a grade A recommendation for upfront somatostatin analogues - a confidence interval that does not exclude no effect supporting the strongest grade available","Belzutifan's 90.9% response figure is imported from a single-arm 22-patient secondary endpoint in VHL disease and placed in a nonfunctioning sporadic pancreatic NET guideline, with the caveat about metastatic disease but not about the design","The E2211 chemotherapy recommendation is built on a PFS advantage with non-significant response and overall survival, in a trial limited to Ki-67 up to 20%, and is then extended to G3 disease on the strength of one retrospective series (evidence 3b, grade B)","There is no systematic search, no evidence table and no description of how the literature informing each question was selected, so the level-of-evidence labels cannot be audited","Eleven of the thirteen authors declare consultancy, speaker or advisory relationships with the manufacturers of the recommended agents - Ipsen, Novartis, AAA, Pfizer, MSD among them - and one holds intellectual property on 64Cu-DOTATATE, the tracer whose superior lesion detection the imaging section endorses"],"bottom_line":"The current ENETS position on nonfunctioning pancreatic NET: observe lesions of 1 cm or less, individualise 1-2 cm, operate above 2 cm or with duct dilation, stage with SSTR-PET/CT and surveil for twenty years or more - sensible, practical and widely followed, but the pivotal surgical thresholds carry level 3 evidence, the follow-up schedule carries level 5, and the prospective studies invoked have two years of follow-up."},"40523372":{"kind":"consensus","limitations":["The recommendations are limited by the varying methodological quality of available data, derived primarily from retrospective series and insufficient to provide high or moderate certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach","Only 37 of 3048 publications (1.2%) met the inclusion criteria for the systematic reviews","Confounding could have arisen in the surgery versus surveillance comparison because surgery for tumours of 2 cm or less was indicated by growth on serial imaging, so the effects of surgery may have been underestimated; given that the implications of surveillance for morbidity, metastasis and mortality are important and irreversible, a more cautious approach might be prudent","Further studies are required to validate and optimise the proposed screening protocols and to develop shared decision-making tools","A similar evidence-based and consensus-based approach is still required for adrenal tumours, which are frequently found as incidentalomas on surveillance MRI","Biomarkers are lacking for accurate risk stratification of neuroendocrine tumours, for predicting aggressive pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, for personalised risk-based management and for early detection of thymic neuroendocrine tumours","Better variant-of-uncertain-significance prediction tools and high-throughput functional assays are needed for genetic testing; prospective, well-annotated cohorts with clinical biobanks and global collaboration are needed to enable the research"],"critique":["The systematic review found no difference between surgery and surveillance for lesions of 2 cm or less, and the panel then declines to follow its own finding, writing that 'a more cautious approach might be prudent' - a defensible clinical judgement, but it means the resulting operative posture is expert preference overriding the evidence the exercise was convened to produce, and should not be cited as evidence-based","1814 patients across 37 mostly retrospective studies for an entire multi-organ syndrome means every pancreatic statement rests on very few events; the panel's own GRADE rating is low or very low throughout while the statements are worded as recommendations carrying 92-100% agreement","A Delphi percentage measures how many experts agree, not how likely they are to be right; the paper's own scale calls 51% agreement a 'consider', so the apparatus systematically converts low-certainty evidence into high-confidence prose, and the agreement figure is the only number most readers will carry away","The 1 mm per year growth criterion in statements 28 and 39 has no cited derivation and lies below the measurement reproducibility of serial MRI of a multifocal pancreas across different scanners and readers, so it will generate both false stability and false progression","Panel selection was by recognised standing within the same societies that issued the 2001 and 2012 guidelines, and several authors wrote those, so the 'new or now explicit' labels partly re-endorse the panel's own prior positions","Recommending pancreatic MRI from age 10-15 commits asymptomatic children to lifelong imaging on the strength of penetrance data alone, with no outcome evidence that earlier detection reduces mortality and no analysis of the harms - incidental adrenal findings, which the paper separately flags as a growing problem, or the psychological burden of surveillance from childhood","The screening recommendations deliberately aim to detect 'clinically relevant disease, and not necessarily the earliest onset of disease', yet the interval recommendations are set by expert vote with no modelling of what interval achieves that distinction","Nothing in this document transfers to sporadic nonfunctioning pancreatic NET: in MEN1 the gland carries a field defect, lesions are multiple, patients are decades younger, and competing parathyroid, pituitary and thymic disease dominates the risk calculus - so the MEN1 2 cm threshold and the sporadic 2 cm threshold happen to share a number but not an evidence base"],"n":"55 recommendations, comprising 52 Delphi consensus statements plus 3 from systematic reviews of 37 of 3048 publications covering 1814 patients","bottom_line":"The most rigorous MEN1 guidance yet assembled, and its most important finding for a pancreatic pathway is negative: across 37 usable studies, surgery and active surveillance for nonfunctioning pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours of 2 cm or less produced no difference in metastasis or mortality at low or very low GRADE certainty - after which the panel recommends caution anyway, on expert judgement rather than data."}}

     "rationale": "FDG positivity is not rare in G1 and G2 disease and predicts progression and prognosis more strongly than grade on the SNMMI/EANM standard's own reading, and the combined score independently predicted survival in a 319-patient cohort.
